layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl:
id='SO-D-01.3.HL' subdomain_id='D-01.3' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source='../../CrossRegulation/DeepAnalysis/D-01_Data-Protection/D-01.3.md §D-01.3' verified_relationship_basis='CRDA-deep verified (3 pairs, all SAME — CRDA initial 3 COMPLEMENTARY corrected to SAME after OJ-text analysis)' emergent_tensions=0 objective='Cryptographic keys and related authentication material are
managed with separation of roles such that possession of the key material
is not bundled with possession of the operational environment that uses it;
the key custodian and the data consumer are distinct roles under distinct
technical and organisational control, with the cryptographic key (not the
storage medium) as the necessary condition for intelligibility of the
protected data.' considerations=['The three participating regulations converge on the same substantive'] anchors=[] csf=[] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto'
hso_per_reg:
id='SO-D-01.3.GDPR' yaml_id='SO-D-01.3.GDPR' regulation='GDPR' subdomain_id='D-01.3' applies_to='[GDPR]' inherits_from='SO-GDPR-002' source_SR='SR-GDPR-003, SR-GDPR-004' activation='if GDPR in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Where pseudonymisation or encryption is applied to personal
data, the additional information required to re-identify the data subject
(the cryptographic key, the mapping table, or the tokenisation seed) is
kept separately and is subject to appropriate technical and organisational
measures that prevent attribution (Art. 4(5) de-attribution test + Art.
34(3)(a) unintelligibility carve-out + Art. 32(1)(a) pseudonymisation/
encryption anchor).

**CSF anchors (from `SR-GDPR-003` + `SR-GDPR-004` v0.3 security_rationale):**
PR.DS-01, PR.IR-03.
*(`SR-GDPR-003` covers the Art. 32(1)(a) + Art. 4(5) pseudonymisation-separation
test anchored to PR.DS-01; `SR-GDPR-004` covers the Art. 34(3)(a)
unintelligibility carve-out anchored to PR.DS-01 + PR.IR-03 — the
resilience dimension of the carve-out presupposes that the key separation
remains effective on the day of the breach.)*' considerations=[] anchors=['Art.
34(3)', 'Art. 32(1)', 'Art. 34(3)', 'Art. 4(5)'] csf=['PR.DS-01', 'PR.IR-03']

id='SO-D-01.3.CRA' yaml_id='SO-D-01.3.CRA' regulation='CRA' subdomain_id='D-01.3' applies_to='[CRA]' inherits_from='SO-CRA-004' source_SR='SR-CRA-004' activation='if CRA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Cryptographic keys and related authentication material used

otherwise processed data by a product with digital elements — personal or
other — are managed with separation of roles such that possession of the
key material is not bundled with possession of the operational environment
that uses it (Annex I Part I (2)(d) access-control + (2)(e) "other technical

mention key management explicitly — the synthesis catalogue
`99_CRA_Synthesis.md` §4 flags this as a T2-vs-text gap — so the
key-separation reading rests on the combination of Annex I (2)(d)
access-control duty with the Annex I (2)(e) "other technical means"
residual).' considerations=['The reading chosen anchors separation in functional role-based access'] anchors=['Annex I', 'Annex I (2)', 'Annex I Part I (2)', '§4'] csf=[]

layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-03.1 Identity Lifecycle Management
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl:
id='SO-D-03.1.HL' subdomain_id='D-03.1' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source=None verified_relationship_basis=None emergent_tensions=None objective="Identities of principals that interact with the entity's
systems, products, services, components and data are managed in a
verifiable, lifecycle-aware manner with documented boundaries between
identity types and explicit hand-off protocols at boundary surfaces." considerations=['All four participating regulations impose the same substantive identity-management duty but each targets a distinct identity subject at a distinct boundary and anchors to a distinct threshold: GDPR data-subject-side proportionate verification on reasonable doubt (Art. 12(6) + Art. 11(2); minimal collection per Art. 5(1)(c)); NIS 2 workforce-side continuous joiner-mover-leaver lifecycle under HR-security discipline (Art. 21(2)(i); the access-control policy and asset-management sub-domains are coordinated by the literal AND in the same sub-point); CRA product-side verifiable identity-management for users, services and integrated components (Annex I Part I (2)(d) + Art. 13(15) + Annex II §3; the "verifiable manner" reading is stricter than the GDPR proportionality test); DORA financial-entity-side strong-authentication identity assertion management (Art. 9(4)(d); the identity-lifecycle is one of the three coordinated controls in the same sub-point — strong authentication + key protection + encryption).', 'The high-level SO describes the common identity-management duty (verifiable, lifecycle-aware, boundary-disciplined); the per-regulation perspective is preserved in the four sub-SOs (identity subject, threshold anchor, evidence template, recipient).', 'A single organisation across all four regulators must operate a multi-boundary identity architecture with explicit boundary hand-offs: data-subject verification flows into staff authentication at the rights-exercise endpoint; staff identity feeds into product-user identity via deployment; product-user identity feeds back into DORA service-identity via integration.', 'For parties that touch only one regulatory scope, only the triggered sub-SO applies.', 'CRA is the strictest knowledge-test floor ("verifiable manner") and discharges the GDPR `reasonable means proportionate to risk` on the identity-management dimension when the same party operates both manufacturer-side and controller-side roles.', "DORA's identity-assertion discipline (PR.AA-04) — managing, protecting and conveying identity assertions in a manner that verifies authenticity — is the strictest assertion-conveyance floor and supports the NIS 2 `where appropriate` test on authentication strength for financial-sector entities also within retained NIS 2 scope."] anchors=['Annex I Part I (2)', 'Annex II', 'Art. 11(2)', 'Art. 12(6)', 'Art. 13(15)', 'Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 5(1)', 'Art. 9(4)', '§3'] csf=['PR.AA-04'] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto  # activates when ≥2 applicable regs target overlapping identity boundaries on the same party'
hso_per_reg:
id='SO-D-03.1.GDPR' yaml_id='SO-D-03.1.GDPR' regulation='GDPR' subdomain_id='D-03.1' applies_to='[GDPR]' inherits_from='SO-GDPR-005' source_SR='SR-GDPR-009, SR-GDPR-010' activation='if GDPR in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='The identity of a natural person making a rights-exercise
request under Art. 15–22 is verified using reasonable means proportionate
to the risk of mis-identification, before action is taken; the controller
may request additional information necessary to confirm the identity, and
the data subject must supply enough information to enable identification
if they wish to exercise the rights (Art. 12(6) + Art. 11(2); the
verification scope is constrained by Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation).' considerations=['The operational substrate is a graduated verification standard (no verification for low-risk requests, document verification for high-risk, strong authentication for very-high-risk) plus an Art. 5(1)(c) minimisation register on the identity-verification artefacts.', 'The data-subject identity object is distinct from the NIS 2 workforce, CRA product users + services + components, and DORA staff + service identities — the controller-facing rights-exercise endpoint is the boundary, and the identity-verification policy is applied at that boundary only.', 'For an organisation across multiple regulators, the GDPR leg documents the data-subject leg of the multi-boundary identity architecture rather than imposing a separate identity-management framework; the boundary hand-off to staff authentication (D-03.2) and to product-user identity management (CRA) is documented as the controlled interface at which the GDPR verification discipline ends.', 'The downstream notification cascade (Art. 33 personal-data-breach notification) is part of D-04.3, not D-03.1.'] anchors=['Art. 11(2)', 'Art. 12(6)', 'Art. 15', 'Art. 33', 'Art. 5(1)'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-03.1.NIS2' yaml_id='SO-D-03.1.NIS2' regulation='NIS2' subdomain_id='D-03.1' applies_to='[NIS2]' inherits_from='SO-NIS2-003' source_SR='SR-NIS2-003, SR-NIS2-004' activation='if NIS2 in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective="Identities of the workforce — employees, contractors and
other authorised personnel with access to network and information
systems — are managed throughout the employment lifecycle, with
provisioning on induction, entitlement review on role change, and
revocation on separation, integrated into the entity's access-control
policy and asset-management discipline (Art. 21(2)(i) HR-security
dimension, coordinated by the literal AND with access-control policies
and asset management)." considerations=['The `appropriate and proportionate` qualifier from Art. 21(1) propagates and operationalises the lifecycle rigour: high-risk roles (privileged access, sensitive data exposure) trigger tighter verification and review cadences than low-risk roles.', 'The workforce identity object is distinct from the GDPR data subjects, CRA product users + services + components, and DORA staff + service identities — the workforce boundary is internal, and the identity-lifecycle discipline operates at that boundary only.', 'The vulnerability handling dimension of the same Art. 21(2)(e) clause captures the supplier-correspondence channel through which identity-related vulnerabilities (e.g. compromised credentials in published advisories) feed the workforce identity-lifecycle register.', 'The disclosure dimension (Art. 12(1) CSIRT-coordinated) is part of D-04.3, not D-03.1.'] anchors=['Art. 12(1)', 'Art. 21(1)', 'Art. 21(2)'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-03.1.CRA' yaml_id='SO-D-03.1.CRA' regulation='CRA' subdomain_id='D-03.1' applies_to='[CRA]' inherits_from='SO-CRA-015' source_SR='SR-CRA-023, SR-CRA-024' activation='if CRA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Identities, credentials, and access entitlements for
users, services, and integrated components of the product with digital
elements are managed in a verifiable manner throughout the operational
lifetime of the product (Annex I Part I (2)(d) + Art. 13(15)
type/batch/serial unique identification + Art. 13(17) single point of
contact; backed by Annex II §3 unique-identification user information).' considerations=['The CRA `verifiable manner` threshold is stricter than GDPR's `reasonable means proportionate to risk` — the manufacturer must demonstrate that identities are managed verifiably throughout the operational lifetime, not merely that verification is proportional to a request risk; CRDA-deep verified the CRA "verifiable manner" reading as the strictest knowledge-test floor of the four participating regulators.', 'The CRA identity-management framework is the upstream input to the controller / NIS 2 entity / DORA financial-entity identity-lifecycle programmes: the product-side identity register, the type/batch/serial marking, and the SBOM-correlated component identities feed downstream entity-side identity-management via published advisories and deployment documentation.', 'The downstream notification cascade (Annex I Part II (4)/(5) CSIRT + ENISA CVD notification) is part of D-04.3, not D-03.1.'] anchors=['Annex I Part I (2)', 'Annex I Part II (4)', 'Annex II', 'Art. 13(15)', 'Art. 13(17)', '§3'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-03.1.DORA' yaml_id='SO-D-03.1.DORA' regulation='DORA' subdomain_id='D-03.1' applies_to='[DORA]' inherits_from='SO-DORA-002' source_SR='SR-DORA-002' activation='if DORA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Identity assertions for financial-entity staff and
service-to-service identities are managed, protected, and conveyed in a
manner that verifies authenticity, as one dimension of the
strong-authentication + cryptographic-key-protection + risk-based
encryption 3-control AND in Art. 9(4)(d).' considerations=['The operational substrate is an identity provider with assertion-conveyance integrity (signed tokens, mutual transport authentication, PKI chain-of-trust), backed by authenticator inventories and AAL mappings aligned with NIST SP 800-63B AAL2/AAL3 (per the EBA Guidelines on ICT and security risk management §145–§148 dominant supervisory expectation).', 'The staff + service identity object is distinct from the GDPR data subjects, NIS 2 workforce, and CRA product users + services + components — the financial-entity boundary is internal, and the assertion-management discipline operates at that boundary only.', 'The `strong authentication mechanisms based on relevant standards and dedicated control systems` threshold is the strictest assertion-conveyance floor of the four participating regulators and discharges the NIS 2 `where appropriate` test on authentication strength for financial-sector entities also within retained NIS 2 scope.', 'For pure-financial entities (NIS 2 §9 fall-back does not apply — DORA is lex specialis), DORA absorbs the NIS 2 workforce-identity-lifecycle obligation and the high-level SO does not aggregate across the lex-specialis boundary.', 'The downstream notification cascade (Art. 19 major ICT-related incident notification) is part of D-04.3, not D-03.1'] anchors=['Art. 19', 'Art. 9(4)', '§145', '§148', '§9'] csf=[]

layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-03.2 Multi-Factor Authentication
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl:
id='SO-D-03.2.HL' subdomain_id='D-03.2' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source=None verified_relationship_basis=None emergent_tensions=None objective="Authentication of users, services, and hardware that
interact with the entity's systems, products, services, components and
data operates through an authentication mechanism of sufficient strength
for the risk in scope, with the strictest applicable floor discharging
the most permissive on the same authentication event when both apply." considerations=['All four participating regulations impose the same substantive authentication-mechanism duty but each anchors it to a distinct OJ-text explicitness level, a distinct threshold anchor, and a distinct authentication target: GDPR silent on authentication strength — staff-side via instructions + confidentiality (Art. 28(3)(b) + Art. 29), data-subject-side via verification (Art. 12(6)); NIS 2 explicit MFA or continuous authentication "where appropriate" (Art. 21(2)(j) first clause); CRA permissive "appropriate control mechanisms, may include authentication" (Annex I Part I (2)(d), no explicit MFA mandate — the "may include" reading is the literal OJ anchor); DORA demanding `strong authentication mechanisms based on relevant standards and dedicated control systems` (Art. 9(4)(d) — T4 reads MFA, OJ does not say MFA; dominant EBA Guidelines reading is MFA but the literal OJ reading admits other `strong` mechanisms; the T4-vs-text gap is P0-flagged in `SR-DORA-002` `ambiguity_notes`).', 'The high-level SO describes the common authentication-mechanism duty (sufficient strength for the risk in scope, calibrated by the strictest applicable floor); the per-regulation perspective is preserved in the four sub-SOs (OJ explicitness, threshold anchor, authentication target, evidence template, recipient).', "DORA is the strictest anchor and discharges the other three on a single authentication event when DORA applies on the same party; for parties not within DORA scope, NIS 2's `where appropriate` (read with the risk-based Art. 21(1) factors) is the operative authentication-strength floor.", 'CRA's "may include" is the product-side baseline; a CRA product implementing the NIS 2 MFA-floor or the DORA strong-authentication-floor exceeds the CRA requirement on the authentication dimension.', 'GDPR is the silent surrounding wrapper — neither MFA-mandating nor MFA-prohibiting, supplying instructions + confidentiality + minimisation rather than authentication-strength threshold.', 'The DORA T4-vs-text gap on `strong authentication` vs MFA is the operative reading-choice risk for financial entities: the dominant EBA Guidelines reading is MFA (R3), but a literal OJ reading admits other `strong` mechanisms (R5); the chosen reading in `SR-DORA-002` is mechanism-agnostic (R5) with R3 (MFA) as the dominant EU supervisory reading, pending the ESAs Joint Committee RTS under Art. 15.'] anchors=['Annex I Part I (2)', 'Art. 12(6)', 'Art. 15', 'Art. 21(1)', 'Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 28(3)', 'Art. 29', 'Art. 9(4)'] csf=[] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto  # activates when ≥2 applicable regs overlap on the same authentication event'
hso_per_reg:
id='SO-D-03.2.GDPR' yaml_id='SO-D-03.2.GDPR' regulation='GDPR' subdomain_id='D-03.2' applies_to='[GDPR]' inherits_from='SO-GDPR-006 (cross-ref), SO-GDPR-005 (cross-ref)' source_SR='SR-GDPR-011, SR-GDPR-012' activation='if GDPR in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Persons authorised to process personal data act only on
documented instructions from the controller (or processor) and are
bound by confidentiality or an appropriate statutory obligation of
confidentiality (Art. 28(3)(b) + Art. 29 + Art. 32(4) instruction-only
processing); the identity of data subjects making rights-exercise
requests is verified using reasonable means proportionate to the risk
of mis-identification (Art. 12(6) + Art. 11(2)).' considerations=['GDPR is the silent-wrapper around authentication: the OJ Art. 28(3)(b) + Art. 29 obligations govern the authorisation and confidentiality of authenticated persons (staff), and Art. 12(6) governs the verification of the data-subject requester at the rights-exercise endpoint — neither clause imposes an authentication-strength threshold.', 'The operational substrate is the chain-of-authority pattern (controller → processor → authorised persons, with documented instructions binding each link) and the verification pattern (data-subject → verification-on-reasonable-doubt → proportionate additional information).', 'A controller selecting MFA at the staff-authentication endpoint satisfies Art. 32(1)(b) confidentiality; a controller selecting single-factor password authentication is not forbidden by GDPR but must satisfy the surrounding instruction + confidentiality + minimisation obligations.', 'The downstream authentication failure notification cascade (Art. 33 personal-data-breach notification) is part of D-04.3, not D-03.2.'] anchors=['Art. 11(2)', 'Art. 12(6)', 'Art. 28(3)', 'Art. 29', 'Art. 32(1)', 'Art. 32(4)', 'Art. 33'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-03.2.NIS2' yaml_id='SO-D-03.2.NIS2' regulation='NIS2' subdomain_id='D-03.2' applies_to='[NIS2]' inherits_from='SO-NIS2-004' source_SR='SR-NIS2-006, SR-NIS2-007' activation='if NIS2 in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Multi-factor authentication or continuous authentication
solutions are used where appropriate, and secured voice, video and text
communications as well as secured emergency communication systems are
deployed within the entity (Art. 21(2)(j)).' considerations=['The OR admits both MFA and continuous-authentication as alternative authentication paradigms — they are not redundant — and the `where appropriate` hedge closes the sub-point.', "ENISA's 2022 baseline security recommendations list MFA as a default for all administrative and privileged access.", "The mechanism selection (FIDO2 / WebAuthn vs SMS-OTP vs TOTP vs hardware-token) is at the entity's discretion under the mechanism-agnostic R5 reading; the SMS-OTP reading is rejected for new deployments given the SS7 / SIM-swap attack surface.", 'NIS 2 is the most explicit OJ-text anchor among the four participating regulators (the only one with an explicit `multi-factor authentication` phrase in OJ text).', 'The `where appropriate` test discharges under the strictest applicable floor (DORA `strong authentication` ≈ MFA via EBA reading) when DORA applies on the same party.', 'The second and third clauses of Art. 21(2)(j) (secured voice/video/text + secured emergency communication systems) are addressed separately by `SR-NIS2-007` and are partially routed to D-01.2 (data-in-transit channel protection) and D-04.4 (resilience under crisis); the D-03.2 leg of NIS 2 is focused on the MFA / continuous-authentication first clause only.'] anchors=['Art. 21(2)'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-03.2.CRA' yaml_id='SO-D-03.2.CRA' regulation='CRA' subdomain_id='D-03.2' applies_to='[CRA]' inherits_from='SO-CRA-016 (partial)' source_SR='SR-CRA-023, SR-CRA-024' activation='if CRA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Protection from unauthorised access uses appropriate
control mechanisms, which may include authentication, identity, or
access-management systems, appropriate to the identified cybersecurity
risk of the product (Annex I Part I (2)(d) — "including but not limited
to" + 3-way OR).' considerations=['The OJ Annex I Part I (2)(d) text does NOT contain the phrase `multi-factor` or `continuous authentication` (the T2 mapping that imposed these phrases is rejected on the literal OJ); the OJ names authentication as one of three admitted control families (the others being identity and access-management).', 'CRA is the most permissive OJ-text anchor among the four participating regulators (the only one with an explicit "may include" language and no OJ-imposed authentication-strength threshold).', 'The CRA partial-coverage flag means that an MFA deployment at the CRA product-side exceeds the CRA requirement on the authentication dimension; a single-factor deployment at a CRA-regulated product is OJ-compliant under CRA but may not satisfy NIS 2 or DORA when those regs apply on the same party.', 'For an organisation across multiple regulators, the CRA leg documents the product-side authentication baseline that the manufacturer operates at; an authentication-mechanism choice that exceeds the CRA permissive baseline (e.g. selecting MFA where the risk assessment warrants) is documented in Annex VII and feeds the downstream controller / NIS 2 essential-entity / financial-entity authentication architecture.', 'The downstream AEV notification cascade (Art. 14) is part of D-04.3, not D-03.2.'] anchors=['Annex I Part I (2)', 'Annex VII', 'Art. 14'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-03.2.DORA' yaml_id='SO-D-03.2.DORA' regulation='DORA' subdomain_id='D-03.2' applies_to='[DORA]' inherits_from='SO-DORA-002' source_SR='SR-DORA-002' activation='if DORA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Strong authentication mechanisms (based on relevant
standards and dedicated control systems) are implemented as one of
three coordinated controls in Art. 9(4)(d), together with
cryptographic-key protection measures and risk-based data encryption.' considerations=['The operational substrate is an authenticator-inventory register, AAL mappings aligned with NIST SP 800-63B AAL2/AAL3 (per the EBA Guidelines on ICT and security risk management §145–§148 dominant supervisory expectation), and authenticator-strength calibration by risk-tier under Art. 4 proportionality.', 'DORA is the most demanding OJ-text anchor among the four participating regulators (the only one that names `relevant standards` and `dedicated control systems`); the OJ Art. 9(4)(d) text does NOT contain the phrase `multi-factor` — the T4-vs-text gap is P0-flagged — but the dominant EBA Guidelines reading is MFA. The chosen reading in `SR-DORA-002` is mechanism-agnostic (R5) with R3 (MFA) as the dominant EU supervisory reading, pending the ESAs Joint Committee RTS under Art. 15 that may eventually name specific authentication-strength standards.', 'DORA is the strictest floor; when DORA applies on the same party as the other three regulators, the DORA strong-authentication architecture discharges the NIS 2 `where appropriate` test (when NIS 2 also applies — typically only on cross-sector entities), exceeds the CRA "may include" permissive baseline, and provides the strong-authentication substrate that the GDPR silent-wrapper surrounds with instructions + confidentiality.', 'For pure-financial entities (NIS 2 §9 fall-back does not apply — DORA is lex specialis), DORA absorbs the NIS 2 authentication-strength obligation and the high-level SO does not aggregate across the lex-specialis boundary.', 'The downstream major ICT-related incident notification cascade (Art. 19) is part of D-04.3, not D-03.2.'] anchors=['Art. 15', 'Art. 19', 'Art. 4', 'Art. 9(4)', '§145', '§148', '§9'] csf=[]

layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-03.3 Authorisation & Least Privilege
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl:
id='SO-D-03.3.HL' subdomain_id='D-03.3' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source=None verified_relationship_basis=None emergent_tensions=None objective="The entitlement to perform actions on the entity's systems,
products, services, components, and data is managed per least privilege
with explicit authorisation-model choice, documented entitlements,
attack-surface-limitation evidence, and boundary hand-offs between access
surfaces." considerations=['All four participating regulations impose the same substantive authorisation duty anchored to PR.AA-05 (access permissions managed per least privilege); each targets a distinct authorisation surface at a distinct textual anchor and discharges through a distinct evidence template: GDPR instruction-bound processing (Art. 29 + Art. 32(4) + Art. 28(3)(a)/(b); the `instructions` polysemy is R1 documented-in-the-contract with operational instructions recorded contemporaneously); NIS 2 model-agnostic access-control policy (Art. 21(2)(i); the literal AND binds access-control + HR-security + asset-management together; the T3-vs-text gap on `RBAC + need-to-know + least privilege` is preserved as model-agnostic); CRA authenticated-and-authorised product access with possible-unauthorised-access reporting and attack-surface limitation (Annex I Part I (2)(d) + (2)(j); R1 inclusive reading on `possible`); DORA legitimate-and-approved functions and activities only (Art. 9(4)(c); the literal `only` qualifier is the binding floor on the financial-entity-side; the T4-vs-text gap on `need-to-know + least privilege` is preserved as OJ-literal).', 'The high-level SO surfaces the common authorisation/least-privilege duty (PR.AA-05 + PR.AA-06 anchors); the per-regulation perspective is preserved in the four sub-SOs (authorisation surface, textual anchor, evidence template, recipient).', 'A single organisation across all four regulators must operate a multi-boundary authorisation architecture with explicit boundary hand-offs: personal-data-scope instructions feed into entity-side access-control policy; entity-side access-control policy feeds into CRA product access; product-side access controls inform DORA financial-entity-side legitimate-and-approved mappings.', 'The DORA `only` qualifier is the strictest authorisation floor and discharges the CRA `limited to authenticated and authorised` and the NIS 2 `access control policies` on the same artefact when both apply.', 'The CRA `possible unauthorised access` reporting dimension is the strictest visibility floor and is not mirrored in the other three regulators; the CRA DE.CM-09 monitoring is the pair to PR.AA-05 + PR.AA-06 in the SR-CRA-024 anchor.', 'For parties that touch only one regulatory scope, only the triggered sub-SO applies.', 'CRA is the strictest reporting floor (`possible unauthorised access` R1 inclusive) and supports the NIS 2 `appropriate and proportionate` test on visibility for entities that are both NIS 2 essential entities AND CRA manufacturers.', "DORA's `only` qualifier supports the NIS 2 `where appropriate` test on authorisation tightness for financial-sector entities also within retained NIS 2 scope."] anchors=['Annex I Part I (2)', 'Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 28(3)', 'Art. 29', 'Art. 32(4)', 'Art. 9(4)'] csf=['DE.CM-09', 'PR.AA-05', 'PR.AA-06'] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto  # activates when ≥2 applicable regs target overlapping authorisation surfaces on the same party'
hso_per_reg:
id='SO-D-03.3.GDPR' yaml_id='SO-D-03.3.GDPR' regulation='GDPR' subdomain_id='D-03.3' applies_to='[GDPR]' inherits_from='SO-GDPR-006' source_SR='SR-GDPR-011, SR-GDPR-012' activation='if GDPR in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Persons authorised to process personal data act only on
documented instructions from the controller (or processor), and are
bound by confidentiality or an appropriate statutory obligation of
confidentiality, with documented instructions binding the controller →
processor → authorised-persons chain of authority under Art. 29 +
Art. 32(4) + Art. 28(3)(a)/(b) and Art. 4(7) + Art. 4(8) anchoring
controller and processor definitions.' considerations=['The `instructions` polysemy (R1 documented in contract with operational instructions recorded contemporaneously; R2 verbal with contemporaneous recording acceptable; R3 workflow-implied rejected) is preserved verbatim from `SR-GDPR-011` `ambiguity_notes`.', 'The `appropriate statutory obligation of confidentiality` polysemy (R1 equivalent-scope NDA; R2 pre-existing statutory professional-secrecy; R3 public-sector employee secrecy under Member State law in narrow contexts) is preserved from `SR-GDPR-012` `ambiguity_notes`.', 'The personal-data-scope chain of authority is distinct from the NIS 2 entity-side access-control policy, the CRA product-side authenticated-and-authorised boundary, and the DORA financial-entity-side legitimate-and-approved-only ICT-asset access — the personal-data-scope boundary is staff-side / processor-bound, and the chain-of-authority discipline operates at that boundary only.', 'For an organisation across multiple regulators, the GDPR leg documents the personal-data-scope leg of the multi-boundary authorisation architecture rather than imposing a separate authorisation framework; the boundary hand-off to NIS 2 workforce-side lifecycle (D-03.1) and to CRA product-side authorisation is documented as the controlled interface at which the GDPR instruction-bound discipline ends.', 'The downstream notification cascade (Art. 33 personal-data-breach notification) is part of D-04.3, not D-03.3.'] anchors=['Art. 28(3)', 'Art. 29', 'Art. 32(4)', 'Art. 33', 'Art. 4(7)', 'Art. 4(8)'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-03.3.NIS2' yaml_id='SO-D-03.3.NIS2' regulation='NIS2' subdomain_id='D-03.3' applies_to='[NIS2]' inherits_from='SO-NIS2-003 (partial)' source_SR='SR-NIS2-003, SR-NIS2-005 (asset-management cross-ref), SR-NIS2-004 (HR-security cross-ref)' activation='if NIS2 in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective="Access-control policies are established and applied at
the entity level for the entity's network and information systems,
covering access limited to authorised users, services, and hardware on
a least-privilege basis, with the literal AND binding access-control +
HR-security + asset-management together (Art. 21(2)(i))." considerations=['The access-control-policy reference is model-agnostic — the OJ text does not impose RBAC, ABAC, MAC or DAC — so any model that satisfies least-privilege is operative at the implementation layer (T3-vs-text gap preserved: T3 imports `RBAC + need-to-know + least privilege` vocabulary not present in the OJ; the SR preserves model-agnostic OJ language).', 'The T3-vs-text gap is preserved verbatim from `SR-NIS2-003` `ambiguity_notes`; Member State transposition divergence may apply on national AC-model compatibility (e.g. French ANSSI classified-inventory expectations for essential sectors; German BSI authoritative-register expectations).', 'The entity-side access-control policy is distinct from the GDPR personal-data-scope chain of authority, the CRA product-side authenticated-and-authorised boundary, and the DORA financial-entity-side legitimate-and-approved-only ICT-asset access — the entity-side boundary is internal, and the model-agnostic access-control policy discipline operates at that boundary only.', 'For an organisation across multiple regulators, the NIS 2 leg documents the entity-side leg of the multi-boundary authorisation architecture rather than imposing a separate authorisation framework; the boundary hand-off to GDPR personal-data-scope chain (D-03.3 GDPR sub-SO) and to CRA product-side authenticated-and-authorised boundary is documented as the controlled interface at which the NIS 2 model-agnostic discipline ends.', 'The vulnerability handling dimension of the same Art. 21(2)(e) clause captures the supplier-correspondence channel through which authorisation-related vulnerabilities (e.g. compromised credentials in published advisories) feed the entity access-control register; the disclosure dimension (Art. 12(1) CSIRT-coordinated) is part of D-04.3, not D-03.3.'] anchors=['Art. 12(1)', 'Art. 21(2)'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-03.3.CRA' yaml_id='SO-D-03.3.CRA' regulation='CRA' subdomain_id='D-03.3' applies_to='[CRA]' inherits_from='SO-CRA-017' source_SR='SR-CRA-024, SR-CRA-017 (update dissemination cross-ref)' activation='if CRA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Access to the product with digital elements, its data,

services, and hardware, with possible unauthorised access reported
(Annex I Part I (2)(d) `protection from unauthorised access through
appropriate control mechanisms` + `possible unauthorised access reported`
— R1 inclusive reading on `possible`) and attack surfaces including
external interfaces limited (Annex I Part I (2)(j)).' considerations=['The `possible unauthorised access` polysemy (R1 inclusive — any successful + any detected-but-failed attempt; R2 overreaches the literal; R3 under-reaches because successful breaches must also be reported) is preserved from `SR-CRA-024` `ambiguity_notes`.', "The CRA product authorisation framework is the upstream input to the controller / NIS 2 entity / DORA financial-entity authorisation programmes: the product-side access boundary feeds downstream entity-side access-control policy via deployment documentation and the product's reporting mechanism (under Annex I Part II (6) + Art. 13(17) per `SR-CRA-019`).", "The reporting dimension is the strictest visibility floor across the four regulations and is not mirrored in GDPR / NIS 2 / DORA's authorisation obligations; a party in CRA + GDPR + NIS 2 + DORA scope has the CRA visibility floor as the operative ceiling on the overlap surface.", 'The downstream notification cascade (Annex I Part II (4)/(5) CSIRT + ENISA CVD notification) is part of D-04.3, not D-03.3.'] anchors=['Annex I Part I (2)', 'Annex I Part II (4)', 'Annex I Part II (6)', 'Art. 13(17)'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-03.3.DORA' yaml_id='SO-D-03.3.DORA' regulation='DORA' subdomain_id='D-03.3' applies_to='[DORA]' inherits_from='SO-DORA-006' source_SR='SR-DORA-010' activation='if DORA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='ICT security policies limit physical or logical access to
information assets and ICT assets to what is required for legitimate
and approved functions and activities only, with the literal `only`
qualifier (Berry §5.3.1 — correctly placed before the limiting phrase)
closing off any access that is not strictly tied to a legitimate and
approved function (Art. 9(4)(c) physical or logical access + `legitimate
AND approved` AND-coordinated + `only` qualifier).' considerations=["The OJ `legitimate AND approved` two-axis gating (function-aligned AND governance-approved) is operationalised through PR.AA-05's documented entitlement rationales and PR.AA-06's access-request approval workflows with multi-party authorisation for privileged grants.", 'The T4-vs-text gap on `need-to-know + least privilege` (T4 imports best-practice vocabulary not in OJ; the SR preserves OJ-literal `legitimate and approved functions and activities only`) is preserved from `SR-DORA-010` `ambiguity_notes`.', 'The DORA `only` qualifier is the strictest authorisation floor across the four regulators and discharges the CRA `limited to authenticated and authorised` and the NIS 2 `access control policies` on the same access-control substrate when both apply.', 'The financial-entity-side ICT-asset access is distinct from the GDPR personal-data-scope chain of authority, the NIS 2 entity-side access-control policy, and the CRA product-side authenticated-and-authorised boundary — the financial-entity boundary is internal/ICT-asset-side, and the `legitimate and approved only` discipline operates at that boundary only.', 'For an organisation across multiple regulators, the DORA leg documents the financial-entity-side leg of the multi-boundary authorisation architecture rather than imposing a separate authorisation framework; the boundary hand-off to NIS 2 entity-side model-agnostic access-control policy and to CRA product-side authenticated-and-authorised boundary is documented as the controlled interface at which the DORA `legitimate and approved only` discipline ends.', 'For pure-financial entities (NIS 2 §9 fall-back does not apply — DORA is lex specialis), DORA absorbs the NIS 2 entity-side-access-control obligation and the high-level SO does not aggregate across the lex-specialis boundary.', 'The downstream notification cascade (Art. 19 major ICT-related incident notification) is part of D-04.3, not D-03.3.'] anchors=['Art. 19', 'Art. 9(4)', '§5', '§9'] csf=['PR.AA-05', 'PR.AA-06']

layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-03.4 Secure System Defaults
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl:
id='SO-D-03.4.HL' subdomain_id='D-03.4' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source=None verified_relationship_basis=None emergent_tensions=None objective="The default disposition of the entity's data-centric
processing systems and the product's product-centric configuration is
managed so that the baseline state of every processing system and every
product configuration is the minimum-necessary / secure configuration,
with relaxation requiring affirmative data-subject or user intervention." considerations=['The two participating regulations impose different-perspective default-disposition obligations anchored to the same CSF operational pivot (PR.PS-01 + PR.DS-12); each targets a distinct default object: GDPR data-by-default (Art. 25(2) — four AND-coordinated dimensions: amount of data collected, extent of processing, period of storage, accessibility; the four dimensions are independent minima per EDPB Guidelines 04/2019); CRA product secure-by-default (Annex I Part I (2)(b) — secure-by-default configuration + reset-to-original-state capability + tailor-made carve-out for business users + auto-update default per Annex I Part I (2)(c) — automatic security updates enabled by default with a clear and easy-to-use opt-out mechanism + notification of available updates + option to postpone temporarily).', 'The high-level SO surfaces the common default-disposition duty (baseline minimum-necessary / secure posture requiring affirmative intervention to relax); the per-regulation perspective is preserved in the two sub-SOs (default object, threshold language, evidence template, recipient).', 'A single organisation across both regulators must operate a two-layer default posture with the data-centric by-default (GDPR) and the product-centric secure-by-default (CRA) documented as two layers of the same default disposition, with the CRA tailor-made carve-out NOT propagating into GDPR scope (a CRA tailor-made product configuration does not exempt the controller from GDPR Art. 25(2)).', 'The CRA reset-to-original-state capability is the CRA-specific recovery path that returns the user to the secure baseline, supporting the GDPR Art. 25(2) four-dimension accessibility test on the data side via product recovery.', 'The CRA auto-update default (Annex I Part I (2)(c)) is the CRA-specific update-default posture that ensures vulnerabilities are addressed by default without requiring affirmative user intervention, supporting the GDPR availability-and-resilience dimension on the data side via maintained-updated product configuration.', 'For parties that touch only one regulatory scope, only the triggered sub-SO applies.', 'For proportionality (P2), a 5-FTE SaaS with both GDPR and CRA applicability can meet the GDPR + CRA floor with a documented data-minimisation by-default policy covering the four Art. 25(2) dimensions + a product secure-by-default configuration + reset capability + auto-update default; the same configuration typically satisfies both regulators with appropriate documentation.', 'CRA is the strictest configuration floor (R1 features-enabled-on-default adopted; reset capability + tailor-made carve-out architecture) and discharges the GDPR `appropriate by-default measures` when the same party operates both manufacturer-side and controller-side roles on the same product.'] anchors=['Annex I Part I (2)', 'Art. 25(2)'] csf=['PR.DS-12', 'PR.PS-01'] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto  # activates when both GDPR and CRA applicable and the CRA product processes personal data'
hso_per_reg:
id='SO-D-03.4.GDPR' yaml_id='SO-D-03.4.GDPR' regulation='GDPR' subdomain_id='D-03.4' applies_to='[GDPR]' inherits_from='SO-GDPR-007' source_SR='SR-GDPR-013' activation='if GDPR in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective="Personal-data processing systems implement appropriate
technical and organisational measures ensuring that, by default, only
personal data which are necessary for each specific purpose of the
processing are processed — across the four AND-coordinated dimensions
of amount of data collected, extent of their processing, period of their
storage, and their accessibility — with the additional constraint that
personal data are not made accessible without the individual's
intervention to an indefinite number of natural persons (Art. 25(2) +
Art. 25(1) privacy-by-design cross-anchor + Art. 5(1)(c) data
minimisation underlying principle)." considerations=['The four-dimensional AND is preserved from `SR-GDPR-013` `ambiguity_notes` (all four dimensions must individually be minimised and AND-coordinated per EDPB Guidelines 04/2019 on Article 25; an alternative reading allowing some dimensions to be relaxed if others are tightened would weaken the default and is rejected; the AND reading is the chosen one).', "On `without the individual's intervention`, the chosen reading treats the intervention requirement as the opt-in gate: the controller must not bypass the data subject's affirmative action to expose data.", 'The data-centric by-default is distinct from the CRA product-centric secure-by-default — the data-processing layer is system/configuration-of-data-side, and the four-dimension AND discipline operates at that layer only.', 'The CRA tailor-made carve-out does NOT propagate into GDPR scope: a CRA tailor-made product configuration does not exempt the controller from GDPR Art. 25(2).', 'For an organisation across both regulators, the GDPR leg documents the data-side leg of the two-layer default posture rather than imposing a separate framework; the boundary hand-off to CRA product-secure-by-default is documented as the controlled layer interface at which the data-centric four-dimension AND ends.', 'The downstream notification cascade (Art. 33 personal-data-breach notification) is part of D-04.3, not D-03.4.'] anchors=['Art. 25(1)', 'Art. 25(2)', 'Art. 33', 'Art. 5(1)', 'Article 25'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-03.4.CRA' yaml_id='SO-D-03.4.CRA' regulation='CRA' subdomain_id='D-03.4' applies_to='[CRA]' inherits_from='SO-CRA-018 + SO-CRA-019' source_SR='SR-CRA-025, SR-CRA-026, SR-CRA-018 (auto-update cross-ref)' activation='if CRA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Products with digital elements are made available on the
market with a secure-by-default configuration — including the possibility
for the user to reset the product to its original state — unless otherwise
agreed between manufacturer and business user in relation to a tailor-made
product with digital elements (Annex I Part I (2)(b)), and the
secure-by-default configuration ensures that vulnerabilities can be
addressed through security updates — automatic security updates installed
within an appropriate timeframe, enabled by default, with a clear and
easy-to-use opt-out mechanism, through notification of available updates
to users, and with the option to temporarily postpone them (Annex I Part I
(2)(c)).' considerations=['R1 features-enabled-on-default adopted on secure-by-default; R2 deny-all-initial and R3 zero-config security operationally convergent with R1 in many cases; R2 and R3 are alternative readings; R4 post-deployment-surface rejected where it would conflict with the tailor-made carve-out.', 'R1 factory-reset-no-user-data on reset-to-original-state; R2 initial-config-preserving-user-data underweights the reset semantic.', 'The tailor-made carve-out (R1 business-user-only; R2 any-customised rejected as overreach; consumer products cannot opt out of the default-secure floor) and the auto-update dimension (R1 enabled-by-default-with-opt-out adopted) are preserved from `SR-CRA-026` + `SR-CRA-018` `ambiguity_notes`.', 'The CRA tailor-made carve-out does NOT propagate into GDPR scope: a CRA tailor-made product configuration does not exempt the controller from GDPR Art. 25(2) on the data side.', 'The product-centric secure-by-default is distinct from the GDPR data-centric by-default — the product configuration layer is product-side, and the configuration-management baseline discipline operates at that layer only.', 'For an organisation across both regulators, the CRA leg documents the product-side leg of the two-layer default posture rather than imposing a separate framework; the boundary hand-off to GDPR data-centric four-dimension AND is documented as the controlled layer interface at which the product-secure-by-default ends.', 'The downstream notification cascade (Annex I Part II (4)/(5) CSIRT + ENISA CVD notification) is part of D-04.3, not D-03.4.'] anchors=['Annex I Part I
(2)', 'Annex I Part I (2)', 'Annex I Part II (4)', 'Art. 25(2)'] csf=[]

layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-04.1 Incident Detection & Triage
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl: id='SO-D-04.1.HL' subdomain_id='D-04.1' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source=None verified_relationship_basis=None emergent_tensions=None objective="Security-relevant events affecting the entity's systems, products, services, components and data are detected and triaged with documented trigger moments that anchor the downstream notification and response pipelines." considerations=["All four participating regulations (GDPR, NIS 2, CRA, DORA) impose a detection-and-triage duty but each targets a distinct detection layer and anchors to a distinct threshold: GDPR's data-flow-boundary awareness of personal-data breach (Art. 4(12) + Art. 33(1) `becoming aware` — the awareness anchor is GDPR-unique and drives the 72h clock); NIS 2's entity-side all-hazards monitoring with the 6-action incident-handling lifecycle covering `detect` (Art. 21(2) chapeau + Recital 56 + Art. 6(8) + Art. 21(2)(b)); CRA's product-side intra-product state-change visibility (Annex I Part I (2)(l); the recording-and-monitoring obligation is CRA-unique and provides the manufacturer's view inside the product boundary); DORA's financial-entity-side multi-class anomalous-activity detection with SPOF identification and threshold-driven escalation (Art. 10(1) + Art. 10(2); the multi-layer + auto-alert + SPOF pattern is DORA-unique).", 'The high-level SO surfaces the common detection-and-triage duty (detect, document the trigger moment, triage, route to the downstream response/notification pipeline); the per-regulation perspective (detection layer, trigger anchor, threshold qualifier, evidence template) is preserved in the four sub-SOs.', 'A single organisation across all four regulators must operate a multi-layer detection architecture with explicit layer hand-offs: data-flow detection feeds entity detection at the controller/NSIE boundary; entity detection feeds product detection via deployment (CRA products instrument their intra-product visibility to feed the deployer-side detection); product detection feeds back into DORA infrastructure detection via integration. For parties that touch only one regulatory scope, only the triggered sub-SO applies.', 'The high-level SO does NOT collapse the four detection layers into a single detection event — the layers detect different objects (personal-data breach vs all-hazards event vs intra-product state change vs anomalous ICT activity) and produce different trigger moments (GDPR `becoming aware`, NIS 2 detection-of-adverse-event, CRA product-internal-event-recording, DORA anomalous-activity-threshold).', 'The high-level SO is honesty-preserving about scope-disjoint cases: for a 5-FTE SaaS startup with GDPR + CRA applicability but no NIS 2 / DORA applicability, only the GDPR and CRA sub-SOs activate; the high-level SO engages on the same party if both apply, with the boundary between data-flow detection (GDPR) and product-internal detection (CRA) documented as the controlled hand-off.', "DORA's multi-layer + SPOF-identification detection (Art. 10(1)/(2)) is the strictest detection-architecture floor and supports the NIS 2 `where appropriate` test on detection depth for financial-sector entities also within retained NIS 2 scope."] anchors=['Annex I Part I (2)', 'Art. 10(1)', 'Art. 10(2)', 'Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 33(1)', 'Art. 4(12)', 'Art. 6(8)'] csf=[] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto  # activates when ≥2 applicable regs target overlapping detection layers on the same party AND ≥1 sub-SO activates'
hso_per_reg: id='SO-D-04.1.GDPR' yaml_id='SO-D-04.1.GDPR' regulation='GDPR' subdomain_id='D-04.1' applies_to='[GDPR]' inherits_from='SO-GDPR-008' source_SR='SR-GDPR-014' activation='if GDPR in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Personal-data breaches are detected and triaged, and the moment of "becoming aware" is documented to anchor the 72-hour notification clock (Art. 33(1) + Art. 4(12) breach definition).' considerations=['The GDPR detection-and-triage obligation is the data-flow-boundary detection of the controller; the operational substrate is monitoring of the five Art. 32(2) risk types (accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to personal data), with a documented `becoming aware` moment that anchors the downstream Art. 33 notification. The awareness anchor is GDPR-unique among the four D-04.1 regulators and binds the notification pipeline in D-04.3.', 'The data-flow detection object is distinct from the NIS 2 entity-level all-hazards detection, the CRA product-internal state-change recording, and the DORA anomalous-ICT-activity detection — the controller-facing data-flow boundary is the detection layer, and the awareness-anchoring discipline operates at that layer only.', 'The downstream notification cascade (Art. 33 supervisory-authority notification + Art. 34 data-subject communication) is part of D-04.3, not D-04.1.'] anchors=['Art. 32(2)', 'Art. 33', 'Art. 33(1)', 'Art. 34', 'Art. 4(12)'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-04.1.NIS2' yaml_id='SO-D-04.1.NIS2' regulation='NIS2' subdomain_id='D-04.1' applies_to='[NIS2]' inherits_from='SO-NIS2-005' source_SR='SR-NIS2-008, SR-NIS2-009' activation='if NIS2 in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='An incident-handling capability is established, covering the prevention, detection, analysis, containment, response, and recovery of incidents (Art. 21(2)(b) + Art. 6(8) six-action `incident handling` definition), with the detection dimension operationalised as all-hazards entity-level monitoring that surfaces adverse events affecting service continuity (Art. 21(2) chapeau + Recital 56).' considerations=['The NIS 2 detection-and-triage obligation is the entity-level all-hazards detection; the operational substrate is an entity-wide monitoring capability covering cybersecurity, operational, and physical-environment hazards (Recital 56 all-hazards approach), with the `detect` action as one of the six Art. 6(8) incident-handling actions. The `appropriate and proportionate` qualifier from Art. 21(1) propagates and operationalises the detection depth: high-risk roles and systems trigger deeper detection coverage than low-risk ones.', 'The entity-level detection object is distinct from the GDPR data-flow detection, the CRA product-internal state-change recording, and the DORA anomalous-ICT-activity detection — the entity boundary is internal, and the all-hazards detection discipline operates at that boundary only.', "A DORA Art. 10 detection event satisfies the NIS 2 detection obligation for the ICT-hazard subset, but the entity must extend detection to physical and operational hazards per the NIS 2 chapeau; a CRA product's Annex I (2)(l) recording feeds detection signals into the NIS 2 entity-level pipeline.", 'The downstream notification cascade (Art. 23(4) 24h early warning + 72h incident notification + 1m final report) is part of D-04.3, not D-04.1.'] anchors=['Annex I (2)', 'Art. 10', 'Art. 21(1)', 'Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 23(4)', 'Art. 6(8)'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-04.1.CRA' yaml_id='SO-D-04.1.CRA' regulation='CRA' subdomain_id='D-04.1' applies_to='[CRA]' inherits_from='SO-CRA-020' source_SR='SR-CRA-027, SR-CRA-100' activation='if CRA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Relevant internal activity of the product with digital elements — including access to or modification of data, services, or functions — is recorded and monitored, with a user-visible opt-out mechanism where appropriate, and any corruption or unauthorised modification is reported (Annex I Part I (2)(l)).' considerations=["The CRA detection-and-triage obligation is the product-internal state-change visibility; the operational substrate is an intra-product recording capability that captures state changes relevant to security, with a user-visible opt-out for events that are not security-critical. The recording-and-monitoring obligation is CRA-unique among the four D-04.1 regulators and provides the manufacturer's view inside the product boundary.", 'The product-internal detection object is distinct from the GDPR data-flow detection, the NIS 2 entity-level all-hazards detection, and the DORA anomalous-ICT-activity detection — the product boundary is internal to the product, and the intra-product recording discipline operates at that boundary only.', "The CRA product feeds detection signals into the deployer's entity-level (NIS 2) and financial-entity (DORA) detection pipelines via Annex I (2)(l); CRA detection does NOT substitute for entity-level detection (NIS 2 / DORA). For an integrated manufacturer-controller (manufacturer is also controller), the CRA product-internal recording feeds the GDPR `becoming aware` trigger for the personal-data subset; for a NIS 2 entity deploying CRA products, the Annex I (2)(l) recording feeds the NIS 2 entity-level detection.", 'The downstream notification cascade (Annex I Part II (4)/(5) CSIRT + ENISA CVD notification; Art. 14(1)/(3) AEV/SI notification) is part of D-04.3, not D-04.1.'] anchors=['Annex I (2)', 'Annex I Part I (2)', 'Annex I Part II (4)', 'Art. 14(1)'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-04.1.DORA' yaml_id='SO-D-04.1.DORA' regulation='DORA' subdomain_id='D-04.1' applies_to='[DORA]' inherits_from='SO-DORA-007' source_SR='SR-DORA-011, SR-DORA-012' activation='if DORA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Anomalous activities — including ICT network performance issues and ICT-related incidents — are promptly detected through detection mechanisms that enable multiple layers of control, define alert thresholds and criteria, trigger and initiate ICT-related incident response processes, and identify potential material single points of failure (Art. 10(1) + Art. 10(2)). An ICT-related incident management process is defined, established and implemented to detect, manage and notify ICT-related incidents (Art. 17(1)).' considerations=['The DORA detection-and-triage obligation is the financial-entity ICT infrastructure detection with SPOF identification and threshold-driven escalation; the operational substrate is a multi-layer detection architecture with explicit alert thresholds, automatic escalation to relevant ICT-incident-response staff, and SPOF identification. The multi-layer + auto-alert + SPOF pattern is DORA-unique and the strictest detection-architecture floor in the AEGIS corpus.', 'The DORA detection object is distinct from the GDPR data-flow detection, the NIS 2 entity-level all-hazards detection, and the CRA product-internal state-change recording — the financial-entity infrastructure boundary is internal to the ICT estate, and the multi-layer detection discipline operates at that boundary only.', 'A DORA Art. 10 detection event automatically feeds the GDPR Art. 33(1) `becoming aware` trigger when personal data are involved; the DORA detection architecture is the operational source of GDPR awareness events for the personal-data subset on the same party. For pure-financial entities (NIS 2 §9 fall-back does not apply — DORA is lex specialis), DORA absorbs the NIS 2 detection obligation for the ICT-hazard subset; the high-level SO does not aggregate across the lex-specialis boundary in that direction.', 'The downstream notification cascade (Art. 19(1) competent-authority + Art. 19(3) client notification) is part of D-04.3, not D-04.1.'] anchors=['Art. 10', 'Art. 10(1)', 'Art. 10(2)', 'Art. 17(1)', 'Art. 19(1)', 'Art. 19(3)', 'Art. 33(1)', '§9'] csf=[]

layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-04.2 Incident Containment & Response
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl: id='SO-D-04.2.HL' subdomain_id='D-04.2' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source=None verified_relationship_basis=None emergent_tensions=None objective="Security incidents affecting the entity's systems, products, services, components and data are contained and mitigated through appropriate measures that address the incident's impact and reduce the probability of further damage." considerations=["All four participating regulations (GDPR, NIS 2, CRA, DORA) impose a containment-and-mitigation duty but each targets a distinct containment layer and anchors to a distinct threshold: GDPR's post-breach TOMs (technical and organisational measures) including unintelligibility rendering (Art. 33(3)(d) + Art. 34(3)(a)/(b) unintelligibility carve-out; the unintelligibility rendering is GDPR-unique and acts as a substitute for Art. 34 data-subject notification when applied); NIS 2's entity-side incident-handling `contain` phase within the 6-action lifecycle (Art. 21(2)(b) + Art. 6(8) six-action definition with `contain` as one of the six actions); CRA's product-side availability preservation + cascading-impact minimisation + exploitation mitigation (Annex I Part I (2)(h) DoS resilience + (2)(i) cross-product impact minimisation + (2)(k) exploitation mitigation; the three-clause constellation is CRA-unique and operates at the product-design level); DORA's financial-entity-side BC arrangements with response and recovery plans + backup policies + restoration procedures (Art. 11(1)/(2)/(3) + Art. 12(1); the BC-arrangements architecture is DORA-unique and the strictest containment-architecture floor in the AEGIS corpus).", "The high-level SO surfaces the common containment-and-mitigation duty (contain the incident's impact, mitigate further damage, take measures to address the breach / incident, route to the downstream recovery / notification pipeline); the per-regulation perspective (containment layer, measure type, threshold qualifier, evidence template) is preserved in the four sub-SOs.", "A single organisation across all four regulators must operate a multi-layer containment architecture with explicit layer hand-offs: personal-data runbook feeds entity-level response plan at the controller/NSIE boundary; entity-level response plan feeds product resilience architecture via deployment (CRA products instrument their resilience & exploitation mitigation to support the deployer's containment); product resilience feeds back into DORA BC arrangements via integration. For parties that touch only one regulatory scope, only the triggered sub-SO applies.", 'The high-level SO does NOT collapse the four containment layers into a single measure type — the layers contain different objects (personal-data breach impact vs all-hazards entity event impact vs product availability vs ICT infrastructure) and produce different measure types (TOMs incl. unintelligibility render vs lifecycle-phase actions vs product-design choices vs BC arrangements).', 'The high-level SO is honesty-preserving about scope-disjoint cases: for a 5-FTE SaaS startup with GDPR + CRA applicability but no NIS 2 / DORA applicability, only the GDPR and CRA sub-SOs activate; the high-level SO engages on the same party if both apply, with the boundary between personal-data runbook (GDPR) and product-resilience architecture (CRA) documented as the controlled hand-off.', "DORA's BC arrangements with response-and-recovery plans (Art. 11(2)/(3)) are the strictest containment-architecture floor — they require dedicated, appropriate and documented arrangements, plans, procedures and mechanisms (the 4-way AND), plus independent internal audit for non-microenterprises (Art. 11(3) — the audit requirement is DORA-unique) — and exceed the NIS 2 `contain` requirement for financial-sector entities also within retained NIS 2 scope."] anchors=['Annex I Part I (2)', 'Art. 11(1)', 'Art. 11(2)', 'Art. 11(3)', 'Art. 12(1)', 'Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 33(3)', 'Art. 34', 'Art. 34(3)', 'Art. 6(8)'] csf=[] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto  # activates when ≥2 applicable regs target overlapping containment layers on the same party AND ≥1 sub-SO activates'
hso_per_reg: id='SO-D-04.2.GDPR' yaml_id='SO-D-04.2.GDPR' regulation='GDPR' subdomain_id='D-04.2' applies_to='[GDPR]' inherits_from='SO-GDPR-009' source_SR='SR-GDPR-015' activation='if GDPR in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Personal-data breaches are contained and mitigated through appropriate technical and organisational measures, including — where applicable — measures rendering the personal data unintelligible to any person who is not authorised to access the data (Art. 34(3)(a)) and subsequent measures that ensure the high risk no longer materialises (Art. 34(3)(b)); the controller describes the measures taken or proposed in the Art. 33(3)(d) supervisory-authority notification.' considerations=['The GDPR containment-and-mitigation obligation is the personal-data post-breach runbook; the operational substrate is a TOMs catalogue that the controller applies when a personal-data breach is detected, with the unintelligibility rendering as the GDPR-unique carve-out that operates as a substitute for Art. 34 data-subject notification when applied. The `where appropriate` qualifier from Art. 33(3)(d) propagates and operationalises the TOMs catalogue depth: high-risk data categories (special categories, financial data, health data) trigger deeper and more aggressive containment than low-risk categories.', 'The personal-data post-breach measure object is distinct from the NIS 2 entity-level lifecycle-phase actions, the CRA product-design availability choices, and the DORA BC arrangements — the controller-facing post-breach runbook is the containment layer, and the TOMs discipline operates at that layer only.', 'For a multi-reg party, the GDPR TOMs are documented as a section within the NIS 2 entity-level response plan (Doc 07 downstream implication) or within the DORA BC arrangements (Doc 07 downstream implication), not as a separate runbook.', 'The downstream notification cascade (Art. 33 supervisory-authority notification including the measures description) is part of D-04.3, not D-04.2.'] anchors=['Art. 33', 'Art. 33(3)', 'Art. 34', 'Art. 34(3)'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-04.2.NIS2' yaml_id='SO-D-04.2.NIS2' regulation='NIS2' subdomain_id='D-04.2' applies_to='[NIS2]' inherits_from='SO-NIS2-005' source_SR='SR-NIS2-008' activation='if NIS2 in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='The entity operates the incident-handling capability across all six actions of the Art. 6(8) `incident handling` lifecycle (prevent, detect, analyse, contain, respond, recover), with the `contain` action documented in the entity-level response plan as the lifecycle phase that isolates affected systems and prevents further damage (Art. 21(2)(b)).' considerations=['The NIS 2 containment-and-mitigation obligation is the entity-level incident-handling `contain` phase; the operational substrate is the entity-wide response plan with the `contain` action as one of the six Art. 6(8) incident-handling actions. The `appropriate and proportionate` qualifier from Art. 21(1) propagates and operationalises the containment depth: high-impact incidents trigger deeper and more aggressive containment than low-impact ones.', 'The entity-level lifecycle-phase action object is distinct from the GDPR personal-data post-breach runbook, the CRA product-design availability choices, and the DORA BC arrangements — the entity response plan is the containment layer, and the lifecycle-phase discipline operates at that layer only.', 'For a multi-reg party, the NIS 2 response plan is the procedural wrapper that hosts the GDPR Art. 33(3)(d) TOMs (controller/NSIE scenario) and the CRA Annex I (2)(h)/(i)/(k) product-resilience evidence (NIS 2 deployer scenario).', 'The downstream notification cascade (Art. 23(4)(b) incident notification + Art. 23(4)(d) 1m final report with mitigation measures) is part of D-04.3, not D-04.2.'] anchors=['Annex I (2)', 'Art. 21(1)', 'Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 23(4)', 'Art. 33(3)', 'Art. 6(8)'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-04.2.CRA' yaml_id='SO-D-04.2.CRA' regulation='CRA' subdomain_id='D-04.2' applies_to='[CRA]' inherits_from='SO-CRA-021' source_SR='SR-CRA-043, SR-CRA-044' activation='if CRA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='The availability of essential and basic functions of a product with digital elements is protected also after an incident, through resilience and mitigation measures including resistance to and recovery from denial-of-service attacks (Annex I Part I (2)(h)); the manufacturer minimises the negative impact by the product itself or connected devices on the availability of services provided by other devices or networks (Annex I Part I (2)(i)); the manufacturer reduces the impact of an incident using appropriate exploitation-mitigation mechanisms and techniques (Annex I Part I (2)(k)). Where the manufacturer knows or has reason to believe that the product or processes are not in conformity with the Annex I cybersecurity requirements, the manufacturer takes the corrective measures necessary to bring the product into conformity, or to withdraw or recall the product (Art. 13(21)).' considerations=['The CRA containment-and-mitigation obligation is the product-level post-incident availability + cross-product impact + exploitation mitigation architecture; the operational substrate is a product-design framework that combines DoS resilience (Annex I Part I (2)(h)), cascading-impact minimisation (Annex I Part I (2)(i)), and exploitation-mitigation mechanisms (Annex I Part I (2)(k)). The three-clause constellation is CRA-unique and operates at the product-design level — the containment happens inside the product boundary.', 'The product-design measure object is distinct from the GDPR personal-data post-breach runbook (post-event reaction), the NIS 2 entity-level lifecycle-phase actions (entity boundary), and the DORA BC arrangements (financial-entity infrastructure) — the product boundary is internal to the product, and the design-level resilience discipline operates at that boundary only.', "The CRA product's Annex I (2)(h)/(i)/(k) architecture supports entity-level NIS 2 containment by reducing blast radius; for a DORA financial entity deploying CRA products, the CRA resilience design feeds the DORA BC arrangements. The CRA containment is pre-event design + post-incident availability preservation, temporally distinct from GDPR's post-event reaction; the high-level SO does not collapse the temporal distinction.", 'The downstream notification cascade (Annex I Part II (4)/(5) CSIRT + ENISA CVD notification; Art. 14(1)/(3) AEV/SI notification including corrective measures) is part of D-04.3, not D-04.2.'] anchors=['Annex I', 'Annex I (2)', 'Annex I Part I (2)', 'Annex I Part II (4)', 'Art. 13(21)', 'Art. 14(1)'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-04.2.DORA' yaml_id='SO-D-04.2.DORA' regulation='DORA' subdomain_id='D-04.2' applies_to='[DORA]' inherits_from='SO-DORA-010' source_SR='SR-DORA-013, SR-DORA-014, SR-DORA-016' activation='if DORA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='A comprehensive ICT business continuity policy is operationalised through dedicated, appropriate and documented arrangements, plans, procedures and mechanisms — including ICT response and recovery plans (subject to independent internal audit for non-microenterprises), backup policies and procedures specifying the scope of data subject to backup and the minimum frequency of backup based on criticality or confidentiality, and restoration and recovery procedures and methods (Art. 11(1) + Art. 11(2) + Art. 11(3) + Art. 12(1)).' considerations=['The DORA containment-and-mitigation obligation is the financial-entity BC arrangements architecture; the operational substrate is a comprehensive BC policy with dedicated, appropriate and documented arrangements including response and recovery plans, backup policies, and restoration procedures; the BC arrangements are subject to independent internal audit for non-microenterprises (the audit requirement is DORA-unique — no other participating regulator imposes an audit obligation on the containment architecture).', 'The BC arrangements measure object is distinct from the GDPR personal-data post-breach runbook, the NIS 2 entity-level lifecycle-phase actions, and the CRA product-design availability choices — the financial-entity BC boundary is internal to the ICT estate, and the BC arrangements discipline operates at that boundary only.', 'For a multi-reg party, the DORA BC arrangements exceed the NIS 2 `contain` requirement for the financial-services subset of incidents; the GDPR Art. 33(3)(d) personal-data TOMs are documented as a section within the DORA BC arrangements (Doc 07 downstream implication), not as a separate runbook. For pure-financial entities (NIS 2 §9 fall-back does not apply — DORA is lex specialis), DORA absorbs the NIS 2 `contain` requirement for the financial-services subset; the high-level SO does not aggregate across the lex-specialis boundary in that direction.', 'The downstream notification cascade (Art. 19(1) competent-authority + Art. 19(3) client notification) is part of D-04.3, not D-04.2.'] anchors=['Art. 11(1)', 'Art. 11(2)', 'Art. 11(3)', 'Art. 12(1)', 'Art. 19(1)', 'Art. 19(3)', 'Art. 33(3)', '§9'] csf=[]

layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl: id='SO-D-04.3.HL' subdomain_id='D-04.3' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source='../../CrossRegulation/DeepAnalysis/D-04_Incident-Response/D-04.3.md §D-04.3' verified_relationship_basis='CRDA-deep verified (10 pairs, 1 SAME + 1 COMPLEMENTARY + 3 SCOPE-DISJOINT + 5 CONTRADICTORY / CONDITIONAL-CONTRADICTORY)' emergent_tensions=2 objective="A major security incident is notified to the applicable recipients within the regulatory timelines applicable to the event's material scope." considerations=["Where the same event overlaps with ≥2 regulations' scopes (e.g., a personal data breach at a financial entity using a CRA-classified high-risk AI product), all applicable timelines bind in parallel from the event's trigger moment — the entity must discharge each applicable notification in parallel, using each regulation's own clock and template. The timelines differ (4h / 24h / 72h / 14d / 15d / 1m) because they are different legislative instruments each governing a different recipient; they apply in parallel when the same event triggers multiple regulations, NOT as contradictions on a single recipient.", "The high-level SO surfaces the cross-recipient map across 5 distinct recipient classes (DPA / CSIRT or CA / financial CA / MSA / AI Office) and the parallel-clock binding requirement. The high-level SO does NOT collapse the per-regulation perspective — each regulation's substantive content template and recipient remains distinct; the per-regulation perspective is preserved in the five sub-SOs.", 'For events that touch only one regulatory scope, only the triggered sub-SO applies.'] anchors=[] csf=[] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto'
hso_per_reg: id='SO-D-04.3.GDPR' yaml_id='SO-D-04.3.GDPR' regulation='GDPR' subdomain_id='D-04.3' applies_to='[GDPR]' inherits_from='SO-GDPR-010' source_SR='SR-GDPR-016' activation='if GDPR in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N  # if GDPR-only, high-level SO is redundant; sub-SO used directly' verified_relationship=None objective="A personal data breach is notified to the competent supervisory authority without undue delay and, where feasible, no later than 72 hours after the controller becomes aware of the breach — unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to data subjects' rights and freedoms (Art. 33(1))." considerations=['The `where feasible` softening of the 72-hour clock is GDPR-unique among the D-04.3 regulators; the other D-04.3 regulations impose stricter `in any event` ceilings. When NIS 2 and GDPR both apply, the NIS 2 ceiling binds (no `where feasible` softening).'] anchors=['Art. 33(1)'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-04.3.NIS2' yaml_id='SO-D-04.3.NIS2' regulation='NIS2' subdomain_id='D-04.3' applies_to='[NIS2]' inherits_from='SO-NIS2-006' source_SR='SR-NIS2-010' activation='if NIS2 in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='A significant incident is notified to the CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority via a twin-trigger pattern — an early warning within 24 hours of awareness (Art. 23(4)(a), `SR-NIS2-010`) followed by an incident notification within 72 hours with severity, impact, and (where available) indicators of compromise (Art. 23(4)(b), `SR-NIS2-011`).' considerations=['The `in any event` ceiling of the NIS 2 72-hour clock leaves no `where feasible` softening — when NIS 2 and GDPR both apply on the same event, the NIS 2 ceiling binds (24h early warning + 72h notification + 1m final report); the GDPR `where feasible` softening does not survive the multi-reg overlap.'] anchors=['Art. 23(4)'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-04.3.CRA' yaml_id='SO-D-04.3.CRA' regulation='CRA' subdomain_id='D-04.3' applies_to='[CRA]' inherits_from='SO-CRA-024' source_SR='SR-CRA-029' activation='if CRA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='An actively-exploited vulnerability contained in a product with digital elements that the manufacturer becomes aware of is notified on a three-tier temporal pattern: early warning within 24 hours (Art. 14(2)(a), `SR-CRA-029`); vulnerability notification within 72 hours with general information, nature of exploit, mitigations, and user actions (Art. 14(2)(b), `SR-CRA-030`); final report within 14 days of a corrective or mitigating measure being available (Art. 14(2)(c), `SR-CRA-030`).' considerations=['The 14-day AEV final tier is CRA-unique and tighter than any NIS 2 / DORA tier. CRA introduces a separate severe-incident (SI) pathway (24h / 72h / 1m) for non-AEV severe incidents per Art. 14(3)/(4).'] anchors=['Art. 14(2)', 'Art. 14(3)'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-04.3.DORA' yaml_id='SO-D-04.3.DORA' regulation='DORA' subdomain_id='D-04.3' applies_to='[DORA]' inherits_from='SO-DORA-008' source_SR='SR-DORA-017' activation='if DORA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='A major ICT-related incident is reported to the relevant competent authority without undue delay (Art. 19(1)); affected clients are separately informed without undue delay as soon as the financial entity becomes aware of the major ICT-related incident (Art. 19(3)).' considerations=['Under the literal OJ text of Art. 19(1), no hard hour-anchor is supplied; the temporal anchor is delegated to the EBA / ESMA / EIOPA RTS under Art. 18(3) and partially addressed in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2956.', 'Where the incident also involves personal data, the parallel GDPR 72h notification under Art. 33 binds via the binding-procedure principle (CRDA-deep §D-04.3 GDPR↔DORA pair): the `where feasible` softening of GDPR does not survive the multi-reg overlap with DORA.', 'Affected-client notification under Art. 19(3) — and, where the OJ-corrective note in `SR-DORA-017` applies, only when the incident has financial-interest impact on clients.'] anchors=['Art. 18(3)', 'Art. 19(1)', 'Art. 19(3)', 'Art. 33'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-04.3.AI_Act' yaml_id='SO-D-04.3.AI_Act' regulation='AI_Act' subdomain_id='D-04.3' applies_to='[AI_Act]' inherits_from='SO-AI_Act-013' source_SR='SR-AI_Act-022' activation='if AI_Act in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='A serious incident involving a high-risk AI system is reported to the market surveillance authorities of the Member States where the incident occurred under a differentiated 4-timeline × 4-trigger matrix (Art. 73(1)–(4)): 15 days after the provider becomes aware (default); 10 days if the incident results in death; 2 days for widespread infringement; 15 days from reasonable likelihood of causal link (whichever is later with the awareness trigger, per Art. 73(2)).' considerations=["The Art. 73 obligation is the most temporally complex notification clause in the AEGIS corpus; the 4-trigger × 4-timeline matrix exceeds any other regulator's single-clock pattern. Operationally, an entity subject to AI Act + GDPR + NIS 2 + CRA + DORA on a single serious AI incident must discharge up to 6 distinct deadlines (2d AI Act widespread-infringement + 10d AI Act death + 15d AI Act default + 24h NIS 2 early warning + 72h GDPR / NIS 2 / CRA + 14d CRA AEV + 1m NIS 2 / CRA final).", 'GPAI providers of systemic-risk models separately report under `SR-AI_Act-024` / `SO-AI_Act-014` to the AI Office without undue delay — distinct recipient, separate clock. The AI Act therefore introduces two distinct recipient classes (MSAs for high-risk AI serious incidents, AI Office for GPAI systemic-risk incidents), each with its own clock pattern.'] anchors=['Art. 73', 'Art. 73(1)', 'Art. 73(2)'] csf=[]
