layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-04.4 Incident Recovery & Lessons Learned
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl: id='SO-D-04.4.HL' subdomain_id='D-04.4' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source=None verified_relationship_basis=None emergent_tensions=None objective='Systems, products, services, components and data are restored and recovered with documented recovery evidence applicable to the recovery dimensions of all four participating regulators on the same party.' considerations=["All four participating regulations (GDPR, NIS 2, CRA, DORA) impose a restoration-and-recovery duty but each operates on a distinct recovery layer with a distinct calibration: GDPR's personal-data timely-manner restoration of availability and access (Art. 32(1)(c) + Art. 5(1)(f) cross + Art. 32(2) risk-enumeration cross; the `timely manner` VAG anchor is the personal-data-specific outcome but does NOT specify a clock — the VAG is resolved by operational layering with NIS 2 / DORA cadence); NIS 2's entity-side BC + backup + DR + CM triad (Art. 21(2)(c) + Art. 21(1) `appropriate and proportionate` + all-hazards chapeau + Recital 56); CRA's product-side intra-product availability preservation also after an incident through resilience and DoS-mitigation (Annex I Part I (2)(h) + exploitation-mitigation (2)(k) + cross-product impact containment (2)(i)); DORA's financial-entity-side comprehensive ICT BC policy with dedicated arrangements, response and recovery plans (independent internal audit for non-microenterprises), backup policies on criticality/confidentiality, and restoration/recovery procedures and methods (Art. 11(1)–(3) + Art. 12(1); subject to the OJ-corrective note on Art. 11(2)(c)/(d)/(e) objective labelling — see DORA sub-SO below).", 'The high-level SO surfaces the common restoration duty (restore availability, integrity and resilience of systems, products, services, components and data; document the recovery architecture; test the recovery capability; deliver the recovery evidence); the per-regulation perspective (recovery layer, anchor, calibration/cadence, evidence template, independent-verification scope) is preserved in the four sub-SOs.', 'A single organisation across all four regulators must operate a multi-layer recovery architecture with explicit layer hand-offs: CRA product resilience reduces the probability that NIS 2 entity BC framework needs to engage; NIS 2 entity BC framework + backup + DR + CM is the operational vehicle that discharges the GDPR `timely manner` outcome for non-financial entities and financial-entity-non-DORA parties; DORA Art. 11–12 is the stricter financial-sector overlay that resolves the GDPR `timely` VAG anchor via the Art. 12(1)(a) backup-scoping on criticality or confidentiality and the Art. 12(1)(b) restoration/recovery procedures and methods, with Art. 11(3) independent internal audit review for non-microenterprises as the verification floor. For parties that touch only one regulatory scope, only the triggered sub-SO applies.', 'The high-level SO does NOT collapse the four recovery layers into a single recovery event — the layers recover different objects (product-resilience vs entity-BC vs backup-architecture vs personal-data-outcome) and produce different evidence templates (resilience-architecture under Annex VII §2 vs BC plan + backup records + DR tests + CM records vs DORA backup-and-restoration documentation + audit-review records vs GDPR controller-side recovery-exercise records under Art. 5(2) + Art. 32 documentation expectations).', 'The high-level SO is honesty-preserving about scope-disjoint cases: for a 5-FTE SaaS startup with GDPR + CRA applicability but no NIS 2 / DORA applicability, only the GDPR and CRA sub-SOs activate; the high-level SO engages on the same party if both apply, with the boundary between CRA product resilience (CRA) and GDPR controller restoration outcome (GDPR) documented as the layer-segregated hand-off (CRA-product resilience reduces probability of restoration trigger; controller still owns the restoration outcome).', "DORA's Art. 12(1)(a) backup-scoping on criticality or confidentiality (VAG) + Art. 11(3) independent internal audit (non-microenterprises) is the strictest recovery-architecture floor and supports the NIS 2 `appropriate and proportionate` test on recovery depth for financial-sector entities also within retained NIS 2 scope, but does NOT make DORA co-extensive with NIS 2 (the DORA-specific overlay is material: response and recovery plans as distinct artefacts; backup-scoping on the risk-based criterion; audit-verified BC arrangements — see DORA sub-SO below)."] anchors=['Annex I Part I (2)', 'Annex VII', 'Art. 11', 'Art. 11(1)', 'Art. 11(2)', 'Art. 11(3)', 'Art. 12(1)', 'Art. 21(1)', 'Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 32', 'Art. 32(1)', 'Art. 32(2)', 'Art. 5(1)', 'Art. 5(2)', '§2'] csf=[] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto  # activates when ≥2 applicable regs target overlapping recovery layers on the same party AND ≥1 sub-SO activates'
hso_per_reg: id='SO-D-04.4.GDPR' yaml_id='SO-D-04.4.GDPR' regulation='GDPR' subdomain_id='D-04.4' applies_to='[GDPR]' inherits_from='SO-GDPR-014' source_SR='SR-GDPR-024' activation='if GDPR in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='The ability to ensure the ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems and services is maintained, and to restore the availability and access to personal data in a timely manner in the event of a physical or technical incident (Art. 32(1)(b) + Art. 32(1)(c); Art. 5(1)(f) integrity/confidentiality cross-reference; Art. 32(2) five-event risk-enumeration cross).' considerations=['The GDPR restoration-and-recovery obligation is the personal-data-availability outcome of the controller; the operational substrate is a tested recovery capability with per-processing-activity RTO/RPO targets, where tested backups (PR.DS-11) and recovery-execution evidence (RC.RP-04) are the verifiable artefacts the supervisory authority may inspect under Art. 58 to confirm Art. 5(2) accountability.', 'The `timely manner` anchor (Art. 32(1)(c)) is VAG (Recital 49 reads "as soon as possible", non-binding); operationalised via (a) tested recovery exercises for non-financial parties — the controller documents RTO per processing activity consistent with the BC framework — or (b) NIS 2 BC framework cadence on NIS 2 + GDPR parties — the NIS 2 BC plan + backup records + DR tests + CM records supply the operationalised evidence base. For a financial-entity + GDPR party, DORA Art. 12(1)(a) backup-scoping on criticality/confidentiality + Art. 12(1)(b) restoration/recovery procedures and methods resolve the `timely` VAG via the Art. 11(3) independent internal audit floor on non-microenterprises.', 'The personal-data-outcome object is distinct from the NIS 2 entity-level BC framework, the CRA product-internal resilience, and the DORA financial-entity BC framework + backup-architecture — the data-availability outcome is verified at the processing-system layer, and the restoration-and-recovery discipline operates at that layer.', 'The controller is responsible for the personal-data-outcome verification, not for the upstream architecture (which is shared with NIS 2 / DORA where applicable) or for the product-resilience layer (which is shared with CRA where applicable). The Art. 32 documentation expectations + Art. 5(2) accountability provide the supervisory-authority evidence path; BC framework documentation + recovery-exercise records + backup-test results are the audit-grade evidence base.'] anchors=['Art. 11(3)', 'Art. 12(1)', 'Art. 32', 'Art. 32(1)', 'Art. 32(2)', 'Art. 5(1)', 'Art. 5(2)', 'Art. 58'] csf=['PR.DS-11', 'RC.RP-04']

id='SO-D-04.4.NIS2' yaml_id='SO-D-04.4.NIS2' regulation='NIS2' subdomain_id='D-04.4' applies_to='[NIS2]' inherits_from='SO-NIS2-013' source_SR='SR-NIS2-019' activation='if NIS2 in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Business continuity, backup management, disaster recovery, and crisis management capabilities are maintained, ensuring the ability to restore the availability and integrity of network and information systems and to manage crises arising from significant incidents (Art. 21(2)(c); the `business continuity, such as backup management and disaster recovery, and crisis management` structure imposes an AND chain across the BC + backup + DR + CM triad).' considerations=["The NIS 2 restoration-and-recovery obligation is the entity-level BC triad (BC + backup + DR + CM, with `business continuity` and `crisis management` as the outer AND and `backup management` and `disaster recovery` as inner pillars per the `such as` opening); the operational substrate is a tested BC framework with the all-hazards chapeau extending the recovery envelope to operational + physical-environment + cyber hazards (Recital 56), and the `appropriate and proportionate` qualifier (Art. 21(1)) calibrates the recovery depth to the entity's risk classification.", 'The BC-framework object is distinct from the GDPR personal-data-availability outcome, the CRA product-internal resilience, and the DORA financial-entity BC framework + backup-architecture — the entity-boundary BC framework is the operational vehicle that delivers the recovery cadence; on a NIS 2 + DORA party, the DORA BC framework absorbs the NIS 2 BC/DR/CM obligation for the ICT-hazard subset (DORA is lex specialis on pure-financial entities); the NIS 2 all-hazards chapeau extends beyond ICT (operational + physical-environment hazards).', "A NIS 2 BC framework operationalises the GDPR `timely manner` VAG anchor (Art. 32(1)(c)) for non-financial parties — the BC framework cadence + tested recovery-exercise records supply the measurable evidence base. CRA Annex I Part I (2)(h) product-internal resilience feeds into the NIS 2 BC framework via deployment (CRA products instrument their intra-product resilience to reduce the load on the entity's BC framework).", 'The NIS 2 BC framework does NOT have a dedicated independent-internal-audit floor (the supervisory authority / CSIRT evidence path is the audit channel; Member State transposition may add internal-audit obligations on a national basis); for DORA + NIS 2 cross-sector parties, DORA Art. 11(3) independent internal audit for non-microenterprises operates as the verification floor on the joint BC framework.'] anchors=['Annex I Part I (2)', 'Art. 11(3)', 'Art. 21(1)', 'Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 32(1)'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-04.4.CRA' yaml_id='SO-D-04.4.CRA' regulation='CRA' subdomain_id='D-04.4' applies_to='[CRA]' inherits_from='SO-CRA-021' source_SR='SR-CRA-043' activation='if CRA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='The availability of essential and basic functions of a product with digital elements is protected *also after an incident*, through resilience and mitigation measures including resistance to and recovery from denial-of-service attacks, and the manufacturer reduces the impact of an incident using appropriate exploitation-mitigation mechanisms and techniques and minimises the negative impact on services of other devices and networks (Annex I Part I (2)(h) + (2)(k) + (2)(i) + Art. 13(21) corrective measures).' considerations=['The CRA restoration-and-recovery obligation (which overlaps D-04.2 + D-04.4 in the source SO/SR) is the product-internal resilience + exploitation-mitigation architecture; the operational substrate is an intra-product resilience mechanism (engineered pre-incident so that essential and basic functions survive an attack) plus an exploitation-mitigation mechanism (operating at the binary layer + runtime layer — rate-limiting, ASLR/DEP, control-flow integrity, configuration hardening) plus a cross-product impact containment (minimising negative impact on services of other devices or networks, the (2)(i) CRA-unique cross-boundary responsibility), all risk-calibrated via the Art. 13(2) risk assessment.', 'The product-resilience object is distinct from the GDPR personal-data-availability outcome, the NIS 2 entity-level BC framework, and the DORA financial-entity BC framework + backup-architecture — the product boundary is internal to the product, and the intra-product resilience discipline operates at that boundary.', "The CRA product reduces the probability that an entity-level recovery event materialises (the product continues to function during/after attack), but does NOT replace the deployer's entity-level BC framework for cases where the product itself fails or the attack propagates beyond the product boundary. For an integrated manufacturer-controller (manufacturer is also controller), the CRA product-internal resilience feeds the controller-side recovery-evidence base via the technical documentation under Annex VII (general description §1 + design / vuln-handling processes §2 + SBOM §2 + risk-assessment §3); for a NIS 2 entity deploying CRA products, the Annex I Part I (2)(h) resilience reduces the load on the entity-level BC framework via deployment.", 'The CRA `also after an incident` anchor (Annex I Part I (2)(h)) is design-time and runtime — the resilience mechanism must be in place before the incident, not bolted on after. The Annex VII §6 test-reports demonstrating verification of conformity with Annex I Part I and Part II cybersecurity requirements (including the post-incident-availability obligation of (2)(h)) are the market-surveillance evidence base on a reasoned request.'] anchors=['Annex I Part I', 'Annex I Part I (2)', 'Annex VII', 'Annex VII (general description §1 + design / vuln-handling processes §2 + SBOM §2 + risk-assessment §3)', 'Art. 13(2)', 'Art. 13(21)', '§1', '§2', '§3', '§6'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-04.4.DORA' yaml_id='SO-D-04.4.DORA' regulation='DORA' subdomain_id='D-04.4' applies_to='[DORA]' inherits_from='SO-DORA-010' source_SR='SR-DORA-013, SR-DORA-014, SR-DORA-015' activation='if DORA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='A comprehensive ICT business continuity policy is operationalised through dedicated, appropriate and documented arrangements, plans, procedures and mechanisms, including ICT response and recovery plans (subject to independent internal audit review for non-microenterprises, Art. 11(3)), backup policies and procedures specifying the scope of the data subject to backup and the minimum frequency of the backup, based on the criticality of information or the confidentiality level of the data (Art. 12(1)(a)), and restoration and recovery procedures and methods (Art. 12(1)(b)).' considerations=['The DORA restoration-and-recovery obligation is the financial-entity ICT BC framework with backup-architecture on criticality/confidentiality + restoration/recovery procedures + audit verification on non-microenterprises; the operational substrate is a comprehensive BC policy (Art. 11(1)) operationalised via dedicated-and-documented arrangements, plans, procedures and mechanisms (Art. 11(2) 3-way AND of adjectives + 4-way AND of artefact types), with response and recovery plans as distinct artefacts (Art. 11(3); independent internal audit review for non-microenterprises), backup policies on criticality or confidentiality (Art. 12(1)(a) — the measurable backup-tier calibration), and restoration and recovery procedures and methods (Art. 12(1)(b) — the technical-and-service coordination).', 'The DORA BC-framework object is distinct from the GDPR personal-data-availability outcome, the NIS 2 entity-level BC framework, and the CRA product-internal resilience — the financial-entity ICT-infrastructure boundary is internal to the ICT estate, and the BC-framework discipline operates at that boundary.', 'A DORA-compliant BC framework discharges the GDPR `timely manner` VAG anchor (Art. 32(1)(c)) for the personal-data subset via the Art. 12(1)(a) backup-tier calibration + Art. 12(1)(b) restoration/recovery procedures + Art. 11(3) independent internal audit floor on non-microenterprises (the audit-verification dimension is material — the recovery arrangements are demonstrably operational, not merely aspirational).', 'A DORA BC framework absorbs the NIS 2 BC/DR/CM obligation for the ICT subset on DORA + NIS 2 parties (DORA is lex specialis on pure-financial entities); the DORA overlayer is material (response and recovery plans as distinct artefacts; risk-calibrated backup scoping; audit-verified BC arrangements — see DORA-correction flag below) and NOT co-extensive with NIS 2. For pure-financial entities (NIS 2 §9 fall-back does not apply), DORA absorbs the NIS 2 BC/DR/CM obligation for the ICT-hazard subset; the high-level SO does NOT aggregate across the lex-specialis boundary in that direction.'] anchors=['Art. 11(1)', 'Art. 11(2)', 'Art. 11(3)', 'Art. 12(1)', 'Art. 32(1)', '§9'] csf=[]

layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-05.1 Data Minimisation
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl: id='SO-D-05.1.HL' subdomain_id='D-05.1' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source=None verified_relationship_basis=None emergent_tensions=None objective='Data collected or otherwise acquired is limited to what is adequate, relevant, and necessary in relation to the purpose for which it is processed, with a documented necessity assessment and, where the underlying purpose changes, a compatibility assessment confirming that the new use is consistent with the original. Special-category data is processed only where a narrow exception applies and is documented to that effect.' considerations=['Three participating regulations (GDPR, CRA, AI Act) each impose this duty on a distinct data class at a distinct trigger: GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) "adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary" on personal data (controller-driven) plus the Art. 6(4) change-of-purpose compatibility test and Art. 9(1) special-category prohibition; CRA Annex I Part I (2)(g) verbatim "adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary" on product data (manufacturer-design, tied to Art. 3(23) intended purpose); AI Act Art. 10(1)/(2) 8-element data-governance practice + Art. 10(3) 4-criterion dataset quality on training data (provider-driven).', 'CRDA-deep verified relationships: GDPR↔CRA = SAME (verbatim operative-language match, controller-driven purpose vs manufacturer-design intended purpose); CRA↔AI_Act = SAME (runtime product data vs training pipeline data, different lifecycle stages); GDPR↔AI_Act = CORRECTED from CONTRADICTORY to SCOPE-DISJOINT with explicit AI Act Art. 10(5) carve-out into GDPR Art. 9(1) (the exception-permission pattern, not prohibition-vs-prohibition).', 'The 1 conditional emergent tension (Art. 10(5) special-category gateway) is regulated by the 6-cumulative-condition matrix (a)–(f): bias detection cannot be achieved by other data + strict necessity + safeguards + enhanced governance + documentation + post-bias deletion. Outside that narrow window, GDPR Art. 9(1) prohibition binds and AI Act Art. 10(5) does not extend.', 'Implementation guidance: the three data classes are layered not collapsed — personal data is collected from data subjects (GDPR), product data is collected at runtime by the product (CRA), training data is collected upstream for the training pipeline (AI Act). A unified data-management platform may serve the technical substrate, but policy and evidence layers must remain class-segregated.', 'Scope caveats: GDPR-CRA verbatim language overlap is literal and the stricter operational interpretation binds on the shared risk substrate; CRA-AI_Act operates at sequential lifecycle stages (runtime vs training pipeline, disjoint in baseline); AI Act Art. 10(5) gateway does NOT extend to other special-category processing beyond the bias-correction window; the high-level SO does NOT relax GDPR Art. 9(1) prohibition beyond what Art. 10(5) explicitly permits.'] anchors=['Annex I Part I (2)', 'Art. 10(1)', 'Art. 10(3)', 'Art. 10(5)', 'Art. 3(23)', 'Art. 5(1)', 'Art. 6(4)', 'Art. 9(1)'] csf=[] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto  # activates when ≥2 applicable regs target overlapping data classes on the same party AND the Art. 10(5) carve-out does not dissolve the engagement'
hso_per_reg: id='SO-D-05.1.GDPR' yaml_id='SO-D-05.1.GDPR' regulation='GDPR' subdomain_id='D-05.1' applies_to='[GDPR]' inherits_from='SO-GDPR-015 + SO-GDPR-016 (cross-ref)' source_SR='SR-GDPR-025, SR-GDPR-026' activation='if GDPR in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Personal data collected and processed are limited to what is adequate, relevant, and necessary in relation to the purposes for which they are processed (Art. 5(1)(c)); further processing is compatible with the original purposes per the Art. 6(4) compatibility test (5 factors); special-category processing requires an Art. 9(2) basis subject to the Art. 9(1) prohibition; by-design and by-default minimisation is applied per Art. 25(1)/(2); a DPIA under Art. 35 is performed for high-risk processing.' considerations=['Verbatim operative-language match with CRA Annex I Part I (2)(g) — when a CRA-compliant product processes personal data at runtime, the same minimisation test applies on the same dataset and the stricter operational interpretation binds.', 'The GDPR Art. 6(4) compatibility test on change of purpose is the residual GDPR-only requirement not absorbed by CRA-side design-time minimisation; for an integrated manufacturer-controller, the Art. 6(4) assessment is documented separately from the CRA Annex I Part I (2)(g) design-time record.', 'The AI Act Art. 10(5) special-category bias-correction gateway is an additional narrow permission for high-risk AI providers (all 6 cumulative conditions (a)–(f) required); outside that window, GDPR Art. 9(1) prohibition binds and the AI Act gateway does not extend the controller-side processing basis.'] anchors=['Annex I Part I (2)', 'Art. 10(5)', 'Art. 25(1)', 'Art. 35', 'Art. 5(1)', 'Art. 6(4)', 'Art. 9(1)', 'Art. 9(2)'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-05.1.CRA' yaml_id='SO-D-05.1.CRA' regulation='CRA' subdomain_id='D-05.1' applies_to='[CRA]' inherits_from='SO-CRA-034' source_SR='SR-CRA-046' activation='if CRA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Data processed by a product with digital elements — personal or other — is limited to what is adequate, relevant, and necessary in relation to the intended purpose of the product (Art. 3(23) `intended purpose` definition), with the risk assessment per Art. 13(2) and the intended purpose + reasonably foreseeable use per Art. 13(3) sentence 2 supplying the proportionality calibration (Annex I Part I (2)(g)).' considerations=['Verbatim operative-language match with GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) — the literal "adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary" wording binds both regimes on the same dataset when a CRA-compliant product processes personal data at runtime.', 'CRA does NOT require the GDPR Art. 6(4) compatibility test on change of purpose; the residual GDPR-only requirement (change-of-purpose compatibility) is documented by the controller on the controller side, not absorbed into CRA Annex I Part I (2)(g).', "Data-class layering: CRA operates at runtime on the product's intended-purpose data; GDPR operates upstream on the data-subject collection decision; AI Act operates upstream on the training pipeline. The three data classes are layered, not collapsed."] anchors=['Annex I Part I (2)', 'Art. 13(2)', 'Art. 13(3)', 'Art. 3(23)', 'Art. 5(1)', 'Art. 6(4)'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-05.1.AI_Act' yaml_id='SO-D-05.1.AIACT' regulation='AI_Act' subdomain_id='D-05.1' applies_to='[AI_ACT]' inherits_from='SO-AI_Act-003, SO-AI_Act-004' source_SR='SR-AI_Act-003, SR-AI_Act-004, SR-AI_Act-005, SR-AI_Act-006' activation='if AI_ACT in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='High-risk AI systems which make use of techniques involving the training of AI models with data are developed on the basis of training, validation and testing data sets that meet the quality criteria — relevant, sufficiently representative, and to the best extent possible, free of errors and complete in view of the intended purpose (Art. 10(3)) — supported by data governance practices that detect, prevent and mitigate possible biases (Art. 10(1) + Art. 10(2) 8-element closed list (a)–(h)).' considerations=['The Art. 10(5) special-category exception is the single overlap point with GDPR Art. 9(1) in D-05.1; outside the narrow Art. 10(5) window (high-risk AI provider training a system with bias-detection needs that cannot be met by non-special-category data, all 6 cumulative conditions (a)–(f) satisfied), the AI Act does not trigger special-category processing and the GDPR ↔ AI_Act pair is scope-disjoint in baseline.', 'CRA-side coverage of training data quality is sequential not concurrent — CRA Annex I Part I (2)(g) operates at runtime on product data; AI Act Art. 10 operates upstream on the training pipeline; the two obligations compose into a 3-track matrix when training data flows into a CRA-classified runtime product.', '`biases` carries POLY ambiguity (statistical / algorithmic / societal); chosen reading is cumulative with all three senses in scope (per SR-AI_Act-004 ambiguity_notes); the 8-element closed list is AND-coordinated so partial compliance with six of eight does not satisfy Art. 10.'] anchors=['Annex I Part I (2)', 'Art. 10', 'Art. 10(1)', 'Art. 10(2)', 'Art. 10(3)', 'Art. 10(5)', 'Art. 9(1)'] csf=[]

layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-05.2 Retention & Archiving
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl: id='SO-D-05.2.HL' subdomain_id='D-05.2' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source=None verified_relationship_basis=None emergent_tensions=None objective='Data — across the data classes in scope — is retained for the period required to satisfy its declared purpose, with documented retention rationale and, where the underlying purpose changes, a reset of the retention clock. Long-term archiving or research-only retention is paired with safeguards proportional to the residual identifiability.' considerations=['Three participating regulations (GDPR, CRA, AI Act) each impose a retention/archiving duty on a distinct data class with a distinct obligation direction: GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) "no longer than is necessary" qualitative ceiling on personal data (controller-side, Art. 30(1)(f) RoPA time-limits + Art. 89(1) safeguards for the public-interest/research/statistical carve-out); CRA Art. 13(8) 5-year support period + Art. 13(9) 10-year update-availability tail + Art. 13(18) 10-year Annex II information accessibility on update artefacts (manufacturer-side, floor); AI Act Art. 19(1) ≥6-month floor on high-risk AI system logs (provider-side, "appropriate to the intended purpose" upward adjustment + GDPR escape clause).', 'CRDA-deep verified relationships: GDPR↔CRA = CORRECTED from CONTRADICTORY (direction) to SCOPE-DISJOINT (the CRDA reasoning itself concedes CRA\'s 10-year tail is on update availability, not personal-data retention; the pair is scope-disjoint in baseline with separation architecture as the layering rule when the CRA update log contains personal data); GDPR↔AI_Act = CORRECTED from CONTRADICTORY (direction) to COMPLEMENTARY (floor-within-ceiling — the AI Act ≥6-month floor is a subset of GDPR\'s "as long as necessary" envelope, with operative range [6 months, "necessary"]); layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl: id='SO-D-05.3.HL' subdomain_id='D-05.3' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source=None verified_relationship_basis=None emergent_tensions=None objective="Data held about a person is rendered inaccessible to the controller on the data subject's election, and data held by a product with digital elements is rendered inaccessible to the manufacturer on the user's election, by whichever mechanism — the controller-side policy execution or the manufacturer-side product affordance — applies to the data object. Erasure is performed without undue delay and is documented to demonstrate compliance; where a processor is involved, the processor-side mirror ensures deletion-or-return at contract end." considerations=['Two participating regulations (GDPR, CRA) stack on the same party in the personal-data subset: GDPR Art. 17(1) data-subject right (controller-bound, 6 grounds (a)–(f)) with Art. 17(2) confirmation + Art. 12 transparency + Art. 19 cascade (to D-04.3) + Art. 28(3)(g) processor-side mirror; CRA Annex I Part I (2)(m) first-limb terminal deletion + second-limb secure cross-product transfer (manufacturer-bound). CRDA-deep verified GDPR↔CRA = COMPLEMENTARY (SAME, layer-stacking pattern).', 'Deletion path converges on cryptographic-erasure or secure-overwrite (both compatible with SR-GDPR-030 + SR-CRA-048); evidence templates diverge (Art. 5(2) accountability + Art. 30 RoPA + Art. 17(2) confirmation + Art. 19 cascade vs Annex VII §2 technical documentation + Annex II §8(d) decommissioning instructions + Annex VII §6 test reports).', 'Art. 17(1) `without undue delay` and CRA `securely and easily` are both VAG (no quantitative clock); the controller-side service-level governs policy execution (typically monthly under EDPB practice, ≤2 months under Art. 12(3) for complex requests); the manufacturer-side affordance-depth governs architectural support (calibrated per Art. 13(2) risk assessment). The two clocks are not aligned by the high-level SO.', 'Art. 17(3) carve-outs (freedom of expression, legal obligation, public-interest public-health, archiving/research/statistical, establishment-exercise-defence of legal claims) are the layer-segregated exception structure: GDPR-side Art. 17(3) governs the controller; CRA-side (2)(m) governs the manufacturer; the two do NOT override each other.', 'For a 5-FTE SaaS with GDPR-only applicability, only the GDPR sub-SO activates; for a CRA-only manufacturer (no personal data), only the CRA sub-SO activates; for an integrated manufacturer-controller on a CRA-classified product, both sub-SOs stack on the same product event.'] anchors=['Annex I Part I (2)', 'Annex II', 'Annex VII', 'Art. 12', 'Art. 12(3)', 'Art. 13(2)', 'Art. 17(1)', 'Art. 17(2)', 'Art. 17(3)', 'Art. 19', 'Art. 28(3)', 'Art. 30', 'Art. 5(2)', '§2', '§6', '§8'] csf=[] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto  # activates when ≥2 applicable regs target overlapping erasure layers on the same party AND ≥1 sub-SO activates'
hso_per_reg: id='SO-D-05.3.GDPR' yaml_id='SO-D-05.3.GDPR' regulation='GDPR' subdomain_id='D-05.3' applies_to='[GDPR]' inherits_from='SO-GDPR-018, SO-GDPR-019' source_SR='SR-GDPR-030, SR-GDPR-031' activation='if GDPR in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective="Personal data are erased without undue delay on the data subject's Art. 17(1) request where one of the six Art. 17(1) grounds (a)–(f) applies: (a) no longer necessary for original purposes; (b) consent withdrawn (no other Art. 6(1) basis applies); (c) Art. 21(1) objection (no overriding compelling legitimate ground) or Art. 21(2) direct-marketing objection; (d) unlawful processing; (e) legal-obligation erasure; (f) information-society-service offers to a child (Art. 8(1)). On processor contract end, the processor deletes or returns all personal data and existing copies per Art. 28(3)(g)." considerations=["The CRA Annex I Part I (2)(m) affordance is the manufacturer-side architectural companion — when a CRA-classified product processes personal data, the controller-side Art. 17 path is executed through the manufacturer's deletion affordance; for an integrated manufacturer-controller, the controller's Art. 5(2) accountability evidence is discharged via the Annex VII technical documentation.", 'Art. 17(3) carve-outs (freedom of expression, legal obligation, public-interest public-health, archiving/research/statistical, establishment-exercise-defence of legal claims) do not relax the erasure duty beyond what they permit; the manufacturer-side CRA (2)(m) obligation is independent of the GDPR-side Art. 17(3) exceptions (the user retains the product-side removal affordance even when the controller-side obligation is lawfully suspended).', 'The Art. 19 cascade (rectification/erasure/restriction notification to recipients) is structurally in D-04.3 SO-GDPR-012 (notification, not erasure); the high-level SO surfaces the erasure itself, not the cascade.', 'The `deletes` polysemy in Art. 28(3)(g) is resolved to the cryptographic-erasure reading per SR-GDPR-030 (key destruction scales across backups/replicas without per-copy destruction; aligns with EDPB Guidelines 5/2020).'] anchors=['Annex I Part I (2)', 'Annex VII', 'Art. 17', 'Art. 17(1)', 'Art. 17(3)', 'Art. 19', 'Art. 21(1)', 'Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 28(3)', 'Art. 5(2)', 'Art. 6(1)', 'Art. 8(1)'] csf=[]

CRA `due diligence` procedural + substantive on third-party components as technical artefacts including non-commercial OSS (Art. 13(5)/(6) + Art. 3(48) FOSS); DORA Art. 28(1) four-factor proportionality on ICT third-party service providers with Art. 28(5) CIF escalator.', 'CRDA-deep verified relationships (6 pairs, all SAME — 2 COMPLEMENTARY + 3 DIFFERENT-PERSPECTIVE + 1 EQUAL; GDPR↔DORA = COMPLEMENTARY (DORA exceeds GDPR — four-factor operationalises `sufficient guarantees` with sharper factors, GDPR-specific Art. 28(3) DPA clauses appended on controller side); NIS2↔CRA = DIFFERENT-PERSPECTIVE (entity-level supplier vs product-level component); typically scope-disjoint in baseline).', 'Implementation guidance: the four target objects are layered not collapsed — processor as legal entity (GDPR), direct supplier as relationship (NIS 2), third-party component as technical artefact (CRA), ICT third-party service provider as financial-entity counterparty (DORA). A unified vendor-risk-assessment platform may serve the technical substrate but policy and evidence layers must remain target-object-segregated.', "Scope caveats: entity-level vs product-level distinction (CRA is upstream — manufacturer's inputs; DORA is midstream — deployer's ICT providers; GDPR/NIS 2 are downstream — deployer's own supplier due diligence); DORA four-factor exceeds both GDPR `sufficient guarantees` and NIS 2 `appropriate and proportionate`; CRA Art. 3(48) FOSS inclusion is the CRA-specific operational handle that GDPR/NIS 2/DORA do not separately replicate; NIS 2 supplier-assessment three-prong is more granular than the GDPR `sufficient guarantees` test and the CRA `due diligence` test."] anchors=['Art. 13(5)', 'Art. 21(1)', 'Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 21(3)', 'Art. 28(1)', 'Art. 28(3)', 'Art. 28(5)', 'Art. 3(48)', 'Art. 4(7)'] csf=[] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto  # activates when ≥2 applicable regs have ≥1 pair with Y/Conditional scope overlap on the same party AND ≥1 sub-SO activates; for D-06.1 all 6 pairs have Y or Conditional Y scope overlap, so once ≥2 regs are applicable the high-level SO engages'
hso_per_reg: id='SO-D-06.1.GDPR' yaml_id='SO-D-06.1.GDPR' regulation='GDPR' subdomain_id='D-06.1' applies_to='[GDPR]' inherits_from='SO-GDPR-021' source_SR='SR-GDPR-033' activation='if GDPR in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='The controller engages only processors providing sufficient guarantees to implement appropriate technical and organisational measures in such a manner that processing meets the requirements of GDPR and protects data-subject rights (Art. 28(1)); the Art. 28(3) DPA closed-list clauses (a)–(h) are documented and the sub-processor authorisation chain (Art. 28(2)) is material to the due diligence.' considerations=['The EDPB Guidelines 07/2020 4-factor reading (knowledge + reliability of resources + compliance track-record + financial stability) operationalises the `sufficient guarantees` qualitative threshold.', "On an integrated-stack manufacturer-controller-deployer, the controller-side GDPR due diligence on the manufacturer-as-processor layers vertically with the manufacturer's own CRA Art. 13(5) third-party component due diligence — the controller is still owed the Art. 28(1) due diligence on the manufacturer as the data-processing counterparty, even where the manufacturer has self-certified the product.", "DORA's Art. 28(1) four-factor proportionality operationalises GDPR `sufficient guarantees` with sharper factors; a financial entity subject to DORA Art. 28 satisfies GDPR Art. 28(1) via the proportionality documentation but must explicitly document the GDPR-specific processor guarantees (Art. 28(3)(a) instruction-bound processing, Art. 28(3)(h) audit, Art. 28(2) sub-processor authorisation, Art. 28(3)(b) confidentiality, Art. 28(3)(e) data-subject-rights assistance, Art. 28(3)(f) Art. 33/34 incident-assistance, Art. 28(3)(g) deletion-or-return)."] anchors=['Art. 13(5)', 'Art. 28', 'Art. 28(1)', 'Art. 28(2)', 'Art. 28(3)', 'Art. 33'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-06.1.NIS2' yaml_id='SO-D-06.1.NIS2' regulation='NIS2' subdomain_id='D-06.1' applies_to='[NIS2]' inherits_from='SO-NIS2-014' source_SR='SR-NIS2-020' activation='if NIS2 in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Essential and important entities take appropriate and proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures across direct supplier and service-provider relationships, including security-related aspects of those relationships (Art. 21(2)(d)), taking into account state of the art (Art. 21(1) sentence 2) and the risks posed to the security of network and information systems; the Art. 21(3) sentence 1 three-prong supplier assessment (supplier-specific vulnerabilities + overall quality of products and cybersecurity practices + supplier secure-development procedures) is performed per direct supplier, with EU-level coordinated risk-propagation inputs (Art. 21(3) sentence 2 → Art. 22) taken into account where available.' considerations=['The `direct` scope-limiter is POLY-S3 with three materially distinct readings per SR-NIS2-020: R1 (Tier-1 strict), R2 (Tier-1 + technically integrated), R3 (Tier-1 + operationally dependent). Chosen reading is R2 (risk-management-precaution principle — technical integration is the primary attack-surface handle on supply-chain risk).', "DORA Art. 28(1) four-factor proportionality operationalises the NIS 2 `appropriate and proportionate` chapeau with explicit factors in the financial-services subset; a financial entity implementing DORA exceeds NIS 2's supply-chain-security requirement.", 'NIS 2 ↔ CRA = DIFFERENT-PERSPECTIVE: entity-level supplier (NIS 2) vs product-level component (CRA); the lists overlap when the deployer is the entity AND the manufacturer supplies a CRA-compliant product — the deployer does NIS 2-level supplier due diligence on the manufacturer (entity-to-entity), while the manufacturer does CRA-level component due diligence on its third-party components (product-internal).'] anchors=['Art. 21(1)', 'Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 21(3)', 'Art. 22', 'Art. 28(1)'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-06.1.CRA' yaml_id='SO-D-06.1.CRA' regulation='CRA' subdomain_id='D-06.1' applies_to='[CRA]' inherits_from='SO-CRA-037' source_SR='SR-CRA-050' activation='if CRA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='The manufacturer exercises due diligence when integrating components sourced from third parties — including components of free and open-source software not made available on the market in the course of a commercial activity (Art. 3(48) FOSS definition) — so that those components do not compromise the cybersecurity of the product with digital elements (Art. 13(5) sentence 1); on becoming aware of a component vulnerability (Art. 13(6) sentence 1), the manufacturer addresses and remediates it without delay and shares relevant information with the component supplier (Art. 13(6) sentence 2).' considerations=['The `due diligence` POLY-S3 is resolved to R3 (procedural + substantive) per Annex VII §2 conformity-assessment evidentiary requirements (both documented vetting process and positive verification of security posture).', 'The Art. 3(48) FOSS inclusion is the CRA-specific operational handle that GDPR / NIS 2 / DORA do not separately replicate; non-commercial OSS components are in scope where the OSS becomes a component of the product with digital elements placed on the Union market.', "CRA ↔ DORA = DIFFERENT-PERSPECTIVE (typically scope-disjoint in baseline): CRA is upstream (manufacturer's inputs), DORA is midstream (deployer's ICT providers); the manufacturer and the financial entity are typically different parties.", 'GDPR ↔ CRA = DIFFERENT-PERSPECTIVE: GDPR processor due diligence is on the entity; CRA third-party component due diligence is on the components; the two layers stack vertically on the integrated manufacturer-controller-deployer.'] anchors=['Annex VII', 'Art. 13(5)', 'Art. 13(6)', 'Art. 3(48)', '§2'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-06.1.DORA' yaml_id='SO-D-06.1.DORA' regulation='DORA' subdomain_id='D-06.1' applies_to='[DORA]' inherits_from='SO-DORA-011' source_SR='SR-DORA-019' activation='if DORA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Financial entities manage ICT third-party risk taking into account four-factor proportionality — nature, scale, complexity and importance of ICT-related dependencies (Art. 28(1) four-way AND) — and the risks arising from contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services; the Art. 28(5) CIF escalator ("most up-to-date and highest quality information security standards") applies to contractual arrangements concerning critical or important functions.' considerations=['The Art. 28(5) `appropriate information security standards` POLY-S3 is resolved by SR-DORA-020 to R1 (entity-selected) with R2 (supervisory-recognised) as the EU-acceptable floor.', "DORA's four-factor operationalises GDPR `sufficient guarantees` and NIS 2 `appropriate and proportionate` chapeau with sharper factors — a financial entity implementing DORA Art. 28(1) discharges GDPR Art. 28(1) in the financial-services subset (with GDPR-specific Art. 28(3) DPA clauses appended on controller side where the ICT provider is also a processor) and exceeds NIS 2's supply-chain-security requirement.", 'The `critical or important functions` POLY-S2 ambiguity (no OJ definition; 18 of 38 clauses use the term) propagates through D-06.3 + D-06.4; chosen reading is the EBA/ESMA/EIOPA RTS-supplied definition (the regulator-level RTS on critical or important functions per Art. 28(13)).'] anchors=['Art. 28(1)', 'Art. 28(13)', 'Art. 28(3)', 'Art. 28(5)'] csf=[]

layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl: id='SO-D-06.2.HL' subdomain_id='D-06.2' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source='../../CrossRegulation/DeepAnalysis/D-06_Supply-Chain/D-06.2.md §D-06.2' verified_relationship_basis='CRDA-deep verified (0 pairs — single-participant sub-domain; CRA is the SOLE AUTHORITY for D-06.2 per AEGIS taxonomy §4.1; GDPR, NIS 2, DORA, AI Act are all out-of-scope; the Annex I Part II (1) SBOM authoring duty + Annex VII §2(b) technical-documentation retention + Annex VII §8 MSA reasoned-request disclosure + Annex II §9 optional user access + Art. 13(24) Commission implementing acts compose the three-anchored SBOM architecture — authoring, retention, regulatory disclosure; the high-level SO describes the common SBOM duty — the manufacturer draws up and maintains an SBOM in a commonly used and machine-readable format covering at least the top-level dependencies, with format flexibility (POLY-S3 R3 reading per SR-CRA-008 pending Commission implementing acts under Art. 13(24)) and `where necessary` MSA-disclosure scope (POLY-S2 R1 reading per SR-CRA-053); no CORRECTED, no SCOPE-DISJOINT, no CONTRADICTORY classifications by construction (single regulator))' emergent_tensions=0 objective='The manufacturer draws up and maintains a software bill of materials (SBOM) covering the components and dependencies contained in the product with digital elements, in a commonly used and machine-readable format that supports automated downstream consumption, with at minimum the top-level dependencies.' considerations=['Only 1 regulator participates (CRA is the SOLE AUTHORITY per AEGIS taxonomy §4.1); GDPR, NIS 2, DORA, AI Act are all out-of-scope. The high-level SO and the CRA sub-SO describe the same obligation at different abstraction levels, and the activation model treats the high-level SO as redundant in this single-regulator case but still emits it for traceability.', 'The format-floor POLY-S3 is resolved to R3 (any commonly-used machine-readable format that supports automated component identification, pending the Commission implementing acts under Art. 13(24)); the depth-floor POLY-S2 is resolved to R1 (first-level direct dependencies with depth-1 look-through, per SR-CRA-052); the `where necessary` MSA-disclosure scope POLY-S2 is resolved to R1 per SR-CRA-053 (necessary subset directly relevant to the compliance question).', 'The soft-touch cross-pollination with SR-GDPR-032 `commonly used` ambiguity in Art. 15(3) is a format-selection-layer architectural support — the CRA-side SBOM format choice and the controller-side GDPR Art. 15(3) portability format choice may share infrastructure (e.g. a single data-catalog machinery) but the two obligations are not the same and the GDPR obligation is data-subject-right-bound while the CRA obligation is manufacturer-side-bound.'] anchors=['Art. 13(24)', 'Art. 15(3)', '§4'] csf=[] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto'

id='SO-D-06.2.CRA' yaml_id='SO-D-06.2.CRA' regulation='CRA' subdomain_id='D-06.2' applies_to='[CRA]' inherits_from='SO-CRA-038' source_SR='SR-CRA-008, SR-CRA-052, SR-CRA-053' activation='if CRA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective="The manufacturer draws up and maintains an SBOM covering the components and dependencies contained in the product with digital elements in a commonly used and machine-readable format that includes, at minimum, the top-level dependencies (Annex I Part II (1)).

**CSF anchors (from `SR-CRA-008` + `SR-CRA-052` + `SR-CRA-053`
v0.3 security_rationale):**
ID.AM-02, GV.SC-02, GV.SC-03.
*(`SR-CRA-008` covers the Annex I Part II (1) SBOM format
operationalised in NIST CSF 2.0 through **ID.AM-02 (inventories of
software platforms and applications maintained)** and **GV.SC-02
(suppliers and other third parties known, prioritised, and assessed
using a cybersecurity supply-chain risk-management process)**.
ID.AM-02 captures the format-side leg — the inventory must be
queryable and automatable; a `commonly used and machine-readable
format` is the structural requirement that turns the SBOM from a
static artefact into an input to vulnerability-management
automation, CVE matching, and downstream supply-chain risk
assessment. GV.SC-02 anchors the supply-chain dimension — the
format must encode supplier and supply-chain relationships (per the
Art. 3(39) definition), so that the SBOM supports both
vulnerability lookup and supplier-prioritisation under the broader
cybersecurity supply-chain risk-management process. `SR-CRA-052`
covers the Annex I Part II (1) top-level-dependencies floor
operationalised through **ID.AM-02** — the SBOM is the most specific
operational expression of the software-inventory principle in the
product-side cybersecurity domain, with the machine-readable format
qualifier supplying the queryable interface that defenders use to
correlate upstream CVEs against the product's dependency surface.
`SR-CRA-053` covers the Annex VII §2(b) + Annex II §9 + Annex VII
§8 retention-and-disclosure architecture operationalised through
**ID.AM-02 + GV.SC-03 (contracts with suppliers and other third
parties used to implement appropriate measures designed to meet
the objectives of an organisation's cybersecurity programme and the
Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management Plan)**. GV.SC-03
captures the user-facing dimension and the supply-chain
coordination — the Annex II §9 user-facing SBOM access is the
contractual-equivalent transparency lever for voluntary disclosure,
and the SBOM-internal record is the contractual coordination point
with downstream integrators who depend on the SBOM for their own
SR-CRA-050 due-diligence work. Together the three subcategories
enable the manufacturer to demonstrate ex post, through the
documented SBOM in the technical documentation under Annex VII
§2(b), the versioning record, the MSA-request response log under
Annex VII §8, and the optional Annex II §9 user-access record,
that the Annex I Part II (1) SBOM duty has been discharged across
the support period and through the 10-year tail.)*" considerations=[] anchors=['Annex I Part II (1)', 'Annex II', 'Annex VII', 'Art. 3(39)', '§2', '§8', '§9'] csf=['GV.SC-02', 'GV.SC-03', 'ID.AM-02']

layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-06.3 Contractual Security Obligations
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl: id='SO-D-06.3.HL' subdomain_id='D-06.3' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source=None verified_relationship_basis=None emergent_tensions=None objective='Third-party security obligations are made enforceable through contracts, transfer safeguards, written mandates, or market-access duties, as appropriate to the regulatory perspective and the actor involved.' considerations=['Four participating regulations (GDPR, NIS 2, CRA, DORA) each use a distinct legal instrument: GDPR uses processor contracts and transfer safeguards; NIS 2 uses direct-supplier contractual security and a supplier-assessment evidence chain; CRA uses importer/distributor market-access duties and component-vulnerability escalation; DORA uses ICT third-party written contractual arrangements, Art. 28(5) standards compliance, and CIF-specific audit/exit clauses where applicable.', 'CRDA-deep verified relationships (6 pairs: 5 SAME + 1 CORRECTED — GDPR↔DORA from CRDA CONTRADICTORY to COMPLEMENTARY because both clause sets add rather than conflict; the operative rule is clause-list union when the same contract is in scope). No verified CONTRADICTORY pairs.', 'Where the same real-world supplier relationship is covered by multiple regulations, the organisation implements a consolidated contractual-security matrix that preserves all applicable mandatory clauses and evidence recipients; the high-level SO does not collapse the regimes into one generic supplier contract — it preserves the per-reg target object, trigger, actor, evidence template, and recipient.', 'The 1 conditional emergent tension (4-track contract architecture — GDPR 8 DPA elements + DORA 9 ICT-contract elements + NIS 2 supplier-assessment + CRA importer/distributor market-access duties) is regulated by preserving the multi-track matrix rather than choosing a single stricter regime.'] anchors=['Art. 28(5)'] csf=[] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto'
hso_per_reg: id='SO-D-06.3.GDPR' yaml_id='SO-D-06.3.GDPR' regulation='GDPR' subdomain_id='D-06.3' applies_to='[GDPR]' inherits_from='[SO-GDPR-022, SO-GDPR-033, SO-GDPR-035]' source_SR='[SR-GDPR-034, SR-GDPR-035, SR-GDPR-036, SR-GDPR-037, SR-GDPR-056, SR-GDPR-059]' activation='if GDPR in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Controller/processor contracts and related transfer instruments include the GDPR-specific contractual security obligations required for personal-data processing: the Art. 28(3)(a)–(h) eight-element DPA floor, sub-processor authorisation and change-notification, processor Art. 32 security-measure commitments, audit/inspection access, and contract-end return/deletion; the Art. 46 appropriate-safeguards mechanism and the Art. 48 international-agreement filter apply where personal data leaves the EEA or is exposed to third-country legal-process pressure.' considerations=['In overlap with DORA, the GDPR layer is additive: the DORA Art. 30(2) list does not remove instruction-bound processing (Art. 28(3)(a)), Art. 28(2) sub-processor authorisation, Art. 28(3)(h) audit contribution, or Chapter V transfer controls.', 'The CRA importer/distributor economic-operator duties are market-surveillance-facing, not DPA-style negotiated contracts; the two regimes do not duplicate on the same instrument.'] anchors=['Art. 28(2)', 'Art. 28(3)', 'Art. 30(2)', 'Art. 32', 'Art. 46', 'Art. 48'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-06.3.NIS2' yaml_id='SO-D-06.3.NIS2' regulation='NIS2' subdomain_id='D-06.3' applies_to='[NIS2]' inherits_from='[SO-NIS2-015, SO-NIS2-016]' source_SR='[SR-NIS2-020, SR-NIS2-021, SR-NIS2-022, SR-NIS2-023, SR-NIS2-024, SR-NIS2-025]' activation='if NIS2 in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Essential and important entities manage contractual security for direct supplier and service-provider relationships by documenting the supplier universe under the `direct` scope-limiter, embedding security-related contractual aspects into supplier relationships, and assessing each direct supplier against the Art. 21(3) three-prong supplier-assessment structure (supplier-specific vulnerabilities + overall quality of products/services and cybersecurity practices + supplier secure-development procedures); Art. 22 coordinated supply-chain risk assessments are taken into account where available.' considerations=["In overlap with DORA, DORA's Art. 30 contract list may satisfy the NIS 2 open-textured contractual-security floor for financial entities, but the NIS 2 `direct` scope-limiter and Member-State-transposition evidence remain separate operational handles.", 'CRA component-vulnerability reporting under Art. 13(6) provides the post-contract upstream feedback path (the NIS2↔CRA lifecycle hinge); CRA does not convert into a DPA-style contract.'] anchors=['Art. 13(6)', 'Art. 21(3)', 'Art. 22', 'Art. 30'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-06.3.CRA' yaml_id='SO-D-06.3.CRA' regulation='CRA' subdomain_id='D-06.3' applies_to='[CRA]' inherits_from='[SO-CRA-039, SO-CRA-040]' source_SR='[SR-CRA-051, SR-CRA-054, SR-CRA-055, SR-CRA-057, SR-CRA-058]' activation='if CRA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='CRA contractual-security coverage is expressed through economic-operator duties rather than a single negotiated contract: importers place products with digital elements on the Union market only after verifying conformity assessment, technical documentation, CE marking, and manufacturer identification, and escalate significant risk or vulnerabilities to the manufacturer and MSA while taking corrective measures; distributors act with due care, verify CE marking and required documentation, confirm manufacturer/importer compliance, and escalate non-conformity or vulnerabilities.' considerations=['Component-vulnerability reporting under Art. 13(6) is the post-contract upstream feedback path that connects CRA-side escalation with the NIS 2 supplier-security assessment (the NIS2↔CRA lifecycle hinge).', 'The CRA layer is regulatory and market-surveillance-facing; it does not become a GDPR-style DPA or a DORA ICT-service contract.'] anchors=['Art. 13(6)'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-06.3.DORA' yaml_id='SO-D-06.3.DORA' regulation='DORA' subdomain_id='D-06.3' applies_to='[DORA]' inherits_from='[SO-DORA-011, SO-DORA-012]' source_SR='[SR-DORA-019, SR-DORA-020, SR-DORA-021, SR-DORA-022]' activation='if DORA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Financial entities structure ICT third-party contractual arrangements so that rights and obligations are clearly allocated and set out in writing, the Art. 30(2)(a)–(i) minimum elements are present, Art. 28(5) information-security standards are contractually evidenced, and contractual arrangements supporting critical or important functions include the additional CIF clauses required under Art. 30(3) (including unrestricted access/inspection/audit rights where applicable).' considerations=['In overlap with GDPR, the contract must contain the union of GDPR Art. 28(3) and DORA Art. 30 clauses; DORA does not erase the GDPR-specific data-processing terms (the CORRECTED CRDA pair from CONTRADICTORY to COMPLEMENTARY is resolved as clause-list union).', 'In overlap with NIS 2, DORA operationalises the NIS 2 open-textured supplier-contract requirement for financial entities, while NIS 2 remains the floor outside that subset.', 'CRA importer/distributor economic-operator duties and DORA ICT-service contracts operate at different supply-chain layers (market-access vs ICT service); the two obligations compose when a CRA-classified product is procured by a financial entity through importer/distributor channels.'] anchors=['Art. 28(3)', 'Art. 28(5)', 'Art. 30', 'Art. 30(2)', 'Art. 30(3)'] csf=[]

layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-06.4 Third-Party Boundary Management
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl: id='SO-D-06.4.HL' subdomain_id='D-06.4' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source=None verified_relationship_basis=None emergent_tensions=None objective='Third-party boundary responsibilities are explicitly allocated so that non-EU representatives, direct-supplier scope, cross-border routing, substantial-modification accountability, economic-operator identification, and audit/access rights remain traceable to the correct actor and recipient.' considerations=['Four participating regulations (GDPR, NIS 2, CRA, DORA) anchor different mechanisms: GDPR anchors non-EU personal-data actors through a written Union representative; NIS 2 anchors entity-level supplier boundaries and cross-MS notification routing; CRA anchors product-compliance accountability through authorised representatives, manufacturer-equivalent triggers, third-party substantial-modification rules, and 10-year economic-operator traceability; DORA anchors financial-entity and competent-authority access, inspection, and audit rights over critical ICT third-party providers.', 'CRDA-deep verified relationships (6 pairs, all SAME: 2 COMPLEMENTARY + 1 EQUAL with different objects + 3 DIFFERENT-PERSPECTIVE; no CORRECTED, no CONTRADICTORY).', 'The high-level SO does not collapse these mechanisms — it builds a boundary matrix showing which representative, route, traceability record, or audit right applies in each factual scenario.', 'The 1 conditional emergent tension (four-party boundary architecture — GDPR representative + CRA authorised representative + NIS 2 cross-MS routing + DORA CIF audit rights at the same time on a non-EU provider) is regulated by role-and-recipient allocation rather than by collapsing boundary mechanisms.'] anchors=[] csf=[] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto'
hso_per_reg: id='SO-D-06.4.GDPR' yaml_id='SO-D-06.4.GDPR' regulation='GDPR' subdomain_id='D-06.4' applies_to='[GDPR]' inherits_from='SO-GDPR-023' source_SR='SR-GDPR-038' activation='if GDPR in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Non-EU controllers and processors falling under GDPR Art. 3(2) designate a representative in writing in the Union unless the Art. 27(2) exception applies; the representative is the legal-address and accountability anchor for supervisory-authority and data-subject contact.' considerations=['In overlap with CRA, the GDPR representative does not replace the CRA authorised representative — one handles data-protection correspondence and one handles product-compliance technical-documentation/MSA cooperation; a single legal entity may perform both roles only if both mandates and recipient channels are separately documented.', "In overlap with DORA, GDPR's representative address coexists with DORA contractual audit rights where the non-EU ICT provider supports critical or important functions for a financial entity."] anchors=['Art. 27(2)', 'Art. 3(2)'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-06.4.NIS2' yaml_id='SO-D-06.4.NIS2' regulation='NIS2' subdomain_id='D-06.4' applies_to='[NIS2]' inherits_from='[SO-NIS2-012, SO-NIS2-014, SO-NIS2-016]' source_SR='[SR-NIS2-018, SR-NIS2-020, SR-NIS2-025]' activation='if NIS2 in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective="NIS 2 boundary management is split across cross-border notification routing and entity-side supplier-scope control: for incidents affecting two or more Member States, CSIRTs, competent authorities, and SPOCs route information to other affected Member States and ENISA; for supply-chain boundaries, the Art. 21(2)(d) `direct` supplier/service-provider scope-limiter defines which third parties sit inside the entity's NIS 2 supplier-security perimeter, and Art. 22 coordinated supply-chain risk-assessment outputs feed into supplier decisions where available." considerations=["In overlap with DORA, DORA audit rights add a deeper CIF-provider verification layer; they do not erase NIS 2's direct-supplier scope record.", 'In overlap with CRA, NIS 2 `direct` supplier scope determines who the entity is liable for; CRA Art. 22/23 determines who becomes the manufacturer after substantial modification and who must identify upstream/downstream economic operators — the two regimes operate at different boundaries.'] anchors=['Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 22'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-06.4.CRA' yaml_id='SO-D-06.4.CRA' regulation='CRA' subdomain_id='D-06.4' applies_to='[CRA]' inherits_from='[SO-CRA-041, SO-CRA-042, SO-CRA-043, SO-CRA-044]' source_SR='[SR-CRA-059, SR-CRA-060, SR-CRA-061, SR-CRA-062, SR-CRA-063]' activation='if CRA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective="CRA third-party boundary management preserves product-compliance accountability across EU/non-EU and supply-chain actor boundaries: a non-EU manufacturer may appoint an authorised representative by written mandate, but core manufacturer obligations remain non-delegable; an importer or distributor that places a product under its own name/trademark or substantially modifies it becomes manufacturer-equivalent; a third party that substantially modifies a product becomes the manufacturer for the affected part (or the entire product if the modification affects the whole product's cybersecurity); economic operators maintain upstream/downstream identification records and provide them to MSAs on reasoned request, retaining the supply-chain information for 10 years." considerations=['In overlap with GDPR, the CRA authorised representative does not replace the GDPR Union representative — the two mandates differ (data-protection correspondence vs product-compliance technical-documentation/MSA cooperation) and must be documented separately.', 'In overlap with DORA, economic-operator identification and DORA CIF audit rights point in different directions but compose where a CRA-classified product is supplied to a financial entity through an economic-operator chain.'] anchors=[] csf=[]

id='SO-D-06.4.DORA' yaml_id='SO-D-06.4.DORA' regulation='DORA' subdomain_id='D-06.4' applies_to='[DORA]' inherits_from='SO-DORA-012' source_SR='SR-DORA-022' activation='if DORA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective="Contractual arrangements concerning critical or important functions grant the financial entity, an appointed third party, and the competent authority unrestricted rights of access, inspection, and audit over the ICT third-party service provider, including on-site copying of relevant documentation where critical to provider operations; those rights must not be impeded or limited by other contractual arrangements or implementation policies, and alternative assurance levels may be agreed only where other clients' rights are affected." considerations=['In overlap with NIS 2, the DORA CIF audit-rights layer exceeds the NIS 2 direct-supplier floor for financial entities; it extends into critical ICT third-party providers beyond direct providers through the critical provider chain.', 'In overlap with CRA, DORA CIF audit rights coexist with CRA economic-operator identification rather than replacing it.'] anchors=[] csf=[]

layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-07.1 Secure-by-Design Principles
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl: id='SO-D-07.1.HL' subdomain_id='D-07.1' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source=None verified_relationship_basis=None emergent_tensions=None objective='Security is integrated into the acquisition, design, development, production, deployment and maintenance of systems and products via documented by-design decisions, risk-assessment propagation, proportionate safeguards, and lifecycle consistency.' considerations=["All five participating regulations (GDPR, NIS 2, CRA, DORA, AI Act) impose a secure-by-design duty at distinct target objects with distinct anchors: GDPR Art. 25(1) privacy-by-design with state-of-the-art + 4-factor qualitative proportionality + Art. 25(2) by-default limits on the controller's means-determination; NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(e) entity-level lifecycle discipline across acquisition, development, and maintenance with `appropriate and proportionate` chapeau + state-of-the-art floor; CRA Art. 13(1) + Art. 13(2) product-level by-design with risk-assessment propagation across 6 lifecycle phases per Annex I Part I; DORA Art. 9(4)(b) + Art. 9(4)(f) network-and-infrastructure management + patch policies — secure-by-design is implicit, not an OJ-mandate standalone, operationalised through Art. 9(4)(e) change-management six-step + Art. 24 testing programme; AI Act Art. 15(1) + Art. 17(1)(c) high-risk AI system accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity with lifecycle consistency + QMS design/design-control/design-verification.", 'Each regulator anchors by-design with a distinct qualitative threshold and proportionality qualifier (GDPR `state of the art` + cost + nature/scope/context/purposes/risks; NIS 2 `appropriate and proportionate` + state-of-the-art; CRA `essential cybersecurity requirements` + 6-phase risk-assessment propagation; DORA `appropriate techniques, methods and protocols` + `controlled manner` + risk-assessment-approach; AI Act `appropriate level` + `perform consistently throughout their lifecycle` + QMS-documented).', '10 pairwise cells are verified by CRDA-deep as 10 SAME — COMPLEMENTARY (no CORRECTED, no CONTRADICTORY, no SCOPE-DISJOINT in baseline): each regulator targets a distinct target object at a distinct trigger, and they stack on a typical entity that is both controller + NSIE + CRA manufacturer + DORA financial entity + AI Act provider/deployer.', 'The high-level SO engages if and only if ≥2 applicable regulations have Y scope overlap on the same party. For a 5-FTE SaaS startup with GDPR + CRA only, the high-level SO engages on the integrated manufacturer-controller-deployer stack. For a NIS 2 essential entity that is not a financial entity and does not manufacture CRA-classified products, only the applicable sub-SOs activate on the GDPR↔NIS2 COMPLEMENTARY pair.', 'The DORA dedicated-by-design absence is the operative structural feature: for a DORA-only entity that is not a CRA manufacturer and does not process personal data via high-risk AI, D-07.1 by-design compliance is demonstrated through the change-management six-step + testing programme outputs, with no standalone OJ-mandated by-design obligation. The OJ-literal absence of a DORA by-design clause is preserved as a structural Layer 2 review item (not a CONTRADICTORY/CORRECTED reclassification).', 'NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(e) operates across 3 coordinated phases (acquisition, development, maintenance); CRA Art. 13(2) operates across 6 phases (planning, design, development, production, delivery, maintenance) — the two are not 1:1 aligned but stack at the supplier-customer boundary.', 'AI Act Art. 15(4)–(5) AI-specific attack categories (data/model poisoning + adversarial examples + model evasion + confidentiality attacks + model flaws) do not substitute for CRA Annex I Part I (2)(j) attack-surface limitation or (2)(k) exploitation-mitigation outcomes; the two stack on AI-enabled CRA products with no OJ-level consolidation rule for attack defence.', 'The `state of the art` anchor is duplicated across the five regulations but interpreted independently; entities implementing all 5 must reconcile through documented decision records.', 'AI Act Recital 78 preserves GDPR, so the two obligations stack with the GDPR personal-data overlay on top of the AI Act AI-system property baseline.', 'The per-regulation perspective (target object, trigger, anchor, threshold, evidence template, recipient, legal anchor) is preserved verbatim in the five sub-SOs; the high-level SO does NOT collapse the five target objects, triggers, anchors, thresholds, evidence templates, or recipients into a single by-design architecture.'] anchors=['Annex I Part I', 'Annex I Part I (2)', 'Art. 13(1)', 'Art. 13(2)', 'Art. 15(1)', 'Art. 15(4)', 'Art. 17(1)', 'Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 24', 'Art. 25(1)', 'Art. 25(2)', 'Art. 9(4)'] csf=[] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto  # activates when ≥2 applicable regs have ≥1 pair with Y scope overlap on the same party AND ≥1 sub-SO activates; for D-07.1 all 10 pairs have Y scope overlap on a single party at the same event, so once ≥2 regs are applicable the high-level SO engages'
hso_per_reg: id='SO-D-07.1.GDPR' yaml_id='SO-D-07.1.GDPR' regulation='GDPR' subdomain_id='D-07.1' applies_to='[GDPR]' inherits_from='SO-GDPR-024' source_SR='SR-GDPR-039' activation='if GDPR in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='The controller implements appropriate technical and organisational measures — such as pseudonymisation — which are designed to implement data-protection principles, such as data minimisation, in an effective manner and to integrate the necessary safeguards into the processing (Art. 25(1) GDPR), and ensures that by default only personal data which are necessary for each specific purpose are processed (Art. 25(2) GDPR).' considerations=['The design anchor is 4-factor qualitative proportionality: state of the art, cost of implementation, nature/scope/context/purposes of processing, and risks of varying likelihood and severity (Art. 25(1)).', 'The by-default leg (Art. 25(2)) covers amount of data collected, extent of processing, period of storage, and accessibility — implies by-default minimal-data-collection pipelines, minimal-access, minimal-storage periods, and minimal-scope-of-processing.', 'The by-design + by-default pair forms a 2-tier architecture: by-design is the architectural decision record; by-default is the operational implementation. Decisions are documented in a necessity assessment often via DPIA (Art. 35(7)) and demonstrated to the supervisory authority (DPA) under Art. 5(2) accountability.', 'For an integrated manufacturer-controller-deployer, CRA-side Annex I Part I product-cybersecurity by-design discharges the engineering substrate (the manufacturer has done CRA Art. 13(1) product by-design) while GDPR Art. 25(1) data-protection by-design discharges the personal-data overlay — the two stack vertically on the same product-lifecycle with distinct design outputs.', 'The pseudonymisation + minimisation + by-default triad propagates downstream to D-07.2 (Secure Coding Practices) as the code-level instruction and D-07.3 (CI/CD Pipeline Security) as the delivery-path instruction.'] anchors=['Annex I Part I', 'Art. 13(1)', 'Art. 25(1)', 'Art. 25(2)', 'Art. 35(7)', 'Art. 5(2)'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-07.1.NIS2' yaml_id='SO-D-07.1.NIS2' regulation='NIS2' subdomain_id='D-07.1' applies_to='[NIS2]' inherits_from='SO-NIS2-017' source_SR='SR-NIS2-026' activation='if NIS2 in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Essential and important entities take appropriate and proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures to ensure security in acquisition, development and maintenance of network and information systems, including vulnerability handling and disclosure (Art. 21(2)(e) NIS 2).' considerations=['The 3-phase coordinated lifecycle (acquisition, development, maintenance) is operationalised through: (1) acquisition-phase supplier SDLC assessment (per SR-NIS2-026 on the basis of Art. 21(3) sentence 1 supplier-secure-development-procedures three-prong); (2) development-phase in-house secure-by-design decisions (per SR-NIS2-027); (3) maintenance-phase vulnerability handling+disclosure + patch-management + change-management (per SR-NIS2-028).', 'Art. 21(1) chapeau `appropriate and proportionate` is read with Art. 21(1) sentence 2 state-of-the-art floor + Recital 56 cost-of-implementation qualifier + Member-State-transposition-supplied proportionality calibration.', 'Art. 20(1) management-body approval+oversight+liability leg (cross to D-09.1) is the upstream governance instrument.', 'For an integrated controller-NSIE, NIS 2 acquisition-phase security (supplier SDLC assessment per SR-NIS2-026) realises GDPR Art. 25(1) controller-side by-design outputs (pseudonymised-by-default pipelines, minimisation-by-default); NIS 2 development-phase security (in-house secure-by-design decisions per SR-NIS2-027) implements the by-design outputs in code (D-07.2), CI/CD (D-07.3), and change-management (D-07.4).', 'The 3-phase NIS 2 lifecycle has a 6-phase CRA lifecycle mapping: CRA covers planning/design/development/production/delivery/maintenance; NIS 2 covers acquisition/development/maintenance (NIS 2 acquisition covers the supplier-side SDLC equivalent of CRA planning + design + development + production).'] anchors=['Art. 20(1)', 'Art. 21(1)', 'Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 21(3)', 'Art. 25(1)'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-07.1.CRA' yaml_id='SO-D-07.1.CRA' regulation='CRA' subdomain_id='D-07.1' applies_to='[CRA]' inherits_from='SO-CRA-045' source_SR='SR-CRA-064' activation='if CRA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='When placing a product with digital elements on the market, the manufacturer ensures that it has been designed, developed and produced in accordance with the essential cybersecurity requirements set out in Part I of Annex I (Art. 13(1) CRA), with the cybersecurity risk assessment propagated across the 6 lifecycle phases (planning, design, development, production, delivery, maintenance) per Art. 13(2) chapeau + sentence 1, with a view to minimising cybersecurity risks, preventing incidents, and minimising their impact (Art. 13(2) sentence 2).' considerations=['The Annex I Part I chapeau establishes the cybersecurity-by-design baseline across 11 sub-points (a)–(k) including attack-surface limitation (2)(j) + exploitation mitigation (2)(k) + automatic security updates (2)(c) + integrity protection (2)(f) + data-minimisation (2)(g) + resilience+availability (2)(h) + cascading-impact minimisation (2)(i) + recording-and-monitoring (2)(l).', 'The risk-assessment propagation across 6 phases is a continuous obligation, not a one-shot pre-launch activity — risk assessment is documented (Art. 13(3) sentence 1) and updated when there is a change of risk represented by the product.', 'Annex VII §3 risk-assessment record + Annex VII §2 design/development documentation form the technical-documentation evidence base (cross to D-09.4).', 'Support period ≥ 5 years (Art. 13(8) sentence 3); 10-year Annex II information accessibility (Art. 13(18)).', 'For an integrated manufacturer-controller-deployer, CRA-side Annex I Part I product-cybersecurity by-design discharges the engineering substrate; GDPR Art. 25(1) data-protection by-design discharges the personal-data overlay; the two stack vertically on the same product-lifecycle.', "For an AI-enabled CRA product, CRA Art. 13(4) sentence 2 explicit AI-Act-substitution for risk assessment permits a unified risk assessment under AI Act Art. 9 to substitute for the CRA risk assessment when both apply (SR-CRA-066) — the by-design risk-assessment obligation is satisfied by the AI Act Art. 9 + Art. 17 risk-management-system documentation that covers both regimes' risk-assessment content.", 'For a CRA manufacturer that is also a DORA financial entity, CRA-side Annex VII §3 risk-assessment record feeds the DORA-side Art. 6(1) ICT risk-management framework + Art. 9(4)(e) change-management six-step + Art. 24 testing programme — the upstream CRA-side by-design discipline documents the product cybersecurity for procurement by the downstream DORA-side deployer.'] anchors=['Annex I (Art. 13(1)', 'Annex I Part I', 'Annex II', 'Annex VII', 'Art. 13(1)', 'Art. 13(18)', 'Art. 13(2)', 'Art. 13(3)', 'Art. 13(4)', 'Art. 13(8)', 'Art. 17', 'Art. 24', 'Art. 25(1)', 'Art. 6(1)', 'Art. 9', 'Art. 9(4)', '§2', '§3'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-07.1.DORA' yaml_id='SO-D-07.1.DORA' regulation='DORA' subdomain_id='D-07.1' applies_to='[DORA]' inherits_from='SO-DORA-004' source_SR='SR-DORA-004' activation='if DORA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Financial entities establish a sound network and infrastructure management structure using appropriate techniques, methods and protocols (Art. 9(4)(b) DORA) with appropriate and comprehensive documented policies for patches and updates maintained (Art. 9(4)(f)).' considerations=['DORA does not impose a dedicated secure-by-design mandate as such — the security-in-design dimension for the financial-entity side is operationalised through Art. 9(4)(e) ICT change-management six-step (recorded/tested/assessed/approved/implemented/verified in a controlled manner) and Art. 24 ICT risk-management testing programme (12-way open list including vulnerability assessments, scans, source-code reviews where feasible, scenario-based tests, penetration testing, etc.).', 'Art. 9(4)(b) network-and-infrastructure-management baseline + Art. 9(4)(f) patch-policies baseline are the standing instruments; change-mgmt six-step (SR-DORA-023) + testing programme (SR-DORA-005) are the by-design operationalisation instruments.', 'For a DORA-only entity that is not a CRA manufacturer and does not process personal data via high-risk AI, D-07.1 by-design compliance is demonstrated through the change-management six-step + testing programme outputs, with no standalone OJ-mandated by-design obligation.', 'For a financial entity that is also a CRA manufacturer, upstream CRA-side Annex I Part I product by-design feeds the downstream DORA-side change-management six-step + testing programme — the by-design architecture stacks with the product-side Annex I Part I essential-requirements providing the by-design output, and the deployer-side Art. 9(4)(e) + Art. 24 providing the by-design operationalisation.', 'For a financial entity that is also a controller processing personal data, controller-side GDPR Art. 25(1) data-protection by-design sits on top of the DORA-side change-mgmt six-step + testing programme — the by-design architecture stacks with the data-protection overlay on top of the financial-entity infrastructure-management baseline.', 'DORA-side by-design obligations propagate downstream to D-07.2 (Secure Coding Practices) as the code-level instruction in the change-management gate, D-07.3 (CI/CD Pipeline Security) as the delivery-path instruction in the testing programme, and D-07.4 (Change Management) as the explicit change-management six-step that operationalises by-design at the entity side.', 'Art. 5(2)+(4) management-body `define, approve, oversee and is responsible for the implementation of all arrangements related to the ICT risk management framework` is the upstream governance instrument for the by-design architecture on the DORA side.'] anchors=['Annex I Part I', 'Art. 24', 'Art. 25(1)', 'Art. 5(2)', 'Art. 9(4)'] csf=[]

AI_Act in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='High-risk AI systems are designed and developed in such a way that they achieve an appropriate level of
