categories (6 categories: data poisoning + model poisoning + adversarial examples + model evasion + confidentiality attacks + model flaws) are AI-specific attack categories that do not substitute for CRA Annex I Part I (2)(j) attack-surface limitation or (2)(k) exploitation-mitigation outcomes (cross to D-07.2).', 'The Quality Management System (QMS) under Art. 17(1) is the AI-Act-side by-design operationalisation mechanism — documented in systematic and orderly manner covering at least 13 enumerated aspects including Art. 17(1)(c) design/design-control/design-verification (3-way AND).', 'Annex IV technical documentation (per Art. 11 + Art. 12(2)) is the technical-documentation evidence base for the by-design outputs.', 'AI Act Recital 78 explicitly preserves the GDPR — for a high-risk AI system processing personal data, AI Act Art. 15(1) accuracy+robustness+cybersecurity + QMS design/design-control/design-verification stacks with GDPR Art. 25(1) data-protection by-design as distinct design outputs (AI-system property vs privacy property).', "For an AI-enabled CRA product, CRA Art. 13(4) sentence 2 explicit AI-Act-substitution for risk assessment permits a unified risk assessment under AI Act Art. 9 to substitute for the CRA risk assessment when both apply (SR-CRA-066) — the by-design risk-assessment obligation is satisfied by the AI Act Art. 9 + Art. 17 risk-management-system documentation that covers both regimes' risk-assessment content.", 'For a financial entity deploying high-risk AI, DORA Art. 9(4)(e) change-management six-step is the operational gate; AI Act QMS design controls is the governance gate; the two stack with the change-mgmt six-step pre-empting the deployment and the QMS design controls governing the design-development activity.', 'The by-design architecture propagates downstream to D-07.2 (Secure Coding Practices) via the AI Act Art. 15(4)–(5) AI-attack-defence categories as the AI/ML-specific secure-coding baseline (cross to D-07.2 — SR-AI_Act-016).'] anchors=['Annex I Part I (2)', 'Annex IV', 'Art. 11', 'Art. 12(2)', 'Art. 13(4)', 'Art. 15(1)', 'Art. 15(4)', 'Art. 17', 'Art. 17(1)', 'Art. 25(1)', 'Art. 9', 'Art. 9(4)'] csf=[]

layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-07.2 Secure Coding Practices
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl: id='SO-D-07.2.HL' subdomain_id='D-07.2' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source=None verified_relationship_basis=None emergent_tensions=None objective='Coding practices deliver attack-surface limitation, exploitation mitigation, and AI-system attack-defence under an appropriate coding-practice evidence base.' considerations=['3 of 5 regulations participate (CRA, DORA partial, AI Act partial); GDPR and NIS 2 are explicitly out-of-scope (OJ Art. 25(1) does not specify secure-coding practices; OJ Art. 21(2)(e) does not mention CI/CD pipeline or secure-coding standards).', 'The coding-practice evidence base is typically built from industry frameworks (NIST SSDF + OWASP SAMM + ISO/IEC 27034) since no OJ clause prescribes specific coding standards.', 'The three participating regulators anchor the coding-practices duty at distinct target objects: CRA `limitation of attack surfaces, including attack surfaces of external interfaces` (Annex I Part I (2)(j)) + `reduce the impact of an incident using appropriate exploitation-mitigation mechanisms and techniques` (Annex I Part I (2)(k)) — product-coding-outcome mandate at the manufacturer side; DORA Art. 9(4)(e) change-management six-step — entity-process mandate at the financial-entity side, with implicit coding-dimension inference through `tested`/`assessed` legs + Art. 25 testing modalities (source-code reviews where feasible) — no OJ-mandated secure-coding-standards prescription (P0 disagreement on AEGIS-taxonomy sole-authority assignment); AI Act Art. 15(4)–(5) — AI-system attack-defence mandate at the AI-system-provider side (6 categories: data poisoning + model poisoning + adversarial examples + model evasion + confidentiality attacks + model flaws).', '3 pairwise cells verified by CRDA-deep as 3 SAME — COMPLEMENTARY (no CORRECTED, no CONTRADICTORY), but with substantial scope-disjoint qualifiers on 2 of 3 pairs in baseline: CRA↔DORA = N typically (manufacturer vs financial-entity, product vs process); CRA↔AI_Act = Conditional Y on AI-enabled CRA products; DORA↔AI_Act = N typically (financial-entity process vs AI-system coding).', 'The high-level SO engages only on the Conditional-Y integrated stack (when an AI-enabled CRA product is also deployed by a DORA financial entity — the vertically-integrated manufacturer-controller-deployer stack). For a 5-FTE SaaS startup with CRA applicability only, the high-level SO is NOT activated.', 'The two Layer 2 review items (P0 DORA-taxonomy-disagreement + CRA outcome-level vs AI Act attack-category layered-stack requirement) are documented separately — not as CONTRADICTORY/CORRECTED reclassifications that require Phase 1C tension-resolution.', 'For AI-enabled CRA products, CRA Annex I Part I (2)(j) + (2)(k) outcome-level obligations + AI Act Art. 15(4)–(5) attack-defence categories stack with **no OJ-level consolidation rule** (unlike CRA Art. 13(4) sentence 2 unified-risk-assessment carve-out for AI Act Art. 9, which does not extend to coding practices).', 'The per-reg perspective (target object, trigger, anchor, threshold, evidence template, recipient, legal anchor) is preserved verbatim in the three sub-SOs; the per-tier scope-disjoint structure is surfaced as a 2-of-3 N qualifier in baseline.'] anchors=['Annex I Part I (2)', 'Art. 13(4)', 'Art. 15(4)', 'Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 25', 'Art. 25(1)', 'Art. 9', 'Art. 9(4)'] csf=[] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto  # activates when ≥2 applicable regs have ≥1 pair with Y/Conditional Y scope overlap on the same party AND ≥1 sub-SO activates; for D-07.2 only 1 of 3 pairs (CRA↔AI_Act) has Conditional Y scope overlap on the AI-enabled CRA product integrated stack; the other 2 pairs (CRA↔DORA + DORA↔AI_Act) are N in baseline — so the high-level SO engages ONLY on the Conditional Y integrated stack (AI-enabled CRA product deployed by a DORA financial entity or similar integrated stack). For a 5-FTE SaaS startup with CRA applicability only, the high-level SO is NOT activated.'
hso_per_reg: id='SO-D-07.2.CRA' yaml_id='SO-D-07.2.CRA' regulation='CRA' subdomain_id='D-07.2' applies_to='[CRA]' inherits_from='SO-CRA-046' source_SR='SR-CRA-067' activation='if CRA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='The manufacturer designs, develops, and produces the product with digital elements to limit its attack surfaces, including attack surfaces of external interfaces (Annex I Part I (2)(j) CRA), and to reduce the impact of an incident using appropriate exploitation-mitigation mechanisms and techniques (Annex I Part I (2)(k) CRA).' considerations=['`attack-surface limitation` is the outcome-level mandate on product-side coding — minimum-necessary external interfaces, minimum-necessary attack surfaces, and minimum-necessary exploitable paths.', '`exploitation-mitigation` is the outcome-level mandate on product-side incident-impact-reduction — appropriate mechanisms and techniques to reduce the impact of an incident (ASLR, stack-canaries, control-flow integrity, sandboxing, memory-safe language subsystems, bounds checking, least-privilege subsystems, reduced-privilege components as typical mechanisms).', 'The CRA-side participation at D-07.2 is partial in the SR sense: OJ Annex I Part I (2)(j) + (2)(k) prescribes outcome-level mandates but does NOT specify secure-coding standards (no coding-language-specific linting, no secure-coding-framework adoption, no NIST SSDF/OWASP SAMM/ISO/IEC 27034 enforcement). The manufacturer builds the coding-standards baseline from industry frameworks (NIST SSDF, OWASP SAMM, ISO/IEC 27034) and demonstrates compliance against the Annex I Part I (2)(j) + (2)(k) outcome-level obligations.', 'CRA-side coding-outcomes are demonstrated in Annex VII §2 design/development documentation + Annex VII §3 risk-assessment record (cross to D-09.4 — SO-CRA-059 + SO-CRA-053).', 'The Annex I Part I (2) attack-surface + exploitation-mitigation outcomes are propagated downstream from the 6-phase CRA risk-assessment-propagation at D-07.1 (planning + design + development + production + delivery + maintenance) — at the development phase, the coding-outcome decisions are realised through in-house secure-coding decisions.', 'For an AI-enabled CRA product, CRA-side Annex I Part I (2)(j) + (2)(k) outcome mandate stacks with AI Act Art. 15(4)–(5) AI-attack-defence mandate — the two regimes DO NOT substitute; **no OJ-level consolidation rule exists for the coding-practices dimension** (unlike CRA Art. 13(4) sentence 2 unified-risk-assessment carve-out for AI Act Art. 9, which does not extend to coding practices).', 'For a 5-FTE manufacturer of a CRA-regulated product, the coding-outcomes baseline is built from industry frameworks and demonstrated against Annex I Part I (2)(j) + (2)(k) outcome-level obligations via the Annex VII §2 design/development documentation record.'] anchors=['Annex I Part I (2)', 'Annex VII', 'Art. 13(4)', 'Art. 15(4)', 'Art. 9', '§2', '§3'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-07.2.DORA' yaml_id='SO-D-07.2.DORA' regulation='DORA' subdomain_id='D-07.2' applies_to='[DORA]' inherits_from='SO-DORA-013 (partial via Art. 9(4)(e) — D-07.4 primary, D-07.2 partial by inference only)' source_SR='SR-DORA-023' activation='if DORA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Financial entities implement documented policies, procedures and controls for ICT change management, including changes to software, hardware, firmware components, systems or security parameters, that are based on a risk assessment approach, in order to ensure that all changes to ICT systems are recorded, tested, assessed, approved, implemented and verified in a controlled manner (Art. 9(4)(e) DORA — 6-step change-management process).' considerations=['The secure-coding dimension for DORA is implicit through the `tested` and `assessed` legs of the change-mgmt six-step + the Art. 25 testing modalities (12-way open list including vulnerability assessments, scans, source code reviews where feasible, scenario-based tests, penetration testing, etc.).', "The DORA-side participation at D-07.2 is partial in the SR sense: no OJ mandate prescribes secure-coding standards specifically. The DORA-side coding dimension is derived from the change-mgmt six-step's `tested` + `assessed` legs + the Art. 25 testing modalities (source-code reviews where feasible as one of 12 modalities).", '**P0 disagreement ON PARTICIPATION (preserved as Layer 2 review item):** AEGIS taxonomy §4.1 marks DORA as SOLE AUTHORITY for D-07.2 but this assignment has no OJ-text anchor per CRDA-deep verification (Art. 9(4)(e) is change-management policy; Art. 9(4)(f) is patches-and-updates policy; no OJ clause prescribes secure-coding standards). Either (a) revise the taxonomy to remove the DORA sole-authority assignment, or (b) identify the OJ clause that supports it.', 'For a 5-FTE financial entity, the DORA-side coding dimension is demonstrated through: (1) documented Art. 9(4)(e) change-management policies/procedures/controls with the 6-step process; (2) Art. 25 testing programme with the 12-way open testing-modality list; (3) Art. 11(3) response-and-recovery plans + Art. 11(2) backup-policies — NOT through an OJ-mandated secure-coding-standards prescription.', "The DORA-side coding-output is the change-management-evidenced deployed code; the coding-standards baseline itself (NIST SSDF/OWASP SAMM/ISO/IEC 27034) is supplied by the entity's ICT risk-management-policy tier rather than by an OJ mandate.", 'CRDA-deep substantive note: the `complementary` label for CRA↔DORA is more a taxonomy artifact than a substantive relationship — the two regimes do not overlap substantively on coding practices (CRA covers the product, DORA covers the process); the high-level SO does NOT engage on the CRA↔DORA pair in baseline because the pair is substantively scope-disjoint.'] anchors=['Art. 11(2)', 'Art. 11(3)', 'Art. 25', 'Art. 9(4)', '§4'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-07.2.AI_Act' yaml_id='SO-D-07.2.AIACT' regulation='AI_Act' subdomain_id='D-07.2' applies_to='[AI_Act]' inherits_from='SO-AI_Act-009 (partial via Art. 15(4)–(5))' source_SR='SR-AI_Act-016' activation='if AI_Act in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective="High-risk AI systems are designed and developed with appropriate technical and organisational measures to enable the AI systems to effectively resist, as appropriate to the AI system's purpose and conditions of use, attempts to manipulate the training data set (data poisoning) or pre-trained components used in training (model poisoning), inputs designed to cause the AI model to make a mistake (adversarial examples or model evasion), confidentiality attacks or model flaws (Art. 15(4)–(5) AI Act)." considerations=['The 6 AI-attack-defence categories are: (1) data poisoning — manipulation of the training data set; (2) model poisoning — manipulation of pre-trained components; (3) adversarial examples — inputs designed to cause the AI model to make a mistake; (4) model evasion — adversarial-example-induced evasion; (5) confidentiality attacks — attacks on confidentiality of training data, parameters, or outputs; (6) model flaws — vulnerabilities or weaknesses inherent in model architecture or training process.', "The `as appropriate to the AI system's purpose and conditions of use` is a proportionality qualifier at the AI-system-purpose level — calibration is informed by the intended purpose (cross to D-09.2 — SO-AI_Act-001 Art. 9 risk-management-system) and the conditions of use (operational environment + reasonably foreseeable use).", 'The AI-Act-side participation at D-07.2 is partial in the SR sense: Art. 15(4)–(5) AI-attack-defence categories are AI/ML-specific and do NOT map to conventional secure-coding mandates (no general coding-standards prescription in AI Act — the AI Act addresses AI-attack-defence, not conventional coding practices).', "For an AI-enabled CRA product, AI Act Art. 15(4)–(5) AI-attack-defence stacks with CRA Annex I Part I (2)(j) + (2)(k) attack-surface + exploitation-mitigation — the two regimes DO NOT substitute (AI Act defence categories do not substitute for CRA's outcome-level obligations, and vice versa); **no OJ-level consolidation rule exists for the coding-practices dimension** (unlike CRA Art. 13(4) sentence 2 unified-risk-assessment carve-out for AI Act Art. 9, which does not extend to coding practices).", 'AI-Act-side attack-defence is documented in QMS design-control records (Art. 17(1)(c) design/design-control/design-verification) + Annex IV technical documentation + Art. 9 risk-management-system documentation (cross to D-09.1 — SO-AI_Act-010 + SO-AI_Act-001).', 'For a high-risk AI system provider, the AI-attack-defence coding-practices baseline is built from AI/ML-specific frameworks (NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 23894, MITRE ATLAS) and demonstrated against the 6 Art. 15(4)–(5) attack-defence categories via the QMS + Annex IV documentation.', 'AI-Act-Recital 78 GDPR preservation operates at the AI-system side for high-risk AI systems processing personal data — the AI-Act-side AI-attack-defence does NOT substitute for the GDPR Art. 25(1) data-protection by-design; the GDPR-side by-design is layered on top via the controller-means-determination + processing-time by-default.'] anchors=['Annex I Part I (2)', 'Annex IV', 'Art. 13(4)', 'Art. 15(4)', 'Art. 17(1)', 'Art. 25(1)', 'Art. 9'] csf=[]

layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl: id='SO-D-07.3.HL' subdomain_id='D-07.3' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source=None verified_relationship_basis=None emergent_tensions=None objective='CI/CD pipeline security delivers build-time control baselines (signed artefacts, build-agent integrity, ephemeral build environments) and update-distribution delivery-path security.' considerations=['2 of 5 regulations participate (NIS 2, CRA); GDPR, DORA, and AI Act are explicitly out-of-scope (none of GDPR / DORA / AI Act OJ text specifies CI/CD build-time controls or CI/CD pipeline-security controls as such).', 'Build-time controls are typically built from industry frameworks (NIST SP 800-204 / OWASP CI/CD Top 10 / SLSA) since no OJ clause prescribes CI/CD build-time controls.', 'NIS 2 `security in … maintenance of network and information systems, including vulnerability handling and disclosure` (Art. 21(2)(e) third clause) — entity-side partial-coverage of CI/CD via the maintenance dimension (T3-vs-text gap: OJ does not mention `pipeline`, `CI`, or `CD` — the partial coverage is realised through the 3-phase coordinated lifecycle via the maintenance phase; AEGIS taxonomy §4.1 marks NIS 2 as sole authority with the T3-vs-text caveat).', 'CRA `securely distribute updates for the product with digital elements in a timely manner, including, where appropriate, through automatic updates` (Annex I Part II (7)) + dissemination free of charge + clearly described + security improvement information + user-actionable guidance (Annex I Part II (8) verbatim) — product-side update-delivery-path partial-coverage (`without delay` qualitative; 5-year support-period floor from Art. 13(8) sentence 3; 10-year update-availability tail from Art. 13(9)).', '1 pairwise cell verified by CRDA-deep as SAME — COMPLEMENTARY with substantial scope-disjoint qualifier on the typical case — the two regimes target distinct objects at distinct actors (entity-side CI/CD pipeline vs product-side update delivery path; NSIE deploying NIS vs manufacturer distributing security updates).', 'The high-level SO engages only on the Conditional-Y integrated stack (when an NIS 2 essential/important entity procures a CRA-regulated product — the supplier-customer boundary where the NIS 2 procurement gate references CRA-conformant products and CRA Part II (7)/(8) update-distribution obligations discharge the NIS 2 supplier-side patch pathway); on the typical-case N scope-disjoint baseline, the high-level SO does NOT engage.', "CI/CD build-time controls (signed artefacts, build-agent integrity, ephemeral build environments) are industry best-practice, not regulatory mandate — Phase 1 entities must construct the CI/CD baseline from industry frameworks (NIST SP 800-204, OWASP CI/CD Top 10, SLSA) and demonstrate compliance against NIS 2's partial-coverage maintenance dimension and CRA's partial-coverage update-distribution pathway.", 'For a 5-FTE SaaS startup with NIS 2 applicability only (no CRA applicability), the high-level SO is NOT activated. For a CRA-regulated manufacturer that is not an NIS 2 entity, the high-level SO is NOT activated either.', 'The per-reg perspective (target object, trigger, anchor, threshold, evidence template, recipient, legal anchor) is preserved verbatim in the two sub-SOs with the substantial scope-disjoint structure on the typical case.'] anchors=['Annex I Part II (7)', 'Annex I Part II (8)', 'Art. 13(8)', 'Art. 13(9)', 'Art. 21(2)', '§4'] csf=[] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto  # activates when ≥2 applicable regs have a Y or Conditional Y scope overlap on the same party AND ≥1 sub-SO activates; for D-07.3 the only 1 pair is NIS2↔CRA = Conditional Y (only when an NIS 2 entity procures a CRA-conformant product) AND N (typically) — so the high-level SO engages ONLY on the Conditional-Y integrated stack (NIS 2 entity procuring CRA-conformant product). For a 5-FTE SaaS startup with NIS 2 applicability only (no CRA applicability), the high-level SO is NOT activated. For a CRA-regulated manufacturer that is not an NIS 2 entity, the high-level SO is NOT activated either.'
hso_per_reg: id='SO-D-07.3.NIS2' yaml_id='SO-D-07.3.NIS2' regulation='NIS2' subdomain_id='D-07.3' applies_to='[NIS2]' inherits_from='SO-NIS2-017 (partial via the maintenance dimension — `SO-NIS2-017` routes to D-07.3 via Art. 21(2)(e) third clause)' source_SR='SR-NIS2-028' activation='if NIS2 in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Essential and important entities take appropriate and proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures to ensure security in the maintenance of network and information systems, including vulnerability handling and disclosure (Art. 21(2)(e) third clause NIS 2).' considerations=['The partial coverage of CI/CD pipeline security via the maintenance dimension is the operational heart of the NIS 2-side participation at D-07.3: the entity-side deployment-and-maintenance pipeline — patch-management policies + vulnerability-handling-and-disclosure records + the 3-phase coordinated lifecycle of Art. 21(2)(e) (acquisition + development + maintenance) with the maintenance phase covering the delivery-path security dimension of the CI/CD pipeline.', '**T3-vs-text gap:** the OJ Art. 21(2)(e) does not mention `pipeline`, `CI`, or `CD`. AEGIS taxonomy §4.1 marks NIS 2 as the SOLE AUTHORITY for D-07.3 CI/CD Pipeline Security, but the OJ literal text is silent on CI/CD build-time controls (signed artefacts, build-agent integrity, ephemeral build environments).', 'The entity-side CI/CD-pipeline compliance is demonstrated through: (a) NIS 2-side partial-coverage via the maintenance dimension (3-phase coordinated lifecycle — patch-management policies + vulnerability-handling-and-disclosure records + the maintenance phase operational implementation); (b) the industry-framework CI/CD build-time baseline (NIST SP 800-204 / OWASP CI/CD Top 10 / SLSA); (c) the supplier-customer boundary evidence trail (NIS 2 procurement gate via `SR-NIS2-026` supplier-secure-development-procedures three-prong + Art. 21(3) sentence 1 supplier-vulnerability-intelligence three-prong) on the Conditional-Y integrated stack.', "The vulnerability-handling-and-disclosure leg (Art. 21(2)(e) fourth clause) is one of three coordinated legs — its operational implementation is the entity's coordinated vulnerability-handling capability (cross to D-02.3 — CRA is sole authority for the CVD-architecture, NIS 2 partial coverage per SO-NIS2-002).", 'Art. 21(1) chapeau `appropriate and proportionate` is read with Art. 21(1) sentence 2 state-of-the-art floor + Recital 56 cost-of-implementation qualifier + Member-State transposition divergence on the appropriateness test.', 'For a 5-FTE essential entity, the NIS 2-side CI/CD-pipeline compliance is demonstrated through the maintenance-dimension partial-coverage + industry-framework CI/CD build-time baseline.'] anchors=['Art. 21(1)', 'Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 21(3)', '§4'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-07.3.CRA' yaml_id='SO-D-07.3.CRA' regulation='CRA' subdomain_id='D-07.3' applies_to='[CRA]' inherits_from='SO-CRA-009 (partial cross-ref via Annex I Part II (7) — secure update distribution; SO-CRA-009 primary sub-domain is D-02.2 patch management with cross-ref to D-07.3 partial)' source_SR='SR-CRA-009' activation='if CRA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='The manufacturer of a product with digital elements shall securely distribute updates for the product with digital elements in a timely manner, including, where appropriate, through automatic updates (Annex I Part II (7) CRA), and ensure that updates are disseminated free of charge, are clearly described, contain information on the security improvements and on the actions the user should take (Annex I Part II (8) CRA).' considerations=['The product-side update delivery path is the operational heart of the CRA-side participation at D-07.3: the manufacturer-side distribution mechanism that securely delivers security updates to users — including, where appropriate, through automatic updates — across the support period (5-year floor from Art. 13(8) sentence 3) + the 10-year update-availability tail (Art. 13(9)).', 'The Annex I Part II (7) + (8) text together constitute the OJ-mandated product-side update-delivery-path obligation — a partial-coverage cross-ref from SO-CRA-009 (D-02.2 patch management primary) to D-07.3 CI/CD Pipeline Security partial.', '**Coverage-scope caveat (CRITICAL):** CRA covers product-side update delivery path only, not CI/CD build-time controls (signed artefacts, build-agent integrity, ephemeral build environments). The manufacturer-side CI/CD-pipeline compliance is demonstrated through: (a) CRA-side Annex I Part II (7)+(8) update-delivery-path evidence (Annex VII §2 design/development documentation covering the secure-update-distribution mechanism + advisory messages describing user-actionable security improvements); (b) the industry-framework CI/CD build-time baseline (NIST SP 800-204 / OWASP CI/CD Top 10 / SLSA); (c) the support-period operational implementation (5-year support-period floor + 10-year update-availability tail).', 'The `without delay` (Annex I Part II (8)) qualitative threshold on update dissemination — no quantitative cadence — is calibrated by the Annex I Part II risk-assessment propagation across the 6 lifecycle phases (planning + design + development + production + delivery + maintenance) per Art. 13(2).', 'For an integrated manufacturer-controller-deployer stack (CRA manufacturer + NIS 2 entity + GDPR controller + DORA financial entity + AI Act provider/deployer), the CRA-side Annex I Part II (7)+(8) update-delivery-path discharges the NIS 2-side supplier-side patch pathway on the supplier-customer boundary of the Conditional-Y integrated stack.'] anchors=['Annex I Part II', 'Annex I Part II (7)', 'Annex I Part II (8)', 'Annex VII', 'Art. 13(2)', 'Art. 13(8)', 'Art. 13(9)', '§2'] csf=[]

objective='Change management delivers documented change-management procedures (manufacturer-side series-production conformity + entity-side change-management six-step), risk-assessment-approach, controlled-manner, and substantial-modification assessment with manufacturer-equivalent status consequences where applicable.' considerations=['2 of 5 regulations participate (CRA, DORA); GDPR, NIS 2, AI Act are explicitly out-of-scope (GDPR Art. 24 imposes review-and-update process outcomes but no change-management controls; NIS 2 has no OJ mandate for change-management controls per CRDA confirmation; AI Act does not impose a change-management mandate).', 'CRA Art. 13(14) `procedures are in place for products with digital elements that are part of a series of production to remain in conformity with this Regulation` + Art. 21-22 substantial-modification = manufacturer trigger (Art. 3(30) substantial-modification definition + Art. 13(10) substantial-modification compliance scope + Art. 13(21) immediate corrective measures on non-conformity) — product-side change-management obligation at the manufacturer side.', 'DORA Art. 9(4)(e) `documented policies, procedures and controls for ICT change management, including changes to software, hardware, firmware components, systems or security parameters … based on a risk assessment approach … in order to ensure that all changes to ICT systems are recorded, tested, assessed, approved, implemented and verified in a controlled manner` (5-way OR change-targets + 6-way AND change-management steps + `controlled manner` mandate) — entity-side change-management obligation at the financial-entity side.', "1 pairwise cell verified by CRDA-deep as SAME — COMPLEMENTARY with Conditional Y scope overlap on the substantial-modification trigger event: the high-level SO engages on the Conditional-Y integrated stack (when a DORA financial entity customises a CRA-conformant product in a manner that triggers Art. 22 third-party substantial modification = manufacturer — same change event triggers both regimes on a single party at a single event, layering DORA's six-step on top of CRA's substantial-modification trigger).", 'On the simple supplier-customer boundary (N (typically)), the two regimes operate independently on the two sides (CRA-side series-production conformity at manufacturer + DORA-side change-management six-step at financial-entity) with the DORA six-step documentation serving as evidence trail for CRA Art. 13(14) series-production conformity when substantively the same change event is recorded on both sides.', 'The two regulators stack on the substantial-modification trigger event with layered documentation (DORA six-step record + CRA Art. 13(14) series-production record + substantial-modification assessment per Art. 13(10) + Annex VII technical-documentation update).', '**AEGIS taxonomy §4.1 sole-authority disagreement (Layer 2 review item):** AEGIS taxonomy §4.1 marks DORA as the SOLE AUTHORITY for D-07.4 but CRDA-deep finds CRA Art. 13(14) + Art. 21-22 + Art. 13(10) constitute dedicated authorities for the substantial-modification trigger. CRA participation at D-07.4 is preserved as co-equal participant rather than partial-coverage cross-ref (per CRA validation report line 177). Either (a) revise the AEGIS taxonomy §4.1 to remove the DORA sole-authority assignment and add CRA as co-equal authority, or (b) identify the OJ clause that supports the DORA sole-authority reading.', 'The per-reg perspective (target object, trigger, anchor, threshold, evidence template, recipient, legal anchor) is preserved verbatim in the two sub-SOs.'] anchors=['Annex VII', 'Art. 13(10)', 'Art. 13(14)', 'Art. 13(21)', 'Art. 21', 'Art. 22', 'Art. 24', 'Art. 3(30)', 'Art. 9(4)', '§4'] csf=[] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto  # activates when ≥2 applicable regs have a Y scope overlap on the same party AND ≥1 sub-SO activates; for D-07.4 the only 1 pair (CRA↔DORA) returns Y on the substantial-modification trigger event (when a DORA financial entity customises a CRA-conformant product) + N (typically) on the simple supplier-customer boundary; the high-level SO engages on the Conditional-Y integrated stack (substantial-modification trigger event). For a CRA-regulated manufacturer that is not a DORA financial entity, the high-level SO is NOT activated. For a DORA financial entity that does not customise CRA-conformant products, the high-level SO is NOT activated either.'
hso_per_reg: id='SO-D-07.4.CRA' yaml_id='SO-D-07.4.CRA' regulation='CRA' subdomain_id='D-07.4' applies_to='[CRA]' inherits_from='SO-CRA-047' source_SR='SR-CRA-069 (Art. 13(14) series-production + SR-CRA-070 Art. 13(10) + 21-22 substantial-modification)' activation='if CRA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='The manufacturer of a product with digital elements that is part of a series of production ensures that procedures are in place for products with digital elements that are part of a series of production to remain in conformity with this Regulation (Art. 13(14) CRA).' considerations=["An importer or distributor who places a product with digital elements on the market under its own name or trademark, or who carries out a substantial modification of a product with digital elements already placed on the market, is considered to be the manufacturer for the purposes of the Regulation and assumes the manufacturer's obligations under Arts. 13 and 14 (Art. 21 CRA).", 'A natural or legal person, other than the manufacturer, importer, or distributor, that carries out a substantial modification of a product with digital elements and makes that product available on the market, is considered to be the manufacturer for the purposes of the Regulation, with obligations attaching to the affected part or — where the substantial modification has an impact on the cybersecurity of the product as a whole — to the entire product (Art. 22(1)+(2) CRA).', 'The substantial-modification definition under Art. 3(30) (D30 — VAG+POLY+COORD-S3) is the boundary between normal-version-update and manufacturer-equivalent liability transfer.', 'Art. 13(10) substantial-modification compliance scope carve-out allows the manufacturer to ensure Annex I Part II (2) compliance for the version last placed on the market subject to user-migration conditions (user is given the choice to migrate to the modified product or retain the last-placed version, with access to the last-placed version free of charge + no additional costs to adjust the hardware/software environment).', 'Art. 13(21) immediate corrective measures duty requires the manufacturer to immediately take the corrective measures necessary to bring the product or processes into conformity, or to withdraw or recall the product (cross to D-04.2 — `SO-CRA-063`).', 'The CRA-side participation at D-07.4 is preserved as co-equal participation rather than as partial-coverage cross-ref per CRA `03_validation_report.md` line 177 — the substantial-modification trigger with manufacturer-equivalent consequences (Art. 22 third-party substantial modification = manufacturer) is a dedicated authority for the substantial-modification dimension that complements the DORA-side entity-level change-management six-step.', 'For an integrated manufacturer that is also a DORA financial entity (Conditional-Y substantial-modification trigger event), the manufacturer-equivalent status transfer (Art. 22) applies on top of the DORA-side six-step process (Art. 9(4)(e)) with layered documentation (DORA six-step record + CRA Art. 13(14) series-production record + substantial-modification assessment per Art. 13(10) + Annex VII technical-documentation update). On the simple supplier-customer boundary (no substantial modification), the DORA-side six-step record can serve as the evidence trail for CRA Art. 13(14) series-production conformity when substantively the same change event is recorded on both sides.'] anchors=['Annex I Part II (2)', 'Annex VII', 'Art. 13(10)', 'Art. 13(14)', 'Art. 13(21)', 'Art. 21', 'Art. 22', 'Art. 22(1)', 'Art. 3(30)', 'Art. 9(4)'] csf=[]

id='SO-D-07.4.DORA' yaml_id='SO-D-07.4.DORA' regulation='DORA' subdomain_id='D-07.4' applies_to='[DORA]' inherits_from='SO-DORA-013' source_SR='SR-DORA-023' activation='if DORA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Financial entities implement documented policies, procedures and controls for ICT change management, including changes to software, hardware, firmware components, systems or security parameters … based on a risk assessment approach … in order to ensure that all changes to ICT systems are recorded, tested, assessed, approved, implemented and verified in a controlled manner (Art. 9(4)(e) DORA — 5-way OR change-targets + 6-way AND change-management steps + `controlled manner` mandate).' considerations=['The 6-step change-management process is operationalised as: (1) recorded — every change to ICT systems is recorded; (2) tested — every change is tested before implementation (with documented test results); (3) assessed — every change is assessed for risk and impact (with documented assessment); (4) approved — every change is approved by an appropriate authority before implementation (with documented approval); (5) implemented — every change is implemented with documented implementation record; (6) verified — every change is verified post-implementation with documented verification.', 'The 6 steps are cumulative (R1 all six required per S3 COORD) — partial-process compliance is non-compliance.', 'The `controlled manner` qualifier (R1 documented procedure + segregated approval R3 both per S2 VAG) is read as the combination of documented procedure and segregated approval.', 'The 5 change-target categories (software + hardware + firmware components + systems + security parameters) are cumulative (R1 all five in scope per S3 COORD).', 'The `based on a risk assessment approach` is the operational anchor — the change-management six-step is calibrated by the risk assessment under Art. 6(1) + Art. 7(2) + Art. 8(2) + EBA Guidelines on ICT and security risk management supervisory baseline.', 'The DORA-side participation at D-07.4 is the unique OJ-mandated dedicated authority for entity-level change-management controls — Art. 9(4)(e) is the only OJ-verbatim dedicated change-management mandate (no equivalent OJ mandate in CRA on the entity-level change-management dimension).', 'For a 5-FTE DORA financial entity, the change-management obligation is the Art. 9(4)(e) six-step process with EBA Guidelines supervisory baseline + the Art. 6(1) ICT risk-management framework.', 'For a DORA financial entity that customises a CRA-conformant product (Conditional-Y substantial-modification trigger event), the entity-side six-step process operates on top of the CRA-side substantial-modification trigger (Art. 22 third-party substantial-modification = manufacturer — the DORA entity becomes a CRA-manufacturer-equivalent with the attendant obligations: Art. 13 conformity-assessment + Art. 14 AEV/SI notification + Annex I compliance + Annex VII technical documentation + Art. 13(8) support period) with layered documentation.', "For a DORA financial entity that does not customise CRA-conformant products (simple supplier-customer boundary), the entity-side six-step process operates on the financial-entity ICT-infrastructure changes with the DORA six-step documentation serving as the change-management evidence trail for the entity's CRA-conformant product procurements when substantively the same change event is recorded on both sides.", "**Caveat (D-07.2 cross-references via SR-DORA-023 partial):** the change-management six-step's `tested` + `assessed` legs + Art. 25 testing modalities (source-code reviews where feasible as one of 12 modalities) imply a secure-coding dimension (D-07.2 cross-reference partial); no OJ-mandated coding-standards prescription. Layer 2 review item preserved at D-07.2: AEGIS-taxonomy §4.1 DORA sole-authority disagreement has no OJ-text support."] anchors=['Annex I', 'Annex VII', 'Art. 13', 'Art. 13(8)', 'Art. 14', 'Art. 22', 'Art. 25', 'Art. 6(1)', 'Art. 7(2)', 'Art. 8(2)', 'Art. 9(4)', '§4'] csf=[]

layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl: id='SO-D-08.1.HL' subdomain_id='D-08.1' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source=None verified_relationship_basis=None emergent_tensions=None objective='General security awareness is established through a documented training programme with population-wide coverage, audience-routing, and governance hooks.' considerations=['4 of 5 regulations participate (GDPR, NIS 2, CRA, DORA); AI Act is fully absent per CRDA-deep §D-08.1 (AI Act Art. 4 AI literacy + SR-AI_Act-012 human-oversight training for high-risk AI are mapped to D-08.2, not D-08.1).', "GDPR Art. 39(1)(a) `inform and advise the controller or the processor and the employees who carry out processing of their obligations` + Art. 39(1)(b) `monitor compliance with this Regulation, including the assignment of responsibilities, awareness-raising and training of staff involved in processing operations` — DPO-catalysed workforce data-protection awareness on the controller's processing-staff audience.", "NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(g) first clause `basic cyber hygiene practices and cybersecurity training` — entity-wide hygiene baseline with `appropriate and proportionate` chapeau + state-of-the-art floor, on the entity's workforce and systems substrate.", 'CRA Annex II §8(a)–(f) `detailed instructions … covering the necessary measures during initial commissioning and throughout the lifetime of the product to ensure its secure use` — manufacturer-shipped user-facing instructions on the end-user audience — **partial coverage** (user-facing not workforce).', 'DORA Art. 13(6) `ICT security awareness programmes and digital operational resilience training as compulsory modules in their staff training schemes, with a level of complexity commensurate to the remit of their functions` — financial-entity compulsory-modules-led staff training on the financial-entity workforce.', '6 pairwise cells: 3 SAME — COMPLEMENTARY (GDPR↔NIS2, GDPR↔DORA, NIS2↔DORA), 1 SAME — EQUAL (NIS2↔DORA on workforce awareness at entity level — DORA `compulsory modules` exceeds NIS 2 `basic cyber hygiene`), 3 SAME — DIFFERENT-PERSPECTIVE substantively scope-disjoint (GDPR↔CRA, NIS2↔CRA, CRA↔DORA — internal workforce vs external end-user with product).', 'The high-level SO engages on the Y-pairs integrated stack when ≥2 regs are applicable: GDPR↔NIS2 (DPO module + hygiene module combined into single curriculum); GDPR↔DORA (DORA programme as carrier + GDPR content as module); NIS2↔DORA (DORA-dominant for financial entities; NIS 2-dominant for non-financial NSIEs).', 'The CRA-involving pairs operate on substantively scope-disjoint audiences (internal workforce vs external end-user with product) — the parallel tracks coexist with no consolidation rule; the high-level SO does NOT collapse the audience boundaries.', 'For a 5-FTE SaaS startup with GDPR + CRA applicability, the two parallel training-programme tracks must be maintained separately (substantively scope-disjoint audiences).', 'The per-reg target audience, trigger, anchor, threshold, evidence template, recipient are preserved verbatim in the four sub-SOs.'] anchors=['Annex II', 'Art. 13(6)', 'Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 39(1)', 'Art. 4', '§8'] csf=[] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto  # activates when ≥2 applicable regs have ≥1 pair with Y scope overlap on the same party AND ≥1 sub-SO activates; for D-08.1 the 3 Y pairs (GDPR↔NIS2, GDPR↔DORA, NIS2↔DORA) all have Y scope overlap in baseline; the 3 N (typically) pairs (GDPR↔CRA, NIS2↔CRA, CRA↔DORA) are substantively scope-disjoint and do not engage the high-level SO. Once ≥2 regs are applicable the high-level SO engages on the joint-condition operator on the Y-pairs integrated stack.'
hso_per_reg: id='SO-D-08.1.GDPR' yaml_id='SO-D-08.1.GDPR' regulation='GDPR' subdomain_id='D-08.1' applies_to='[GDPR]' inherits_from='SO-GDPR-025' source_SR='SR-GDPR-042' activation='if GDPR in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='The data protection officer informs and advises the controller or the processor and the employees who carry out processing of their obligations pursuant to this Regulation and to other Union or Member State data protection provisions (Art. 39(1)(a) GDPR), and monitors compliance with this Regulation, including the assignment of responsibilities, awareness-raising and training of staff involved in processing operations (Art. 39(1)(b) GDPR).' considerations=["The DPO is the catalyst for the controller-side awareness programme — distinct from the controller's substantive training obligation — operating as the internal advisor and awareness-raising/training agent for staff involved in processing.", 'The design-anchor is DPO-discretionary cadence (no quantitative cadence in Art. 39(1)(b); the OJ is silent on training-frequency or completion-thresholds); `awareness-raising` implies ongoing reinforcement rather than one-off induction (per SR-GDPR-042 ambiguity reading).', "The DPO's awareness-raising obligation is structurally a general-population training duty covering all personnel involved in processing, on a recurring cadence and with content that updates to reflect emerging threats and changing data flows (PR.AT-01 anchor).", 'The role-specific layer (PR.AT-02) covers personnel with data-subject-facing, access-management, breach-response, or DPO-deputy responsibilities — distinct from the general awareness programme.', "The DPO's awareness function is documented under Art. 5(2) accountability on the controller side — the controller must demonstrate that the Art. 39(1)(a)+(b) DPO-catalysed awareness function was operationally exercised and recorded on the day of any supervisory inspection.", 'For an integrated controller-NSIE workforce, the GDPR data-protection awareness module combines with the NIS 2 entity-wide hygiene baseline into a single curriculum where the data-protection module feeds the GDPR obligation and the hygiene module feeds the NIS 2 obligation (per CRDA-deep §D-08.1 GDPR↔NIS2 verified relationship).', 'For a DORA financial entity that is a controller processing personal data over its own staff, the DORA Art. 13(6) programme is the carrier and the GDPR Art. 39(1)(b) DPO-catalysed data-protection awareness is the module (per CRDA-deep §D-08.1 GDPR↔DORA verified relationship).', 'For a CRA-regulated manufacturer that is also a controller, the GDPR workforce awareness obligation is independent of the CRA Annex II §8(a)–(f) user-facing instructions (substantively scope-disjoint audiences — workforce vs end-user — no consolidation rule applies).'] anchors=['Annex II', 'Art. 13(6)', 'Art. 39(1)', 'Art. 5(2)', '§8'] csf=['PR.AT-01', 'PR.AT-02']

id='SO-D-08.1.NIS2' yaml_id='SO-D-08.1.NIS2' regulation='NIS2' subdomain_id='D-08.1' applies_to='[NIS2]' inherits_from='SO-NIS2-018' source_SR='SR-NIS2-029' activation='if NIS2 in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Essential and important entities take appropriate and proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures to ensure basic cyber hygiene practices and cybersecurity training (Art. 21(2)(g) first clause NIS 2).' considerations=['The NIS 2 hygiene baseline is the entity-wide substrate covering all users of network and information systems with access to entity systems and services (per SO-NIS2-018 scope).', 'The hygiene practices are not enumerated in the OJ — `basic cyber hygiene` admits three operative readings (minimal-password-patch-antivirus, broader ENISA baseline, sector-specific), with the chosen reading being entity-discretionary interpretation under Recital 56 proportionality (per SR-NIS2-029 ambiguity_notes).', 'PR.AT-01 anchors the human-side hygiene substrate (phishing awareness, password discipline, social-engineering recognition, removable-media hygiene, disciplined use of administrative privileges).', 'PR.PS-01 anchors the system-side hygiene substrate (baseline configurations, secure configuration standards, change management and patch cadence for the NIS inventory).', 'The two together define the workforce-and-assets hygiene baseline that ENISA, the SANS Top 20, and the Australian Cyber Security Centre Essential Eight converge on (per SR-NIS2-029 security_rationale).', 'For an integrated controller-NSIE workforce, the NIS 2 hygiene module combines with the GDPR DPO-catalysed data-protection awareness module into a single curriculum.', "For DORA financial entities, the DORA Art. 13(6) `compulsory modules` is more prescriptive than NIS 2's `basic cyber hygiene` (entity-discretionary under Recital 56) — DORA-dominant for financial entities; NIS 2-dominant for non-financial NSIEs (per CRDA-deep §D-08.1 NIS2↔DORA EQUAL classification).", 'For a CRA-regulated manufacturer, the NIS 2 hygiene baseline on the workforce is independent of the CRA Annex II §8(a)–(f) user-facing instructions (substantively scope-disjoint audiences — workforce vs end-user — no consolidation rule applies).'] anchors=['Annex II', 'Art. 13(6)', 'Art. 21(2)', '§8'] csf=['PR.AT-01', 'PR.PS-01']

id='SO-D-08.1.CRA' yaml_id='SO-D-08.1.CRA' regulation='CRA' subdomain_id='D-08.1' applies_to='[CRA]' inherits_from='SO-CRA-048 (partial)' source_SR='SR-CRA-071' activation='if CRA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='A product with digital elements is accompanied by detailed instructions — or an internet address referring to such detailed instructions — covering the necessary measures during initial commissioning and throughout the lifetime of the product to ensure its secure use (Annex II §8(a)–(e) CRA), and — where the product is intended for integration into other products — the information necessary for the integrator to comply with the essential cybersecurity requirements set out in Part I of Annex I and the documentation requirements set out in Annex VII (Annex II §8(f) CRA).' considerations=['Annex II §8(a) covers necessary measures during initial commissioning and throughout the lifetime of the product; §8(b) covers how changes to the product can affect the security of data; §8(c) covers how security-relevant updates can be installed; §8(d) covers secure decommissioning of the product including user data removal; §8(e) covers how the default setting enabling automatic installation of security updates can be turned off.', 'Art. 13(18) extends this to a duty to provide the instructions in paper or electronic form, accessible for the support period (10-year Annex II information accessibility; cross to D-09.4).', "The CRA participation at D-08.1 is partial: Annex II §8(a)–(f) addresses the end-user audience with the product — not the manufacturer's or operator's workforce. AEGIS taxonomy §4.1 marks NIS 2 / DORA / GDPR as the authorities for full staff awareness.", 'The Annex II §8(f) integrator information is the workforce-side partial dimension — integrators who incorporate the product into a downstream system are informed of the cybersecurity measures required to maintain Annex I compliance (B2B integrators are the closest workforce-side dimension at D-08.1).', 'The chosen PR.AT-01 mapping at SR-CRA-071 anchors the workforce-side (integrator) dimension; the user-side is marked UNMAPPED_CSF per SR-CRA-071 unmapped_csf_justification (NIST CSF 2.0 PR.AT-01 trains the workforce, not the end-user; no direct CSF 2.0 Subcategory for end-user instructions on secure product use).', 'For an integrated manufacturer-controller-deployer, the CRA-side user-facing instructions are independent of the GDPR workforce awareness programme (DPO-catalysed workforce) and the NIS 2 hygiene baseline on the manufacturer workforce (substantively scope-disjoint audiences — workforce vs end-user).', 'For a CRA-regulated manufacturer, the workforce awareness obligation is discharged via NIS 2 / DORA / GDPR; the parallel tracks coexist on substantively scope-disjoint audiences.'] anchors=['Annex I', 'Annex II', 'Annex VII (Annex II §8(f)', 'Art. 13(18)', '§4', '§8'] csf=['PR.AT-01']

id='SO-D-08.1.DORA' yaml_id='SO-D-08.1.DORA' regulation='DORA' subdomain_id='D-08.1' applies_to='[DORA]' inherits_from='SO-DORA-015' source_SR='SR-DORA-025' activation='if DORA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Financial entities develop ICT security awareness programmes and digital operational resilience training as compulsory modules in their staff training schemes, with a level of complexity commensurate to the remit of their functions (Art. 13(6) DORA).' considerations=['The Art. 13(6) workforce training duty is the workforce-scale counterpart to Art. 5(4) management-body training (governance track, mapped to D-08.3) and to the digital operational resilience testing duty at Chapter IV.', 'The clause co-exists with GDPR Art. 39 staff-awareness duties for personal-data processing and with NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(g) first-clause basic security training baselines. EBA Guidelines on ICT and security risk management set out the supervisory expectation on calibration.', 'The chosen reading of `compulsory` is completion-mandatory (not mere attendance) per SR-DORA-025 ambiguity_notes; the chosen reading of `level of complexity commensurate to the remit of their functions` is function-specific calibration per the OJ literal formulation.', 'PR.AT-01 anchors the baseline awareness layer that closes the human-factor gap — phishing recognition, social-engineering resistance, password hygiene, incident-reporting reflexes — and converts the OJ `ICT security awareness programmes` from an opt-in CPD activity into a compulsory training-module floor across the workforce.', 'PR.AT-02 layers the role-specific depth dimension for staff in security-critical roles (incident response, ICT operations, fraud investigation, third-party governance) — distinct from the uniform baseline.', 'For an integrated financial-entity-controller, the DORA programme is the carrier and the GDPR data-protection awareness is the module (per CRDA-deep §D-08.1 GDPR↔DORA verified relationship).', 'For DORA financial entities that are also NSIEs, DORA-dominant for the workforce awareness dimension (Art. 13(6) `compulsory modules` is more prescriptive than NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(g) first clause `basic cyber hygiene` which is entity-discretionary under Recital 56 — per CRDA-deep §D-08.1 NIS2↔DORA EQUAL classification).', 'For a DORA financial entity that is also a CRA manufacturer, the DORA workforce training is independent of the CRA Annex II §8(a)–(f) user-facing instructions (substantively scope-disjoint audiences — internal staff vs external end-user — no consolidation rule applies).'] anchors=['Annex II', 'Art. 13(6)', 'Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 39', 'Art. 5(4)', '§8'] csf=['PR.AT-01', 'PR.AT-02']

layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-08.2 Role-Specific Competence
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl: id='SO-D-08.2.HL' subdomain_id='D-08.2' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source=None verified_relationship_basis=None emergent_tensions=None objective='Role-specific competence is established through a function-specific depth, audience-routing, competence-criteria-anchored training, and governance hooks architecture.' considerations=['5 of 5 regulations participate (GDPR, NIS 2, CRA, DORA, AI Act — all 5 participate).', "GDPR Art. 39(1)(b) `monitor compliance with this Regulation, including the assignment of responsibilities, awareness-raising and training of staff involved in processing operations` — DPO-catalysed role-specific training for processing staff with data-subject-facing or access-management responsibilities, on the controller's processing-staff audience.", 'NIS 2 Art. 20(2) sentence 2 `offer similar training to their employees on a regular basis, in order that they gain sufficient knowledge and skills to identify risks and assess cybersecurity risk-management practices` — Member-State-encouraged employee training on risk-identification capability (binding force on the Member State rather than directly on the entity per SR-NIS2-030).', 'CRA Annex II §8(f) `where the product is intended for integration into other products, the information necessary for the integrator to comply with the essential cybersecurity requirements set out in Part I of Annex I and the documentation requirements set out in Annex VII` — integrator-facing B2B information for Annex I compliance by the integrator — **partial coverage** per AEGIS taxonomy §4.1.', 'DORA Art. 13(6) `commensurate to the remit of their functions` — financial-entity function-specific-depth training, on the financial-entity workforce with function-specific depth audience.', 'AI Act Art. 14(4)(a)–(e) 5-element closed-list (properly understand; remain aware of automation bias; correctly interpret; decide not to use / disregard / override / reverse; intervene on operation or interrupt) + Art. 26(2) `competence, training AND authority AND support` 4-element AND — AI Act human-overseer 5-element + 4-element competence set, on the high-risk-AI human-overseer audience within the deployer organization (provider-side Art. 14 design + deployer-side Art. 26(2) assignment).', '10 pairwise cells in 5×5 matrix: 5 verified by CRDA as SAME (3 SAME — COMPLEMENTARY: GDPR↔NIS2, NIS2↔DORA, NIS2↔AI_Act; 1 SAME — EQUAL: NIS2↔DORA on workforce awareness at entity level; 1 SAME — DIFFERENT-PERSPECTIVE: GDPR↔AI_Act on same natural person as both data-processing staff and AI human overseer); 5 CRDA-omitted pairs with Executor-recommended classifications (4 SCOPE-DISJOINT on different-audiences: GDPR↔CRA, NIS2↔CRA, CRA↔DORA, CRA↔AI_Act — workforce / encouraged-employee / financial-entity-workforce / AI-human-overseer vs B2B integrator; 1 COMPLEMENTARY: GDPR↔DORA — DORA programme as carrier + GDPR role-specific module on DORA financial entity = controller).', 'The high-level SO engages on the Y-pairs integrated stack when ≥2 regs are applicable: GDPR↔NIS2 (Conditional Y on controller-NSIE adopting Member-State encouragement); GDPR↔DORA (Y on DORA financial entity = controller with role-specific staff — DORA programme as carrier + GDPR role-specific module); GDPR↔AI_Act (Conditional Y on same natural person as both data-processing staff and AI human overseer); NIS2↔DORA (Y on DORA financial entity = NSIE applying role-specific training — DORA-dominant for financial entities); NIS2↔AI_Act (Y on NSIE deploys high-risk AI and assigns human oversight — NIS 2 risk-identification baseline + AI Act 5-element competence stack); DORA↔AI_Act (Y on DORA financial entity deploys high-risk AI — DORA `commensurate to the remit` carrier + AI Act 5-element sub-component).', 'The 4 CRA-involving pairs operate on substantively scope-disjoint audiences (internal workforce / Member-State-encouraged employee / financial-entity workforce / AI human overseer vs B2B integrator) — the parallel tracks coexist with no consolidation rule; the high-level SO does NOT collapse the audience boundaries.', 'For a 5-FTE SaaS startup with GDPR + CRA applicability, the two parallel training-programme tracks must be maintained separately (substantively scope-disjoint audiences — GDPR workforce role-specific training is independent of the CRA Annex II §8(f) integrator-facing information).', 'The per-reg target role, trigger, anchor, threshold, evidence template, recipient are preserved verbatim in the five sub-SOs.'] anchors=['Annex I', 'Annex II', 'Annex VII', 'Art. 13(6)', 'Art. 14', 'Art. 14(4)', 'Art. 20(2)', 'Art. 26(2)', 'Art. 39(1)', '§4', '§8'] csf=[] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto  # activates when ≥2 applicable regs have ≥1 pair with Y scope overlap on the same party AND ≥1 sub-SO activates; for D-08.2 the 5 Y-pairs (GDPR↔NIS2 conditional, GDPR↔DORA recommended, GDPR↔AI_Act conditional, NIS2↔DORA, NIS2↔AI_Act, DORA↔AI_Act) cover all 5 participating regulators; the 4 N-pairs (GDPR↔CRA, NIS2↔CRA, CRA↔DORA, CRA↔AI_Act) are substantively scope-disjoint on different audiences; once ≥2 regs are applicable the high-level SO engages on the joint-condition operator on the Y-pairs integrated stack'

considerations=['The role-specific dimension targets staff with data-subject-facing or access-management responsibilities — distinct from the general awareness programme at D-08.1.', 'The chosen role-specific layer — personnel with data-subject-facing, access-management, breach-response or DPO-deputy responsibilities need role-specific reinforcement of their GDPR and cybersecurity obligations, distinct from the general awareness programme.', 'The role-specific depth is documented under Art. 5(2) accountability on the controller side — the controller must demonstrate that the Art. 39(1)(b) DPO-catalysed role-specific training was operationally exercised and recorded on the day of any supervisory inspection.', 'For an integrated controller-NSIE adopting Member-State encouragement, the GDPR role-specific layer stacks with the NIS 2 Member-State-encouraged employee risk-identification training on the same workforce (Conditional Y per CRDA-deep §D-08.2 GDPR↔NIS2 verified relationship).', 'For a DORA financial entity that is a controller processing personal data with role-specific staff, the DORA Art. 13(6) `commensurate to the remit` programme is the carrier and the GDPR Art. 39(1)(b) DPO-catalysed role-specific training is the module (per CRDA-deep §D-08.2 GDPR↔DORA Executor-recommended COMPLEMENTARY classification).', 'For an AI Act deployer-controller with the same natural person as both data-processing staff and AI human overseer, the AI Act Art. 14(4) + Art. 26(2) layer is the additional competence dimension on top of the GDPR role-specific training (Conditional Y per CRDA-deep §D-08.2 GDPR↔AI_Act verified relationship).', 'For a CRA-regulated manufacturer that is also a controller, the GDPR role-specific workforce training is independent of the CRA Annex II §8(f) integrator-facing information (substantively scope-disjoint audiences — workforce vs B2B integrator — per CRDA-deep §D-08.2 GDPR↔CRA Executor-recommended SCOPE-DISJOINT classification — no consolidation rule applies).'] anchors=['Annex II', 'Art. 13(6)', 'Art. 14(4)', 'Art. 26(2)', 'Art. 39(1)', 'Art. 5(2)', '§8'] csf=['PR.AT-02']

id='SO-D-08.2.NIS2' yaml_id='SO-D-08.2.NIS2' regulation='NIS2' subdomain_id='D-08.2' applies_to='[NIS2]' inherits_from='SO-NIS2-019' source_SR='SR-NIS2-030' activation='if NIS2 in applicable_regs  # entity-side SR applies to entities that adopt the Member-State encouragement (Orchestrator-recommended treatment per SR-NIS2-030 ambiguity_notes)' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Member States shall encourage essential and important entities to offer similar training to their employees on a regular basis, in order that they gain sufficient knowledge and skills to identify risks and assess cybersecurity risk-management practices (Art. 20(2) sentence 2 NIS 2).' considerations=['The binding force of Art. 20(2) sentence 2 is on the Member State rather than directly on the entity (Orchestrator-recommended treatment per SR-NIS2-030 ambiguity_notes) — the entity-side SR applies to entities that adopt the encouragement.', 'The cross-link to Art. 20(2) sentence 1 anchors the purpose clause: training must equip employees to identify risks and assess cybersecurity risk-management practices, the same purpose clause that governs the management-body training in SR-NIS2-031.', 'The chosen reading of `shall encourage` is the cumulative reading (national policy + financial incentives + sectoral guidance + all) since the OJ is silent on the encouragement mechanism (per SR-NIS2-030 ambiguity_notes).', 'The compound `similar training` admits a parallel-to-management-training reading — the chosen reading is literal (parallel-to-management-training because the OJ coordinates sentence 2 with sentence 1 within the same paragraph).', 'The temporal anchor `on a regular basis` is entity-discretionary under Recital 56.', 'PR.AT-01 anchors the recurring training content (phishing, social engineering, password discipline, threat-recognition capability — per SR-NIS2-030 security_rationale).', "PR.AT-02 anchors the role-specific dimension — each employee understands how their own role contributes to the entity's cybersecurity objectives — supporting the OJ's purpose clause that employees must `gain sufficient knowledge and skills to identify risks and assess cybersecurity risk-management practices`.", 'For an integrated controller-NSIE adopting Member-State encouragement, the NIS 2 Member-State-encouraged employee risk-identification training stacks with the GDPR Art. 39(1)(b) DPO-catalysed role-specific training on the same workforce (Conditional Y per CRDA-deep §D-08.2 GDPR↔NIS2 verified id='SO-D-08.2.CRA' yaml_id='SO-D-08.2.CRA' regulation='CRA' subdomain_id='D-08.2' applies_to='[CRA]' inherits_from='SO-CRA-048 (partial via SR-CRA-108 Annex II §8(f))' source_SR='SR-CRA-108' activation='if CRA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Where the product with digital elements is intended for integration into other products with digital elements, the manufacturer provides the information necessary for the integrator to comply with the essential cybersecurity requirements set out in Part I of Annex I and the documentation requirements set out in Annex VII (Annex II §8(f) CRA).' considerations=['The clause sits within the Annex II user-information package; it is the supply-chain-facing counterpart to the §8(a)–(e) user-facing instructions.', "The CRA participation at D-08.2 is partial: Annex II §8(f) addresses the integrator-B2B audience — not the manufacturer's or operator's workforce. id='SO-D-08.2.DORA' yaml_id='SO-D-08.2.DORA' regulation='DORA' subdomain_id='D-08.2' applies_to='[DORA]' inherits_from='SO-DORA-015 (partial via Art. 13(6) `commensurate to the remit`)' source_SR='SR-DORA-025' activation='if DORA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Financial entities develop ICT security awareness programmes and digital operational resilience training as compulsory modules in their staff training schemes, with a level of complexity commensurate to the remit of their functions (Art. 13(6) DORA).' considerations=['The role-specific layer of the Art. 13(6) workforce training duty is anchored on `commensurate to the remit of their functions` — function-specific depth on the workforce (D-08.2 layer), distinct from the baseline awareness programme at D-08.1.', 'The chosen reading of `level of complexity commensurate to the remit of their functions` is function-specific calibration per the OJ literal formulation (per SR-DORA-025 ambiguity_notes).', '**T4-vs-text gap awareness:** T4 reads `role-specific training` but the OJ Art. 13(6) uses only `commensurate to the remit of their functions` (per SR-DORA-025 ambiguity_notes); the Executor keeps the OJ-literal locus.', 'PR.AT-02 layers the role-specific depth dimension — staff in security-critical roles (incident response, ICT operations, fraud investigation, third-party governance) receive calibrated depth rather than a uniform baseline. activation='if AI_Act in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='High-risk AI systems are designed and developed in such a way, including with appropriate human-machine interface tools, that they can be effectively overseen by natural persons during the period in which they are in use (Art. 14(1) AI Act) — the provider-side design obligation for the human-oversight capability.' considerations=['The natural persons assigned to human oversight are enabled, as appropriate and proportionate, to discharge the 5 cumulative abilities of Art. 14(4): (a) properly understand the relevant capacities and limitations of the high-risk AI system and foreseeable misuse; (b) remain aware of automation bias; (c) correctly interpret the output; (d) decide not to use the high-risk AI system or to disregard, override or reverse its output; (e) intervene on the operation or interrupt the system through a stop button or similar procedure.', 'The 5-element closed list is AND-coordinated (all five must be enabled cumulatively — partial compliance is non-compliance per SR-AI_Act-013 ambiguity_notes).', 'On the deployer-side assignment obligation, deployers of high-risk AI systems assign human oversight to natural persons who have the necessary competence, training and authority, as well as the necessary support (Art. 26(2) AI Act) — the 4-element AND `competence, training AND authority AND support` (all four required per SR-AI_Act-020 ambiguity_notes).', 'The provider-design-by-design + deployer-assignment-on-deployment twin-trigger is the AI-Act-specific competence architecture.', 'PR.AT-02 anchors the role-understanding dimension — the workforce-supplier analog of `properly understand` (Art. 14(4)(a)) and `correctly interpret` (Art. 14(4)(c)).', 'PR.AT-01 anchors the awareness-and-training substrate — `remain aware of automation bias` (Art. 14(4)(b)) + `decide` (Art. 14(4)(d)) + `intervene` (Art. 14(4)(e)) require overseers to detect and respond to AI-specific failure modes including the cognitive-bias correction that `automation bias` operationalises.', 'GV.RR-02 supplies the RACI substrate — overseers must hold formal authority to override and interrupt the system.', 'For an integrated GDPR-controller deployer with the same natural person as both data-processing staff and AI human overseer, the AI Act Art. 14(4) + Art. 26(2) layer is the additional competence dimension on top of the GDPR role-specific training (Conditional Y per CRDA-deep §D-08.2 GDPR↔AI_Act verified relationship).', 'For NSIEs deploying high-risk AI and assigning human oversight, the NIS 2 Art. 20(2) sentence 2 employee risk-identification training stacks with the AI Act Art. 14(4) + Art. 26(2) human-overseer 5-element + 4-element AND competence (per CRDA-deep §D-08.2 NIS2↔AI_Act verified relationship).', 'For DORA financial entities deploying high-risk AI, the DORA Art. 13(6) `commensurate to the remit` programme is the carrier and the AI Act Art. 14(4) + Art. 26(2) human-overseer 5-element + 4-element AND competence is the sub-component (per CRDA-deep §D-08.2 DORA↔AI_Act verified relationship).', 'For a CRA-regulated manufacturer that is also an AI Act provider, the CRA Annex II §8(f) integrator-facing information is independent of the AI Act Art. 14(4) + Art. 26(2) human-overseer competence (substantively scope-disjoint audiences — B2B integrator vs AI-overseer role within deployer organization — per CRDA-deep §D-08.2 CRA↔AI_Act Executor-recommended SCOPE-DISJOINT classification — no consolidation rule applies).'] anchors=['Annex II', 'Art. 13(6)', 'Art. 14(1)', 'Art. 14(4)', 'Art. 20(2)', 'Art. 26(2)', '§8'] csf=['GV.RR-02', 'PR.AT-01', 'PR.AT-02']
