layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-08.3 Management Board Training
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl: id='SO-D-08.3.HL' subdomain_id='D-08.3' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source=None verified_relationship_basis=None emergent_tensions=None objective='Management bodies of essential and important entities (NIS 2) and financial entities (DORA) maintain an executive-literacy substrate with documented training records, governance competence, and personal-capacity threshold for approve+oversee+liable governance duties through a management-body training programme.' considerations=['2 of 5 regulations participate (NIS 2, DORA); GDPR, CRA, AI Act are fully absent per CRDA-deep §D-08.3 (GDPR has no management-board training mandate; CRA has no management-board training mandate; AI Act does not impose a management-board-training mandate per CRDA — but AI Act Art. 4 AI literacy may extend management-body competence to AI risk literacy for entities deploying high-risk AI in NIS-critical / ICT-risk contexts, and the interplay is **unresolved per CRDA** as a structural Layer 2 review item).', 'NIS 2 Art. 20(2) sentence 1 `Member States shall ensure that members of the management bodies of essential and important entities are required to follow training, in order that they gain sufficient knowledge and skills to identify risks and assess cybersecurity risk-management practices and their impact on the services provided by the entity` — Member-State-imposed literacy prerequisite for Art. 20(1) approve+oversee+liable governance duties (binding force on the MS, with entity-side SR applying only where the MS has transposed, per SR-NIS2-031 ambiguity_notes).', 'DORA Art. 5(4) `Members of the management body shall actively keep up to date with sufficient knowledge and skills to enable them to understand and assess ICT risk and its impact on the operations of the financial entity, including by following specific training on a regular basis, commensurate to the ICT risk being managed` — direct entity-side obligation with `actively keep up to date` + `regular basis` + `commensurate to the ICT risk`, the literacy underpinning of Art. 5(2) management-body responsibility.', '1 pairwise cell verified by CRDA-deep as SAME — EQUAL — both regulations impose management-body training with the same operative target (senior-executive literacy + governance competence) and the same CSF substrate (PR.AT-03 + GV.RR-01); the dominant-authority reading (DORA-dominant for DORA financial entities; NIS 2-dominant for non-financial NSIEs) is the operational consequence of the DORA-direct-applicability vs NIS 2-MS-transposition asymmetry.', 'The high-level SO engages on the Y-pair integrated stack when the DORA financial entity is also an NSIE applying management-body training.', '**The CRDA-unresolved interplay note** (AI Act Art. 4 may extend management-body competence to AI risk literacy for entities deploying high-risk AI) is preserved as a structural Layer 2 review item; the high-level SO does NOT collapse the CRDA-unresolved interplay into a presumed EQUAL or CONTRADICTORY classification; the AI Act Art. 4 layer is documented as an unresolved parallel-but-unmapped obligation that may add a sub-component to the management-body syllabus without a standalone management-body training mandate.', '0 conditional emergent tensions — no CONTRADICTORY or CORRECTED reclassifications on the management-body training duty itself.', 'The per-reg binding-force locus, target audience, trigger, anchor, threshold, recipient, and evidence template are preserved verbatim in the two sub-SOs.'] anchors=['Art. 20(1)', 'Art. 20(2)', 'Art. 4', 'Art. 5(2)', 'Art. 5(4)'] csf=['GV.RR-01', 'PR.AT-03'] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto  # activates when ≥2 applicable regs have ≥1 pair with Y scope overlap on the same party AND ≥1 sub-SO activates; for D-08.3 the 1 verified pair (NIS2↔DORA = SAME — EQUAL, Y scope overlap when the DORA financial entity is also an NSIE) is the only pair in the 2×2 matrix; the high-level SO engages on the joint-condition operator on the Y-pair integrated stack. For entities with only NIS 2 applicability (non-financial NSIE) or only DORA applicability (non-NSIE financial entity), the high-level SO is redundant in this case but is still emitted for traceability. For entities with neither NIS 2 nor DORA applicability, the high-level SO is NOT activated.'
hso_per_reg: id='SO-D-08.3.NIS2' yaml_id='SO-D-08.3.NIS2' regulation='NIS2' subdomain_id='D-08.3' applies_to='[NIS2]' inherits_from='SO-NIS2-020' source_SR='SR-NIS2-031' activation='if NIS2 in applicable_regs  # entity-side SR applies to entities that have an MS-transposed Member-State obligation under Art. 20(2) sentence 1; the standard MS-implementation pattern is the both reading (statute mandates, entity operationalises), per SR-NIS2-031 ambiguity_notes' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Member States shall ensure that members of the management bodies of essential and important entities are required to follow training, in order that they gain sufficient knowledge and skills to identify risks and assess cybersecurity risk-management practices and their impact on the services provided by the entity (Art. 20(2) sentence 1 NIS 2).' considerations=['The training obligation is structurally the literacy prerequisite for the Article 20(1) management-body obligations (approve, oversee, can be held liable under SR-NIS2-032/033/034): without trained members, the management body cannot meaningfully discharge the approve-and-oversee obligations or be held accountable for infringements (per SR-NIS2-031 regulatory_rationale).', 'The purpose clause anchors two distinct knowledge objects (identify risks; assess cybersecurity risk-management practices) and a third impact object (impact on the services provided), which together define the syllabus scope without prescribing specific content.', "The Member-State implementation determines whether the training is statutory (statute-imposed curriculum), entity-internal (entity's own programme), or both; the chosen reading is the both reading as the standard MS-implementation pattern (per SR-NIS2-031 ambiguity_notes).", 'The binding force of Art. 20(2) sentence 1 is on the Member State (`Member States shall ensure`); the entity-side SR applies only where the Member State has transposed.', "The construction `are required to follow training` carries an S3 ambiguity on the binding-force locus — a statutory reading, an entity-internal reading, or a both reading — with the chosen reading being the both reading since the OJ's literal `are required to follow` is compatible with either locus.", 'The compound `training` admits three operative readings (formal certified programme, awareness briefing, or tabletop exercise), with the chosen reading being entity-discretionary, with formal certified training preferred where the entity seeks documented compliance evidence (per SR-NIS2-031 ambiguity_notes).', 'The scope `members of the management bodies` admits three readings (every member individually, the body collectively, or a designated subset), with the literal reading being every member individually because the OJ does not provide a designation carve-out; the definition of `management body` is Member-State-determined under Article 6 (Recital 75).', 'The qualifier `sufficient knowledge and skills` admits a general-management or cybersecurity-specific reading, with the cybersecurity-specific reading being dominant because the OJ coordinates it with `cybersecurity risk-management practices`.', "PR.AT-03 (All senior executives understand their roles and responsibilities in achieving the organization's cybersecurity objectives) anchors the executive-literacy substrate: management-body members individually possess sufficient knowledge to identify risks and assess cybersecurity risk-management practices, with documented evidence of training completion.", 'GV.RR-01 (Organizational leadership is responsible and accountable for cybersecurity risk and promotes a risk-aware ethical culture) anchors the leadership-culture substrate: trained members exercise the approve-and-oversee obligations of Article 20(1) with informed judgement and accept personal liability exposure under Article 20(1) sentence 1 third clause on a substantively-informed basis.', 'For an integrated controller-NSIE with both NIS 2 and DORA applicability on the management-body-training substrate, the DORA Art. 5(4) programme is the dominant authority (per CRDA-deep §D-08.3 NIS2↔DORA verified relationship: "DORA Art. 5(4) `actively keep up to date` + `commensurate to the ICT risk` discharges both DORA\'s dedicated management-body obligation and NIS 2\'s Member-State-imposed Art. 20(2) sentence 1 literacy prerequisite for DORA financial entities").', 'For a non-financial NSIE that is not a financial entity (NIS 2 only), only the NIS 2 sub-SO activates and the management-body training is discharged against the Art. 20(2) sentence 1 Member-State-imposed literacy prerequisite with the MS-supervised evidence trail.', '**The CRDA-unresolved interplay note** (AI Act Art. 4 may extend management-body competence to AI risk literacy for entities deploying high-risk AI in NIS-critical contexts) is preserved as a structural Layer 2 review item; the HSO does NOT collapse the CRDA-unresolved interplay into a presumed reclassification.'] anchors=['Art. 20(2)', 'Art. 4', 'Art. 5(4)', 'Article 20(1)', 'Article 6'] csf=['GV.RR-01', 'PR.AT-03']

id='SO-D-08.3.DORA' yaml_id='SO-D-08.3.DORA' regulation='DORA' subdomain_id='D-08.3' applies_to='[DORA]' inherits_from='SO-DORA-014' source_SR='SR-DORA-024' activation='if DORA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_N' verified_relationship=None objective='Members of the management body shall actively keep up to date with sufficient knowledge and skills to enable them to understand and assess ICT risk and its impact on the operations of the financial entity, including by following specific training on a regular basis, commensurate to the ICT risk being managed (Art. 5(4) DORA).' considerations=['The clause is the literacy underpinning of Art. 5(2) management-body responsibility (`define, approve, oversee and be responsible for the implementation of all arrangements related to the ICT risk management framework`) and defines the personal-capacity threshold for Art. 5(2) to operate meaningfully (per SR-DORA-024 regulatory_rationale).', 'The clause co-exists with EBA Guidelines on Internal Governance and with the fit-and-proper frameworks (CRD Art. 91, MiFID II Art. 4(1)(36)/(37) cross-reference); for smaller entities under Art. 4 proportionality, training evidence can be proportionate to risk exposure.', 'The OJ-literal anchor is direct (Art. 5(4) is the entity-side obligation — `shall actively keep up to date`); the binding force is on the financial entity, not on a Member State.', 'S2 VAG on `sufficient` is read at the role-relevant-competency end of the spectrum per the `commensurate to the ICT risk` qualifier (per SR-DORA-024 ambiguity_notes).', 'S2 VAG on `regular basis` is read as risk-driven cadence per the literal `actively keep up to date` formulation (alternatives include scheduled or ongoing).', 'S2 VAG on `commensurate to the ICT risk` — the chosen reading is risk-proportional rather than risk-quantified.', 'S2 POLY on `actively keep up to date` — alternatives include self-study, formal training, or both; layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl: id='SO-D-09.1.HL' subdomain_id='D-09.1' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source=None verified_relationship_basis=None emergent_tensions=None objective="Information security policies are established through a **documented policy architecture** with **governance hooks** and an **accountability chain** that anchor the entity's cybersecurity posture." considerations=['5 of 5 regulations participate with **distinct anchors and governance bodies** — GDPR (Art. 24(1) + Art. 5(2) + DPO Art. 37-39 — controller-side data-protection policies with DPO as governance anchor), NIS 2 (Art. 20(1) + Art. 21(2)(a)+(f) — entity-level policy artefacts with management-body approve/oversee/liable architecture), CRA (Art. 24(1) OSS-steward + Art. 13(8) manufacturer + Art. 27(1)/(2)/(5)/(8)/(9) presumption-of-conformity machinery), DORA (Art. 5(2) + Art. 6(1) + Art. 6(4) + Art. 7(1) — financial-entity ICT risk-management framework with three-lines-of-defence), AI Act (Art. 17(1) 13-element QMS closed list + Art. 13(1)+(3) transparency-to-deployers).', '**CRDA-deep verified (10 pairs: 9 SAME — COMPLEMENTARY + 1 SAME — EQUAL NIS 2 ↔ DORA on policy + governance dimension, DORA-dominant for financial entities)** — no CORRECTED, no CONTRADICTORY, no scope-disjoint pairs; the high-level SO does NOT collapse any per-reg policy artefact.', '**Most heavily-overlapped sub-domain** with no OJ-level consolidation rule (unlike D-09.2 where CRA Art. 13(4) sentence 2 covers risk-assessment, not policy); Phase 1 entities must build a 5-policy architecture with 5 distinct governance bodies (DPO / management body / manufacturer-OSS-steward / management body / provider) and reconcile the DPO role with the management body in the corporate-governance charter.', '**Scope caveats**: (a) NIS 2 ↔ DORA EQUAL discharges both obligations on the DORA-dominant stack for financial entities; (b) DPO (GDPR) vs. management body (NIS 2 / DORA) interplay is a Layer 1 architecture-mapping item (DPO reports to management body but is not a member per Art. 38(6)); (c) CRA presumption of conformity does not extend cross-regulation — it discharges the CRA conformity-assessment obligation only, not GDPR/NIS 2/DORA policy obligations.'] anchors=['Art. 13(1)', 'Art. 13(4)', 'Art. 13(8)', 'Art. 17(1)', 'Art. 20(1)', 'Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 24(1)', 'Art. 27(1)', 'Art. 37', 'Art. 38(6)', 'Art. 5(2)', 'Art. 6(1)', 'Art. 6(4)', 'Art. 7(1)'] csf=[] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto  # activates when ≥2 applicable regs have ≥1 pair with Y or Conditional-Y-on-same-party scope overlap AND ≥1 sub-SO activates; for D-09.1 the matrix above shows every pair has Y or Conditional-Y activation on the joint-condition operator (no N (typically) scope-disjoint pairs), so the high-level SO engages whenever ≥2 regs are applicable; the 9 SAME — COMPLEMENTARY pairs stack on a layered 5-policy architecture; the 1 SAME — EQUAL pair (NIS 2 ↔ DORA) discharges both obligations on the DORA-dominant stack for financial entities. The high-level SO does NOT collapse any per-reg policy artefact; it surfaces the common documented-policy-architecture duty with the per-reg anchor, governance body, content template, threshold, evidence template, and recipient preserved verbatim in the 5 sub-SOs.'

id='SO-D-09.1.GDPR' yaml_id='SO-D-09.1.GDPR' regulation='GDPR' subdomain_id='D-09.1' applies_to='[GDPR]' inherits_from='SO-GDPR-026 + SO-GDPR-027 + SO-GDPR-037' source_SR='SR-GDPR-043 + SR-GDPR-044 + SR-GDPR-062 + SR-GDPR-063 + SR-GDPR-064' activation='if GDPR in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_5' verified_relationship=None objective="The controller implements **appropriate technical and organisational measures, such as policies … which are designed to implement data-protection principles … in an effective manner** (Art. 24(1) GDPR), with the Art. 5(2) accountability burden and the DPO as the governance anchor (Art. 37-39).

id='SO-D-09.1.NIS2' yaml_id='SO-D-09.1.NIS2' regulation='NIS2' subdomain_id='D-09.1' applies_to='[NIS2]' inherits_from='SO-NIS2-021 + SO-NIS2-022 + SO-NIS2-023' source_SR='SR-NIS2-032 + SR-NIS2-033 + SR-NIS2-034 + SR-NIS2-035 + SR-NIS2-036 + SR-NIS2-037' activation='if NIS2 in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_5' verified_relationship=None objective="The management body of essential and important entities **approves the cybersecurity risk-management measures, oversees their implementation, and can be held liable for infringements** (Art. 20(1) sentence 1 NIS 2); the entity adopts **policies on risk analysis and information system security** (Art. 21(2)(a)) and **policies and procedures to assess the effectiveness of cybersecurity risk-management measures** (Art. 21(2)(f)).

**CSF anchors (from `SR-NIS2-035` + `SR-NIS2-036` + `SR-NIS2-037` v0.3 security_rationale):**
GV.PO-01 (primary), GV.OV-01, GV.PO-02.
*(GV.PO-01 — Organizational cybersecurity policy established, communicated, enforced — anchors the NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(a)+(f) policy artefacts mapped to NIST CSF 2.0 GV.PO-01; GV.OV-01 — Risk management strategy outcomes reviewed — anchors the NIS 2 management-body approve/oversee/liable governance act per DomainAnalysis §D-09.1 line 178 cross-validation; the management body's liability exposure for NIS 2 infringements (Art. 20(1) sentence 1) is the operational evidence layer for the governance hook. The three subcategories together enable the entity to demonstrate ex post, against the Member State transposition, that the Art. 21(2)(a)+(f) policies + Art. 20(1) management-body approval records were established, reviewed, and updated in light of the proportionality factors (degree of exposure; likelihood of incidents; severity of incidents).)*" considerations=[] anchors=['Art. 20(1)', 'Art. 21(2)'] csf=['GV.OV-01', 'GV.PO-01', 'GV.PO-02']

id='SO-D-09.1.CRA' yaml_id='SO-D-09.1.CRA' regulation='CRA' subdomain_id='D-09.1' applies_to='[CRA]' inherits_from='SO-CRA-049 + SO-CRA-050 + SO-CRA-051 + SO-CRA-052' source_SR='SR-CRA-072 + SR-CRA-073 + SR-CRA-075 + SR-CRA-077 + SR-CRA-078' activation='if CRA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_5' verified_relationship=None objective="An open-source software steward **puts in place and documents in a verifiable manner a cybersecurity policy** (Art. 24(1) CRA) covering vulnerability documentation, remediation, and information-sharing within the open-source community; a manufacturer **establishes policies, processes and procedures necessary to implement its CRA cybersecurity obligations** (Art. 13(8) CRA) including CVD policy, secure-update distribution, support-period determination, and cessation-of-operations communication.

**CSF anchors (from `SR-CRA-072` + `SR-CRA-075` + `SR-CRA-077` v0.3 security_rationale):**
GV.PO-01 (primary), GV.PO-02.
*(GV.PO-01 — Organizational cybersecurity policy established, communicated, enforced — anchors the OSS-steward cybersecurity policy (Art. 24(1)) + manufacturer policies/processes/procedures (Art. 13(8)) mapped to NIST CSF 2.0 GV.PO-01. The presumption-of-conformity machinery (Art. 27(1)/(2)/(5)/(8)/(9)) is the upstream gate for the policy object's evidence trail — a CRA-conformant product is presumed to meet the Annex I essential cybersecurity requirements when the manufacturer's processes conform to harmonised standards (Art. 27(1)) or common specifications (Art. 27(2)/(5)) or European cybersecurity certification schemes (Art. 27(8)/(9)). The OSS-steward policy is the workforce-level policy anchor for OSS projects under the steward's umbrella; the manufacturer policies/processes/procedures are the operational policy artefacts for the manufacturer's Annex I compliance chain. The two subcategories together enable the OSS steward / manufacturer to demonstrate ex post, against the market surveillance authority, that the Art. 24(1) OSS-steward policy or Art. 13(8) manufacturer policies were adopted, reviewed, and updated during the support period, with the Art. 27(1)/(2)/(5)/(8)/(9) presumption-of-conformity machinery as the upstream gate. **IMPORTANT — CRA presumption does not extend cross-regulation**: per DomainAnalysis §D-09.1 line 173, CRA presumption of conformity discharges the CRA conformity-assessment obligation only and does not substitute for the GDPR Art. 24(1) appropriate-measures obligation, NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(a)+(f) policy obligation, or DORA Art. 6(1) ICT risk-management framework obligation. Phase 1 entities must discharge each regime's policy obligation separately even when the underlying product is CRA-conformant.)*" considerations=[] anchors=['Annex I', 'Art. 13(8)', 'Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 24(1)', 'Art. 27(1)', 'Art. 27(2)', 'Art. 27(8)', 'Art. 6(1)'] csf=['GV.PO-01', 'GV.PO-02']

id='SO-D-09.1.DORA' yaml_id='SO-D-09.1.DORA' regulation='DORA' subdomain_id='D-09.1' applies_to='[DORA]' inherits_from='SO-DORA-016 + SO-DORA-017' source_SR='SR-DORA-026 + SR-DORA-027 + SR-DORA-028' activation='if DORA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_5' verified_relationship=None objective="The management body of the financial entity **defines, approves, oversees and is responsible for the implementation of all arrangements related to the ICT risk management framework** (Art. 5(2) DORA), supported by a **sound, comprehensive and well-documented ICT risk management framework** (Art. 6(1)) with a three-lines-of-defence model (Art. 6(4)).

**CSF anchors (from `SR-DORA-026` + `SR-DORA-027` + `SR-DORA-028` v0.3 security_rationale):**
GV.PO-01 (primary), GV.RR-02, GV.RM-04.
*(GV.PO-01 — Organizational cybersecurity policy established, communicated, enforced — anchors the DORA Art. 6(1) `sound, comprehensive and well-documented ICT risk management framework` mapped to NIST CSF 2.0 GV.PO-01; GV.RR-02 — Roles/responsibilities/accountabilities established — anchors the DORA Art. 6(4) `three lines of defence model` per DomainAnalysis §D-09.1 line 178 cross-validation; the management-body define/approve/oversee/be-responsible architecture (Art. 5(2) four-verb coordination) extends to all arrangements related to the ICT risk-management framework, with the management body collectively responsible for the framework's implementation. The three subcategories together enable the financial entity to demonstrate ex post, against the national competent authority + EBA supervisory baseline, that the Art. 6(1) ICT risk-management framework + Art. 5(2) management-body oversight + Art. 6(4) three-lines-of-defence architecture were established and maintained in light of the proportionality factors (size, nature, scale, complexity per Art. 4). For DORA financial entities that are also NIS 2 NSIEs, the DORA ICT risk-management framework discharges both obligations — DORA-dominant under DORA's direct scope (EQUAL classification). For DORA financial entities that are also controllers, the GDPR Art. 24(1) data-protection policies become a module within the DORA framework — DORA-led stack with GDPR as module.)*" considerations=[] anchors=['Art. 24(1)', 'Art. 4', 'Art. 5(2)', 'Art. 6(1)', 'Art. 6(4)'] csf=['GV.PO-01', 'GV.RM-04', 'GV.RR-02']

id='SO-D-09.1.AI_Act' yaml_id='SO-D-09.1.AI_Act' regulation='AI_Act' subdomain_id='D-09.1' applies_to='[AI_Act]' inherits_from='SO-AI_Act-007 + SO-AI_Act-010' source_SR='SR-AI_Act-010 + SR-AI_Act-011 + SR-AI_Act-017 + SR-AI_Act-019' activation='if AI_Act in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_5' verified_relationship=None objective="High-risk AI systems are **designed and developed to ensure that their operation is sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret a system's output and use it appropriately** (Art. 13(1) AI Act), accompanied by **concise, complete, correct and clear instructions for use** (Art. 13(3) AI Act); a provider **puts a quality management system in place** documented in written policies, procedures and instructions covering at least the 13 enumerated aspects (a)-(m) (Art. 17(1) AI Act).

**CSF anchors (from `SR-AI_Act-010` + `SR-AI_Act-017` v0.3 security_rationale):**
GV.PO-01 (primary), GV.PO-02.
*(GV.PO-01 — Organizational cybersecurity policy established, communicated, enforced — anchors the AI Act Art. 17(1) QMS documented `in a systematic and orderly manner in the form of written policies, procedures and instructions` mapped to NIST CSF 2.0 GV.PO-01. The 13-element closed list (a)-(m) is the most content-codified of the 5 regulators: it specifies strategies, procedures, and instructions across compliance, design/design control/design verification (per (c)), risk-management-system documentation cross-reference to Art. 9 (per (g)), data quality (per (d) — cross to D-05 Data-Lifecycle), post-market monitoring (per (k) — cross to D-10.1 Continuous Security Monitoring), and other AI-specific controls. The Art. 13(1)+(3) transparency-to-deployers instructions-for-use is the deployer-side policy content delivered alongside the high-risk AI system. The two subcategories together enable the AI Act provider to demonstrate ex post, against the MSA / AI Office supervisory baseline, that the Art. 17(1) QMS documented `written policies, procedures and instructions` were adopted, reviewed, and updated across the AI lifecycle, with the Art. 9 risk-management-system documentation cross-reference operationalising the continuous-iterative risk dimension (cross to D-09.2 — `SR-CRA-066 ambiguity_notes` notes the CRA Art. 13(4) sentence 2 unification rule applies at D-09.2 but not at D-09.1). AI Act Recital 78 explicitly preserves GDPR for personal-data processing, so providers that are also controllers stack the GDPR data-protection policies with the AI Act QMS as a sub-policy.)*" considerations=[] anchors=['Art. 13(1)', 'Art. 13(3)', 'Art. 13(4)', 'Art. 17(1)', 'Art. 9'] csf=['GV.PO-01', 'GV.PO-02']

layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl: id='SO-D-09.2.HL' subdomain_id='D-09.2' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source=None verified_relationship_basis=None emergent_tensions=None objective='Impact and risk assessments are established through a **documented assessment** of identified risks and mitigation measures, with a **review cadence** calibrated to the lifecycle phase of the assessment object.' considerations=['5 of 5 regulations participate with **distinct assessment objects and cadences** — GDPR (Art. 35(1) + Art. 35(7) 4-item content + Art. 35(11) — pre-launch DPIA on data-subject rights, on-change review), NIS 2 (Art. 21(2)(a) + Art. 22(1) — continuous operational risk-analysis policy, all-hazards methodology under Recital 56), CRA (Art. 13(3) + Annex VII §3 — pre-market + support-period cybersecurity risk assessment, on-material-change review), DORA (Art. 6(4) + Art. 7(2) — continuous + at-least-yearly ICT risk framework), AI Act (Art. 9(1) + Art. 9(2)(a)-(d) 4-step — continuous iterative risk-management system across AI lifecycle; Art. 27 FRIA for certain Annex III categories).', '**CRDA-deep verified (10 pairs: 4 SAME — DIFFERENT-PERSPECTIVE all 4 GDPR pairs reflecting pre-launch DPIA vs continuous/iterative asymmetry + 5 SAME — COMPLEMENTARY + 1 SAME — EQUAL NIS 2 ↔ DORA on continuous operational risk identification, DORA-dominant for financial entities)** — no CORRECTED, no CONTRADICTORY, no scope-disjoint pairs; the high-level SO does NOT collapse the 5 distinct assessment regimes.', '**Single OJ-level cross-regulation consolidation rule — CRA Art. 13(4) sentence 2**: `The cybersecurity risk assessment referred to in paragraph 2 shall be part of, or combined with, the risk assessment required by other Union legal acts applicable to the product with digital elements.` For AI-enabled CRA-regulated products, a unified AI Act Art. 9 risk-management system substitutes for the CRA Art. 13(3) cybersecurity risk assessment (per SR-CRA-066 ambiguity_notes) — the only OJ-level consolidation rule in D-09.2. No other cross-regulation substitution is OJ-permitted.', '**Scope caveats**: (a) 5 cadences are not synchronised (pre-launch / continuous / pre-market + support-period / continuous + yearly / continuous iterative) — an entity must satisfy 5 independent review triggers without a unified cadence; (b) GDPR DPIA does NOT address cybersecurity risk per CRDA flag (DomainAnalysis §D-09.2 line 175) — for CRA-regulated products processing personal data, GDPR DPIA must be a separate artefact even when the CRA risk assessment has been performed; (c) NIS 2 ↔ DORA EQUAL discharges both obligations on the DORA-dominant stack for financial entities.'] anchors=['Annex III', 'Annex VII', 'Art. 13(3)', 'Art. 13(4)', 'Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 22(1)', 'Art. 27', 'Art. 35(1)', 'Art. 35(11)', 'Art. 35(7)', 'Art. 6(4)', 'Art. 7(2)', 'Art. 9', 'Art. 9(1)', 'Art. 9(2)', '§3'] csf=[] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto  # activates when ≥2 applicable regs have ≥1 pair with Y or Conditional-Y scope overlap on the same party AND ≥1 sub-SO activates; for D-09.2 the matrix above shows every pair has Y or Conditional-Y activation on the joint-condition operator (no N (typically) scope-disjoint pairs); the 4 SAME — DIFFERENT-PERSPECTIVE pairs (all 4 GDPR pairs) reflect the structural pre-launch DPIA vs continuous / iterative assessment asymmetry; the 5 SAME — COMPLEMENTARY pairs stack on distinct assessment *objects* with no consolidation rule (except the CRA↔AI_Act pair which has the CRA Art. 13(4) sentence 2 OJ-level consolidation rule permitting substitution); the 1 SAME — EQUAL pair (NIS 2 ↔ DORA) discharges both obligations on the DORA-dominant stack for financial entities. The high-level SO does NOT collapse any per-reg assessment regime; it surfaces the common documented-assessment duty with the per-reg assessment object, trigger, content template, threshold, recipient, and review cadence preserved verbatim in the 5 sub-SOs. **The single OJ-level cross-regulation consolidation rule** is CRA Art. 13(4) sentence 2: a unified AI Act Art. 9 risk-management system substitutes for the CRA Art. 13(3) cybersecurity risk assessment when both apply to the same product.'

id='SO-D-09.2.GDPR' yaml_id='SO-D-09.2.GDPR' regulation='GDPR' subdomain_id='D-09.2' applies_to='[GDPR]' inherits_from='SO-GDPR-028 + SO-GDPR-036 + SO-GDPR-037 (cross-ref from D-09.1)' source_SR='SR-GDPR-045 + SR-GDPR-046 + SR-GDPR-047' activation='if GDPR in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_5' verified_relationship=None objective='Prior to processing that is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller carries out a **data-protection impact assessment** covering the four Art. 35(7) content items and reviewed on change of risk per Art. 35(11) (Art. 35(1) + Art. 35(7) GDPR).

**CSF anchors (from `SR-GDPR-045` + `SR-GDPR-046` + `SR-GDPR-047` v0.3 security_rationale):**
ID.RA-05 (primary), ID.RA-04.
*(ID.RA-05 — Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, impacts used to understand inherent risk and inform risk response — anchors the convergent D-09.2 assessment regime across the 5 regulators per DomainAnalysis §D-09.2 line 180 cross-validation; ID.RA-04 — Potential impacts and likelihoods of threats exploiting vulnerabilities are identified and recorded — anchors the DPIA-specific impact-and-likelihood dimension per DomainAnalysis §D-09.2 line 180 cross-validation. The DPIA object — risks to data-subject rights and freedoms — is captured by Art. 35(7)(c) `assessment of the risks to the rights and freedoms of data subjects`; the impact dimension is captured by Art. 35(7)(d) `measures envisaged to address the risks`. The two subcategories together enable the controller to demonstrate ex post, against the Art. 5(2) accountability burden, that the DPIA was carried out prior to processing with the 4-item Art. 35(7) content, reviewed on change of risk per Art. 35(11), and was submitted for prior consultation where the residual risk is high per Art. 36(1). **GDPR DPIA does NOT address cybersecurity risk** — for the cybersecurity dimension, the CRA Art. 13(2) risk assessment (Annex VII §3 risk-assessment record) or the NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(a) risk-analysis policy discharges the cybersecurity-risk-assessment obligation on a separate artefact.)*' considerations=[] anchors=['Annex VII', 'Art. 13(2)', 'Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 35(1)', 'Art. 35(11)', 'Art. 35(7)', 'Art. 36(1)', 'Art. 5(2)', '§3'] csf=['ID.RA-04', 'ID.RA-05']

id='SO-D-09.2.NIS2' yaml_id='SO-D-09.2.NIS2' regulation='NIS2' subdomain_id='D-09.2' applies_to='[NIS2]' inherits_from='SO-NIS2-022 + SO-NIS2-016 + SR-NIS2-028 (Art. 21(1))' source_SR='SR-NIS2-035 + SR-NIS2-039 + SR-NIS2-040' activation='if NIS2 in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_5' verified_relationship=None objective='Essential and important entities establish **policies on risk analysis and information system security** (Art. 21(2)(a) NIS 2) on a continuous basis, taking into account the proportionality factors (degree of exposure, likelihood of incidents, severity, state of the art, costs of implementation per Recital 56); the Cooperation Group may carry out coordinated supply-chain risk assessments under Art. 22(1) NIS 2 that NSIEs take into account per Art. 21(3) sentence 2.

**CSF anchors (from `SR-NIS2-035` + `SR-NIS2-039` + `SR-NIS2-040` v0.3 security_rationale):**
ID.RA-05 (primary), GV.OV-01.
*(ID.RA-05 — Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, impacts used to understand inherent risk and inform risk response — anchors the NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(a) continuous operational risk-analysis policy mapped to NIST CSF 2.0 ID.RA-05. SR-NIS2-040 establishes the **all-hazards methodology** with the proportionality factors (degree of exposure; likelihood of incidents; severity; state of the art; cost of implementation per Recital 56) calibrating the depth. The Cooperation Group coordinated supply-chain assessments per Art. 22(1) are the EU-level coordinated-assessment substrate for NSIEs to incorporate via Art. 21(3) sentence 2. The two subcategories together enable the NSIE to demonstrate ex post, against the Member State transposition + competent authority, that the Art. 21(2)(a) risk-analysis policy is operational continuous with all-hazards methodology, calibrated by the proportionality factors, and incorporates the Art. 22(1) Cooperation Group coordinated assessments.)*' considerations=[] anchors=['Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 21(3)', 'Art. 22(1)'] csf=['GV.OV-01', 'ID.RA-05']

id='SO-D-09.2.CRA' yaml_id='SO-D-09.2.CRA' regulation='CRA' subdomain_id='D-09.2' applies_to='[CRA]' inherits_from='SO-CRA-053 + SO-CRA-054' source_SR='SR-CRA-064 + SR-CRA-065 + SR-CRA-066 + SR-CRA-079 + SR-CRA-080 + SR-CRA-081' activation='if CRA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_5' verified_relationship=None objective='The manufacturer documents the **cybersecurity risk assessment referred to in Art. 13(2)** and updates it as appropriate during the support period, with the assessment covering intended purpose and reasonably foreseeable use (Art. 13(3) sentence 2) and indicating Annex I Part I (2) applicability (Art. 13(3) sentence 3) — documented in the **Annex VII §3 risk-assessment record** (Art. 13(4) sentence 1 + Annex VII §3 CRA).

**CSF anchors (from `SR-CRA-064` + `SR-CRA-065` + `SR-CRA-066` + `SR-CRA-079` v0.3 security_rationale):**
ID.RA-05 (primary), ID.SC-04.
*(ID.RA-05 — Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, impacts used to understand inherent risk and inform risk response — anchors the CRA Art. 13(3) documented-and-updated cybersecurity risk assessment mapped to NIST CSF 2.0 ID.RA-05. ID.SC-04 — Suppliers prioritised by criticality — anchors the supply-chain risk dimension per DomainAnalysis §D-09.2 line 180 cross-validation. The CRA risk assessment covers (1) intended purpose + reasonably foreseeable use (including operational environment and assets to be protected) per Art. 13(3) sentence 2; (2) Annex I Part I (2) applicability mapping per Art. 13(3) sentence 3; (3) technical-documentation inclusion per Art. 13(4) sentence 1; (4) Annex VII §3 risk-assessment record per the documentation requirement. The **CRA Art. 13(4) sentence 2 unification rule** permits the AI Act Art. 9 risk-management system to substitute for the CRA cybersecurity risk assessment when both apply to the same product — for AI-enabled CRA-regulated products, a unified AI Act Art. 9 risk-management system discharges both CRA Art. 13(3) cybersecurity risk assessment and AI Act Art. 9 risk management on a single artefact (per SR-CRA-066 ambiguity_notes). The two subcategories together enable the manufacturer to demonstrate ex post, against the market surveillance authority, that the Art. 13(3) sentence 1 documented-and-updated risk assessment was carried out with Annex VII §3 documentation, Annex I Part I (2) applicability mapping, and updated on material change of risk per Art. 13(3) sentence 1 `updated as appropriate` + Art. 13(7) update-on-becoming-aware-of-vulnerability. **Note — CRA risk assessment does NOT extend to data-subject rights**: per CRDA flag (DomainAnalysis §D-09.2 line 175), the GDPR DPIA on data-subject rights must be a separate artefact even when the CRA cybersecurity risk assessment has been performed.)*' considerations=[] anchors=['Annex I Part I (2)', 'Annex VII', 'Art. 13(2)', 'Art. 13(3)', 'Art. 13(4)', 'Art. 13(7)', 'Art. 9', '§3'] csf=['ID.RA-05', 'ID.SC-04']

id='SO-D-09.2.DORA' yaml_id='SO-D-09.2.DORA' regulation='DORA' subdomain_id='D-09.2' applies_to='[DORA]' inherits_from='SO-DORA-017 + SO-DORA-003' source_SR='SR-DORA-028 + SR-DORA-004 + SR-DORA-005' activation='if DORA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_5' verified_relationship=None objective='Financial entities shall, on a continuous basis, **identify all sources of ICT risk** including risk exposure to and from other financial entities, and **assess cyber threats and ICT vulnerabilities relevant to ICT supported business functions, information assets and ICT assets** (Art. 7(2) sentence 1 DORA); risk scenarios are reviewed on a regular basis, and at least yearly (Art. 7(2) sentence 2), under a three-lines-of-defence model (Art. 6(4) DORA).

**CSF anchors (from `SR-DORA-028` + `SR-DORA-004` + `SR-DORA-005` v0.3 security_rationale):**
ID.RA-05 (primary), GV.RR-02.
*(ID.RA-05 — Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, impacts used to understand inherent risk and inform risk response — anchors the DORA Art. 7(2) sentence 1 continuous ICT risk identification + sentence 2 at-least-yearly risk-scenario review mapped to NIST CSF 2.0 ID.RA-05. The three-lines-of-defence model (Art. 6(4)) provides the governance architecture for the ICT risk identification + asset classification + risk-scenario review chain. The two subcategories together enable the financial entity to demonstrate ex post, against the national competent authority + EBA Guidelines on ICT and security risk management supervisory baseline, that the Art. 7(2) sentence 1 continuous ICT risk identification register + sentence 2 at-least-yearly risk-scenario review records + Art. 6(4) three-lines-of-defence documentation + Art. 7(1) asset identification/classification/documentation chain are maintained on the entity-level operational continuous + at-least-yearly cadence per Art. 4 proportionality. **Note — DORA ICT risk framework does NOT extend to data-subject rights**: per CRDA flag (DomainAnalysis §D-09.2 line 175), the GDPR DPIA on data-subject rights must be a separate artefact even when the DORA ICT risk framework is in place; **DORA has no equivalent to CRA Art. 13(4) sentence 2** — DORA ↔ AI Act pair has no OJ-level consolidation rule. **Note — DORA OJ-literal locus**: the OJ-literal locus for Art. 7(2) sentence 1 + sentence 2 is Art. 8(2) per the SR-DORA-004 / SR-DORA-005 v0.2 audit note; the SR preserves the substantive content of the risk-identification-on-a-continuous-basis + at-least-yearly risk-scenario review obligation.)*' considerations=[] anchors=['Art. 13(4)', 'Art. 4', 'Art. 6(4)', 'Art. 7(1)', 'Art. 7(2)', 'Art. 8(2)'] csf=['GV.RR-02', 'ID.RA-05']

id='SO-D-09.2.AI_Act' yaml_id='SO-D-09.2.AI_Act' regulation='AI_Act' subdomain_id='D-09.2' applies_to='[AI_Act]' inherits_from='SO-AI_Act-001' source_SR='SR-AI_Act-001 + SR-AI_Act-002' activation='if AI_Act in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_5' verified_relationship=None objective='A risk management system is **established, implemented, documented and maintained** in relation to high-risk AI systems (Art. 9(1) AI Act), comprising the four Art. 9(2)(a)-(d) steps: identify and analyse known and reasonably foreseeable risks; estimate and evaluate reasonably-foreseeable-misuse risks; evaluate post-market-monitoring-data risks; and adopt appropriate and targeted risk-management measures.

**CSF anchors (from `SR-AI_Act-001` + `SR-AI_Act-002` v0.3 security_rationale):**
ID.RA-05 (primary), GV.RM-04.
*(ID.RA-05 — Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, impacts used to understand inherent risk and inform risk response — anchors the AI Act Art. 9(1) + Art. 9(2)(a)-(d) continuous iterative risk-management system across AI lifecycle mapped to NIST CSF 2.0 ID.RA-05. GV.RM-04 — Strategic direction for risk response — anchors the continuous-iterative dimension per DomainAnalysis §D-09.2 line 180 cross-validation. The 4-step Art. 9(2)(a)-(d) process — (a) identify/analyse known + reasonably foreseeable risks to health, safety and fundamental rights; (b) estimate/evaluate reasonably-foreseeable-misuse risks; (c) evaluate post-market-monitoring-data risks; (d) adopt appropriate and targeted risk-management measures — defines the AI-system-level continuous iterative assessment methodology. **CRITICAL CONSOLIDATION RULE — CRA Art. 13(4) sentence 2 unification**: for AI-enabled CRA-regulated products, a unified AI Act Art. 9 risk-management system substitutes for the CRA Art. 13(3) cybersecurity risk assessment (per SR-CRA-066 ambiguity_notes); this is the only OJ-level cross-regulation consolidation rule in D-09.2. The two subcategories together enable the AI Act provider / deployer to demonstrate ex post, against the MSA / AI Office + Art. 27 FRIA documentation for certain Annex III categories, that the Art. 9(1) `established, implemented, documented and maintained` risk-management system was carried out across the AI lifecycle with the 4-step Art. 9(2)(a)-(d) process documented and applied to the high-risk AI system, with post-market monitoring integrated per Art. 9(2)(c) and reasonable foreseeability scoping per Art. 9(2)(a) + (b). **Note — AI Act risk management does NOT address data-subject rights**: per CRDA flag (DomainAnalysis §D-09.2 line 175), the GDPR DPIA on data-subject rights must be a separate artefact even when the AI Act Art. 9 risk-management system is in place; AI Act Recital 78 explicit GDPR preservation.)*' considerations=[] anchors=['Annex III', 'Art. 13(3)', 'Art. 13(4)', 'Art. 27', 'Art. 9', 'Art. 9(1)', 'Art. 9(2)'] csf=['GV.RM-04', 'ID.RA-05']

layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl: id='SO-D-09.3.HL' subdomain_id='D-09.3' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source=None verified_relationship_basis=None emergent_tensions=None objective='Asset inventories are established through a **documented entity-level asset inventory** with **identification + classification + documentation** of ICT supported business functions, information assets, ICT assets, and their roles and dependencies.' considerations=['**3 of 5 regulations participate** (NIS 2, CRA, DORA — **GDPR + AI Act explicitly out-of-scope** per CRDA). NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(i) provides **partial coverage** via access-control coordination (asset-management is one of three coordinated sub-domains of access control); CRA Annex VII §1-§2 provides **partial coverage** (documentation-centric — general description + architecture description, not a formal asset register in the DORA sense); **DORA Art. 7(1) is the dedicated authority** with explicit OJ-literal `3-way AND` of ICT supported business functions + information assets + ICT assets + roles + dependencies.', '**CRDA-deep verified (3 pairs: 1 SAME — COMPLEMENTARY NIS 2 ↔ CRA — substantively scope-disjoint per CRDA `N (typically)`, different objects (entity asset register vs. product architecture documentation), CRDA `complementary` is a taxonomy artifact; + 1 SAME — EQUAL NIS 2 ↔ DORA on entity-level asset inventory, DORA-dominant; + 1 SAME — COMPLEMENTARY CRA ↔ DORA, Conditional-Y when DORA entity procures CRA-conformant products)** — no CORRECTED, no CONTRADICTORY. The high-level SO does NOT collapse the entity-level asset register with the product-level architecture documentation.', '**DORA sole-authority flag (per AEGIS taxonomy §4.1, OJ-literal)** distinguishes D-09.3 from D-07.2 where the sole-authority assignment is OJ-text-unsupported; NIS 2 and CRA provide partial coverage only.', '**Scope caveats**: (a) NIS 2 ↔ CRA substantively scope-disjoint (entity asset register vs. product architecture documentation) — different audit purposes (entity-level NCA review vs. product-level MSA review), the two regimes meet only at the supplier-customer interface; (b) NIS 2 ↔ DORA EQUAL discharges both on the DORA-dominant stack for financial entities; (c) CRA ↔ DORA is DORA-led with CRA Annex VII §1-§2 as upstream product-level sub-register feeding the DORA entity-level master record.'] anchors=['Annex VII', 'Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 7(1)', '§1', '§2', '§4'] csf=[] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto  # activates when ≥2 applicable regs have ≥1 pair with Y or Conditional-Y-on-same-party scope overlap AND ≥1 sub-SO activates; for D-09.3 the matrix above shows 2 pairs with Y or Conditional-Y activation on the joint-condition operator (NIS2↔DORA = Y; CRA↔DORA = Conditional-Y when DORA entity procures CRA-conformant products). The NIS2↔CRA pair is **substantively scope-disjoint per CRDA `N (typically)`** so it does **NOT** engage the high-level SO on its own — the high-level SO engages on the NIS2↔DORA EQUAL pair (DORA-dominant stack) and/or the CRA↔DORA COMPLEMENTARY pair (DORA-led stack with CRA Annex VII §1-§2 as upstream product sub-register). The high-level SO does NOT collapse any per-reg asset-inventory artefact; it surfaces the common entity-level asset-inventory duty with DORA Art. 7(1) as the dedicated authority for DORA financial entities and NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(i) + CRA Annex VII §1-§2 as partial-coverage inputs.'

id='SO-D-09.3.NIS2' yaml_id='SO-D-09.3.NIS2' regulation='NIS2' subdomain_id='D-09.3' applies_to='[NIS2]' inherits_from='SO-NIS2-003 + SO-NIS2-021 (cross)' source_SR='SR-NIS2-005' activation='if NIS2 in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_3' verified_relationship=None objective='Essential and important entities adopt **access control policies coordinated with human resources security and asset management** (Art. 21(2)(i) NIS 2), with the management body approving, overseeing, and being liable for the cybersecurity risk-management measures (Art. 20(1) sentence 1 NIS 2).

**CSF anchors (from `SR-NIS2-005` v0.3 security_rationale):**
PR.PS-01 (primary), ID.AM-01, ID.AM-02.
*(PR.PS-01 — Configuration management practices established — anchors the NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(i) asset-management coordinated-with-access-control sub-domain mapped to NIST CSF 2.0 PR.PS-01 per CRDA DomainAnalysis §D-09.3 line 86 cross-validation; ID.AM-01 — Inventories of hardware managed within the system — and ID.AM-02 — Inventories of software, services, and systems managed — are the convergent NIST CSF 2.0 subcategories for the entity-level hardware + software + services + systems inventory per CRDA DomainAnalysis §D-09.3 line 86. The three subcategories together enable the NSIE to demonstrate ex post, against the Member State competent authority, that the Art. 21(2)(i) asset-management sub-domain — coordinated with access control — is established, reviewed, and updated in light of the proportionality factors (degree of exposure; likelihood of incidents; severity per Recital 56).)*' considerations=[] anchors=['Art. 20(1)', 'Art. 21(2)'] csf=['ID.AM-01', 'ID.AM-02', 'PR.PS-01']

id='SO-D-09.3.CRA' yaml_id='SO-D-09.3.CRA' regulation='CRA' subdomain_id='D-09.3' applies_to='[CRA]' inherits_from='SO-CRA-061' source_SR='SR-CRA-087 + SR-CRA-088' activation='if CRA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='2_of_3' verified_relationship=None objective='Manufacturers of products with digital elements draw up **technical documentation** containing at least a **general description** of the product (Annex VII §1) and a **description of the design, development, production and vulnerability-handling processes** including the system architecture description (Annex VII §2); the technical documentation is drawn up before placing on the market and updated during the support period (Art. 31(2) CRA), and kept at the disposal of market surveillance authorities for at least 10 years or the support period, whichever is longer (Art. 13(13) CRA).

**CSF anchors (from `SR-CRA-087` + `SR-CRA-088` v0.3 security_rationale):**
ID.AM-01, ID.AM-02.
*(ID.AM-01 — Inventories of hardware managed within the system — and ID.AM-02 — Inventories of software, services, and systems managed — are the convergent NIST CSF 2.0 subcategories per CRDA DomainAnalysis §D-09.3 line 86 cross-validation; the CRA Annex VII §1-§2 mandate covers the software-versions + system-architecture dimensions of these subcategories at the product level (intended purpose + software versions affecting compliance + architecture description). The two subcategories together enable the manufacturer to demonstrate ex post, against the market surveillance authority, that the Annex VII §1-§2 general description + architecture description were drawn up before placing on the market (Art. 31(2)) and kept up to date during the support period with the 10-year retention per Art. 13(13). **IMPORTANT — CRA partial coverage**: CRA Annex VII §1-§2 is documentation-centric (general description + architecture), not a formal asset register in the DORA sense; the partial coverage does not substitute for the NIS 2 entity-level asset-management sub-domain (substantively scope-disjoint per CRDA `N (typically)`) or the DORA entity-level `3-way AND` inventory (different audit purposes — product-level MSA review vs. entity-level NCA review). **CRA presumption of conformity per Art. 27(1)/(2)/(5)/(8)/(9)** discharges the CRA conformity-assessment obligation only; it does not substitute for the NIS 2 entity-level asset-management sub-domain or the DORA Art. 7(1) `3-way AND` inventory obligation.)*' considerations=[] anchors=['Annex VII', 'Art. 13(13)', 'Art. 27(1)', 'Art. 31(2)', 'Art. 7(1)', '§1', '§2'] csf=['ID.AM-01', 'ID.AM-02']

id='SO-D-09.3.DORA' yaml_id='SO-D-09.3.DORA' regulation='DORA' subdomain_id='D-09.3' applies_to='[DORA]' inherits_from='SO-DORA-017 (sole authority per AEGIS taxonomy §4.1)' source_SR='SR-DORA-029' activation='if DORA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='3_of_3' verified_relationship=None objective="Financial entities **identify, classify and adequately document all ICT supported business functions, the roles and responsibilities supporting those functions, the information assets and ICT assets supporting those functions, and their roles and dependencies in relation to ICT risk** (Art. 7(1) DORA — the dedicated authority with explicit OJ-literal `3-way AND`); responsibility for managing and overseeing ICT risk is assigned to a control function with appropriate independence per the three lines of defence model (Art. 6(4) DORA).

**CSF anchors (from `SR-DORA-029` v0.3 security_rationale):**
ID.AM-01, ID.AM-02, ID.AM-05.
*(ID.AM-01 — Inventories of hardware managed within the system — anchors the DORA Art. 7(1) `information assets` + `ICT assets` dimensions mapped to NIST CSF 2.0 ID.AM-01; ID.AM-02 — Inventories of software, services, and systems managed — anchors the DORA Art. 7(1) `ICT supported business functions` + software-inventory dimensions; ID.AM-05 — Assets are prioritized based on classification, criticality, and business value — anchors the DORA Art. 7(1) `classify` dimension per CRDA DomainAnalysis §D-09.3 line 86 cross-validation. The three subcategories together (ID.AM-01 + ID.AM-02 + ID.AM-05) are the convergent NIST CSF 2.0 subcategories for DORA's entity-level asset inventory with the **classification dimension unique to DORA** (NIS 2 does not impose the classify dimension; CRA does not impose the classify dimension). The three subcategories together enable the financial entity to demonstrate ex post, against the national competent authority + EBA supervisory baseline, that the Art. 7(1) `3-way AND` ICT asset register + Art. 6(4) three-lines-of-defence were established, reviewed, and updated in light of the proportionality factors (size, nature, scale, complexity per Art. 4). For DORA financial entities that are also NSIEs, the DORA Art. 7(1) `3-way AND` discharges both the NIS 2 partial-coverage asset-management dimension and DORA's dedicated Art. 7(1) obligation — **DORA is the dedicated authority with OJ-literal `3-way AND`** distinct from the D-07.2 OJ-text-unsupported sole-authority assignment.)*" considerations=[] anchors=['Art. 4', 'Art. 6(4)', 'Art. 7(1)'] csf=['ID.AM-01', 'ID.AM-02', 'ID.AM-05']

layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-09.4 Records of Processing
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl: id='SO-D-09.4.HL' subdomain_id='D-09.4' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source=None verified_relationship_basis=None emergent_tensions=None objective='Records of processing activities are established through **parallel documentation regimes** that produce records of processing activities, technical documentation, certification records, information security policy documentation, and quality management system documentation serving distinct audit purposes.' considerations=['**5 of 5 regulations participate** on **parallel artefacts** with distinct triggers, retention cadences, and recipients — GDPR Art. 30(1)/(2)/(3)/(4)/(5) RoPA (DPA audit); NIS 2 Art. 24(1)/(2)/(3) certification-driven records per Member State (Member State / competent authority audit); CRA Annex VII §1-§8 8-item technical documentation + Art. 13(12)/(13)/(15)-(25)/(28)/(30)/(31)/(32) (MSA audit, 10-year or support-period retention); DORA Art. 9(4)(a) information security policy (NCA audit — **different record type from RoPA, DORA is fully absent for RoPA-equivalent per CRDA explicit note**); AI Act Art. 11 + Art. 12(1)/(2) + Art. 17(1) 13-element QMS + Art. 19(1) provider logs (MSA + AI Office audit).', '**CRDA-deep verified (10 pairs: 2 SAME — DIFFERENT-PERSPECTIVE — GDPR ↔ NIS 2 + GDPR ↔ CRA — substantively scope-disjoint per CRDA `N (typically)`, different record types; + 3 SAME — COMPLEMENTARY classified by CRDA — GDPR ↔ AI Act, NIS 2 ↔ CRA, CRA ↔ AI Act; + 1 SAME — DIFFERENT-PERSPECTIVE RECOMMENDED-by-CRDA — GDPR ↔ DORA substantively scope-disjoint; + 4 SAME — COMPLEMENTARY RECOMMENDED-by-CRDA — NIS 2 ↔ DORA, NIS 2 ↔ AI Act, CRA ↔ DORA, DORA ↔ AI Act)** — no CORRECTED, no CONTRADICTORY.', '**DORA-absence flag (CRDA-deep §D-09.4 line 29)**: DORA is fully absent for RoPA-equivalent — no analogue to GDPR Art. 30. For DORA financial entities, the GDPR RoPA remains the dedicated authority for processing-activities documentation; DORA Art. 9(4)(a) IS-policy documentation is a separate artefact.', '**No OJ-level cross-regulation consolidation rule for documentation** — unlike D-09.2 where CRA Art. 13(4) sentence 2 permits AI Act Art. 9 risk-management to substitute for CRA risk assessment, that rule covers the *risk-assessment object* not the *documentation object*. The 5 documentation regimes operate in parallel; no OJ-permitted cross-substitution exists.', '**Scope caveats**: (a) 3 substantively scope-disjoint pairs (GDPR ↔ NIS 2 + GDPR ↔ CRA + GDPR ↔ DORA) — different record types, different audit purposes; the high-level SO does NOT engage on these pairs alone; (b) the only cross-regulation link involving CRA + NIS 2 is the CRA Art. 27(8)/(9) CSA-certification presumption-of-conformity as upstream gate for NSIE procurements; (c) the 5 documentation regimes must be maintained in parallel even when the product is CRA-conformant and the AI system is AI-Act high-risk.'] anchors=['Annex VII', 'Art. 11', 'Art. 12(1)', 'Art. 13(12)', 'Art. 13(4)', 'Art. 17(1)', 'Art. 19(1)', 'Art. 24(1)', 'Art. 27(8)', 'Art. 30', 'Art. 30(1)', 'Art. 9', 'Art. 9(4)', '§1', '§8'] csf=[] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto  # activates when ≥2 applicable regs have ≥1 pair with Y or Conditional-Y-on-same-party scope overlap AND ≥1 sub-SO activates; for D-09.4 the matrix above shows **3 same-row pairs with N (typically)** (GDPR↔NIS 2, GDPR↔CRA, GDPR↔DORA-recommended — substantively scope-disjoint per CRDA) and **7 pairs with Y or Conditional-Y activation on the joint-condition operator** (GDPR↔AI_Act = Conditional-Y; NIS2↔CRA = Conditional-Y; NIS2↔DORA = Conditional-Y; NIS2↔AI_Act = Conditional-Y; CRA↔DORA = Conditional-Y; CRA↔AI_Act = Y; DORA↔AI_Act = Conditional-Y). The high-level SO engages on the 7 same-event activation pairs — not on the 3 substantively scope-disjoint pairs. The high-level SO does NOT collapse the 5 documentation regimes into a single artefact; it surfaces the **common documentation-regime duty** (records of processing activities + technical documentation + certification records + IS-policy documentation + QMS documentation) on parallel artefacts serving distinct audit purposes.'

id='SO-D-09.4.GDPR' yaml_id='SO-D-09.4.GDPR' regulation='GDPR' subdomain_id='D-09.4' applies_to='[GDPR]' inherits_from='SO-GDPR-029 + SO-GDPR-038' source_SR='SR-GDPR-048 + SR-GDPR-050 + SR-GDPR-065 + SR-GDPR-066 + SR-GDPR-067 + SR-GDPR-068' activation='if GDPR in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_5' verified_relationship=None objective='Each controller and processor **maintains a record of processing activities under its responsibility** (Art. 30(1) GDPR), in writing or electronic form (Art. 30(3) GDPR), containing the Art. 30(1) 7-item content list; the processor maintains a parallel record under Art. 30(2) GDPR; records are made available to the supervisory authority on request (Art. 30(4) GDPR), subject to the Art. 30(5) 250-employee exception.

**CSF anchors (from `SR-GDPR-048` + `SR-GDPR-050` + `SR-GDPR-065-068` v0.3 security_rationale):**
ID.AM-08 (primary), PR.DS-12, GV.PO-02.
*(ID.AM-08 — Systems, hardware, software, services, and data are managed throughout their life cycle — anchors the GDPR Art. 30 RoPA `record of processing activities under its responsibility` mapped to NIST CSF 2.0 ID.AM-08 per CRDA DomainAnalysis §D-09.4 line 113 cross-validation; PR.DS-12 — Data managed consistent with risk strategy — anchors the GDPR Art. 30(1)(g) `general description of the technical and organisational security measures` per CRDA DomainAnalysis §D-09.4 line 113; GV.PO-02 — Cybersecurity processes and procedures established, communicated, enforced — anchors the GDPR Art. 30(3) `in writing, including in electronic form` per CRDA DomainAnalysis §D-09.4 line 113 cross-validation (GDPR specifically maps GV.PO-02 for the demonstrable-compliance dimension). The three subcategories together enable the controller or processor to demonstrate ex post, against the Art. 5(2) accountability burden, that the Art. 30(1) RoPA 7-item content list + Art. 30(3) in-writing-or-electronic-form + Art. 30(4) on-DPA-request records were established, reviewed, and updated as processing activities changed (Art. 30(1) `shall maintain`). **IMPORTANT — DORA-absence flag**: per CRDA-deep §D-09.4 line 29, **DORA is fully absent for RoPA-equivalent**; for DORA financial entities, the GDPR RoPA remains the dedicated authority for processing-activities documentation. The GDPR RoPA does **NOT** substitute for the CRA Annex VII 8-item technical documentation (substantively scope-disjoint per CRDA `N (typically)`), the NIS 2 Art. 24 certification-driven records (substantively scope-disjoint per CRDA `N (typically)`), the DORA Art. 9(4)(a) IS-policy documentation (different record type), or the AI Act Annex IV + Art. 17(1) QMS documentation (parallel artefacts). Phase 1 entities with GDPR + CRA applicability must maintain both GDPR RoPA + CRA Annex VII technical documentation on distinct artefacts that are not substitutable.)*' considerations=[] anchors=['Annex IV', 'Annex VII', 'Art. 17(1)', 'Art. 24', 'Art. 30', 'Art. 30(1)', 'Art. 30(2)', 'Art. 30(3)', 'Art. 30(4)', 'Art. 30(5)', 'Art. 5(2)', 'Art. 9(4)'] csf=['GV.PO-02', 'ID.AM-08', 'PR.DS-12']

id='SO-D-09.4.NIS2' yaml_id='SO-D-09.4.NIS2' regulation='NIS2' subdomain_id='D-09.4' applies_to='[NIS2]' inherits_from='SO-NIS2-024' source_SR='SR-NIS2-043' activation='if NIS2 in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='2_of_5' verified_relationship=None objective="Member States shall **encourage the use of European or internationally accepted standards and specifications relevant to the security of network and information systems** (Art. 24(1) sentence 1 NIS 2) and of qualified trust services (Art. 24(1) sentence 2); the Commission may adopt delegated acts specifying entities that must use certified ICT products, services and processes (Art. 24(2) NIS 2), and ENISA may be requested to prepare a candidate European cybersecurity certification scheme (Art. 24(3) NIS 2).

**CSF anchors (from `SR-NIS2-043` v0.3 security_rationale):**
ID.AM-08 (primary), PR.DS-12.
*(ID.AM-08 — Systems, hardware, software, services, and data are managed throughout their life cycle — anchors the NIS 2 Art. 24(1)/(2)/(3) certification-driven recordkeeping mapped to NIST CSF 2.0 ID.AM-08 per CRDA DomainAnalysis §D-09.4 line 113 cross-validation; PR.DS-12 — Data managed consistent with risk strategy — anchors the NIS 2 Art. 24(1) use of certified ICT products/services/processes per CRDA DomainAnalysis §D-09.4 line 113. The two subcategories together enable the NSIE to demonstrate ex post, against the Member State competent authority, that the Art. 24(1)/(2)/(3) certification-driven records were established for the certified ICT products/services/processes procured. **IMPORTANT — NIS 2 partial coverage at D-09.4**: the NIS 2 Art. 24(1)/(2)/(3) certification-driven recordkeeping is **partial coverage** — Member-State-driven use of certified ICT products/services/processes, not a RoPA-equivalent; substantively scope-disjoint from GDPR per CRDA `N (typically)` (different record types, different triggers). Phase 1 entities with NIS 2 + GDPR applicability must maintain both GDPR Art. 30 RoPA + NIS 2 Art. 24 certification-driven records on distinct artefacts that are not substitutable. For NSIEs that are CRA-conformant product procurers, the CRA Art. 27(8)/(9) CSA-certification presumption-of-conformity machinery is the upstream gate for NIS 2 procurements — Phase 1 must verify that procured CRA products hold CSA certification at the assurance level required by the Commission's delegated act under Art. 24(2). The **NIS 2 → CRA certification link** is the only cross-regulation link at D-09.4 involving NIS 2.)*" considerations=[] anchors=['Art. 24', 'Art. 24(1)', 'Art. 24(2)', 'Art. 24(3)', 'Art. 27(8)', 'Art. 30'] csf=['ID.AM-08', 'PR.DS-12']

id='SO-D-09.4.CRA' yaml_id='SO-D-09.4.CRA' regulation='CRA' subdomain_id='D-09.4' applies_to='[CRA]' inherits_from='SO-CRA-055 + SO-CRA-056 + SO-CRA-057 + SO-CRA-058 + SO-CRA-059 + SO-CRA-061 + SO-CRA-062 + SO-CRA-063 + SO-CRA-064 + SO-CRA-065 + SO-CRA-066 + SO-CRA-067' source_SR='SR-CRA-085 + SR-CRA-087 + SR-CRA-088 + SR-CRA-078' activation='if CRA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='3_of_5' verified_relationship=None objective="The manufacturer **draws up before placing a product with digital elements on the market the technical documentation referred to in Art. 31** (Art. 13(12) sentence 1 CRA), carries out the conformity assessment procedure referred to in Art. 32, draws up the EU declaration of conformity under Art. 28, and affixes the CE marking under Art. 30 (Art. 13(12) sentence 2); the manufacturer keeps the technical documentation and the EU declaration of conformity at the disposal of market surveillance authorities for at least 10 years or the support period, whichever is longer (Art. 13(13) CRA).

**CSF anchors (from `SR-CRA-085` + `SR-CRA-087` + `SR-CRA-088` + `SR-CRA-078` v0.3 security_rationale):**
ID.AM-08 (primary), PR.DS-12, ID.RA-05.
*(ID.AM-08 — Systems, hardware, software, services, and data are managed throughout their life cycle — anchors the CRA Annex VII §1-§8 8-item content list mapped to NIST CSF 2.0 ID.AM-08 per CRDA DomainAnalysis §D-09.4 line 113 cross-validation; PR.DS-12 — Data managed consistent with risk strategy — anchors the CRA Annex VII §1 `general description` + §3 `cybersecurity risk assessment` dimensions per CRDA DomainAnalysis §D-09.4 line 113; ID.RA-05 — Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to determine the priority risk responses — anchors the CRA Annex VII §3 `cybersecurity risk assessment` documentation per CRDA DomainAnalysis §D-09.4 line 113 (CRA specifically maps ID.RA-05 for the risk-assessment documentation). The three subcategories together enable the manufacturer to demonstrate ex post, against the market surveillance authority, that the Annex VII §1-§8 8-item content list + Art. 13(12)/(13)/(15)/(16)/(17)/(19)/(20)/(21)/(22)/(23) documentation were established before placing on the market and kept up to date during the support period with the 10-year retention per Art. 13(13). **IMPORTANT — CRA full content codification**: CRA Annex VII §1-§8 is **fully content-codified** — the 8-item content list is explicit. The CRA sub-SO is the densest documentation regime of the 5 (covering product identification + manufacturer contact + SPOC + support-period + EU declaration + CE marking + conformity assessment + MSA cooperation + cessation-of-operations + Commission implementing/delegated acts). **IMPORTANT — CRA Annex VII does NOT cross-substitute for GDPR RoPA**: substantively scope-disjoint per CRDA `N (typically)` (different record types, different triggers, different audit purposes). **IMPORTANT — CRA + AI Act for AI-enabled products do NOT have OJ-level consolidation for documentation**: unlike the CRA Art. 13(4) sentence 2 risk-assessment consolidation rule at D-09.2 (which substitutes AI Act Art. 9 risk-management for CRA risk-assessment), there is no equivalent documentation-level consolidation rule at D-09.4; the two regimes maintain parallel artefacts (CRA Annex VII + AI Act Annex IV + AI Act Art. 17 QMS). **CRA Art. 27(8)/(9) CSA-certification presumption-of-conformity**: the CRA Art. 27(8)/(9) `A product with digital elements and the processes put in place by the manufacturer for which the manufacturer has obtained an EU statement of conformity or an EU certificate under a European cybersecurity certification scheme adopted pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2019/881, at assurance level at least 'substantial', shall be presumed to be in conformity with the essential cybersecurity requirements` is the upstream gate for NIS 2 procurements of CRA-conformant products; Phase 1 entities with NIS 2 + CRA applicability that procure CSA-certified CRA products discharge the Conditional-Y scope overlap at the certification boundary.)*" considerations=[] anchors=['Annex IV', 'Annex VII', 'Art. 13(12)', 'Art. 13(13)', 'Art. 13(4)', 'Art. 17', 'Art. 27(8)', 'Art. 28', 'Art. 30', 'Art. 31', 'Art. 32', 'Art. 9', '§1', '§3', '§8'] csf=['ID.AM-08', 'ID.RA-05', 'PR.DS-12']

id='SO-D-09.4.DORA' yaml_id='SO-D-09.4.DORA' regulation='DORA' subdomain_id='D-09.4' applies_to='[DORA]' inherits_from='(out-of-scope as RoPA-equivalent — partial via DORA Art. 9(4)(a) SO-DORA-018 cross)' source_SR='SR-DORA-031' activation='if DORA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='4_of_5' verified_relationship=None objective='Financial entities **develop and document an information security policy defining rules to protect the availability, authenticity, integrity and confidentiality of data, information assets and ICT assets, including those of their customers, where applicable** (Art. 9(4)(a) DORA); this is entity-level IS-policy documentation serving NCA audit purposes and is a **different record type from the GDPR RoPA**.

id='SO-D-09.4.AI_Act' yaml_id='SO-D-09.4.AI_Act' regulation='AI_Act' subdomain_id='D-09.4' applies_to='[AI_Act]' inherits_from='SO-AI_Act-009 + SO-AI_Act-010 + SO-AI_Act-008 (logs)' source_SR='SR-AI_Act-008 + SR-AI_Act-009 + SR-AI_Act-010 + SR-AI_Act-017' activation='if AI_Act in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='5_of_5' verified_relationship=None objective='Providers of high-risk AI systems **draw up and keep up-to-date the technical documentation of the high-risk AI system in accordance with Annex IV before that system is placed on the market or put into service** (Art. 11(1) AI Act), **keep the logs automatically recorded by the high-risk AI system to the extent under their control** (Art. 19(1) AI Act), and document the **quality management system** in written policies, procedures, and instructions covering at least the 13 enumerated aspects (a)-(m) (Art. 17(1) AI Act).

layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl: id='SO-D-10.1.HL' subdomain_id='D-10.1' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source=None verified_relationship_basis=None emergent_tensions=None objective='Continuous security monitoring is established through a **layered detection-and-monitoring architecture** spanning personal-data processing systems, network and information systems, on-device product activity, ICT systems and tools, and high-risk AI systems, with detection capability feeding the incident-response chain.' considerations=['5 of 5 regulations participate with **distinct anchors and scope layers** — GDPR (Art. 32(2) 5-risk-type detection + Art. 33(1) 72-hour breach-`becoming-aware` clock — entity-level personal-data monitoring); NIS 2 (Art. 21(2)(b) all-hazards detection capability as incident-handling dimension — **partial coverage, no dedicated continuous-monitoring mandate**); CRA (Annex I Part I (2)(l) on-device internal-activity monitoring with **user opt-out** + Annex I Part II (6) vulnerability reporting — product-level); DORA (Art. 8(1) `continuously monitor and control the security and functioning of ICT systems and tools` (OJ-literal locus Art. 9(1) per SR-DORA-030) + Art. 10(1)+(2) prompt anomalous-activity detection + Art. 7(2) continuous ICT risk identification — financial-entity); AI Act (Art. 72(1)-(2) `actively and systematically collect, document and analyse` post-market monitoring `proportionate to the nature of the AI technologies and the risks` + Art. 74 market-surveillance cooperation — AI-system lifecycle).', '**CRDA-deep verified (10 pairs: 9 SAME — COMPLEMENTARY + 1 SAME — EQUAL NIS 2 ↔ DORA on continuous-monitoring dimension, DORA-dominant for financial entities)** — no CORRECTED reclassifications, no scope-disjoint pairs.', "**1 CRDA-flagged GENUINE TENSION — Layer 2 OJ-level resolution required**: CRA Annex I Part I (2)(l) user opt-out vs. mandatory-monitoring regimes (GDPR Art. 32(2) + NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(b) + DORA Art. 8(1)). The conflict propagates to 3 of 10 pairs (GDPR↔CRA primary, NIS2↔CRA, CRA↔DORA). The OJ does not resolve the conflict. The two regimes can stack on the layered monitoring architecture (entity-layer mandatory + product-layer with opt-out), but the user's opt-out from CRA monitoring may not legally exempt the controller/NSIE/DORA entity from the respective mandatory-monitoring regime. Phase 1C Doc 07 must perform the Layer 2 OJ-level resolution.", '**Scope caveats**: (a) NIS 2 ↔ DORA EQUAL discharges both on the DORA-dominant stack for financial entities; (b) DORA-led stack for financial entities — DORA Art. 8(1) monitoring is broader (security AND functioning) than GDPR Art. 32(2) 5-risk-type, with GDPR detection as a sub-component; (c) AI Act post-market monitoring adds the analysis-to-risk-management feedback loop (Art. 72(2) → Art. 9 + Art. 17) not present in the other 4 regulators.'] anchors=['Annex I Part I (2)', 'Annex I Part II (6)', 'Art. 10(1)', 'Art. 17', 'Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 32(2)', 'Art. 33(1)', 'Art. 7(2)', 'Art. 72(1)', 'Art. 72(2)', 'Art. 74', 'Art. 8(1)', 'Art. 9', 'Art. 9(1)'] csf=[] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto  # activates when ≥2 applicable regs have ≥1 pair with Y or Conditional-Y-on-same-party scope overlap AND ≥1 sub-SO activates; for D-10.1 the matrix above shows every pair has Y or Conditional-Y activation on the joint-condition operator (no N (typically) scope-disjoint pairs), so the high-level SO engages whenever ≥2 regs are applicable; the 9 SAME — COMPLEMENTARY pairs stack on a layered 5-monitoring-architecture; the 1 SAME — EQUAL pair (NIS 2 ↔ DORA) discharges both obligations on the DORA-dominant continuous-monitoring stack for financial entities. The high-level SO does NOT collapse any per-reg monitoring mandate; it surfaces the common continuous-monitoring duty (pre-breach-detection + on-device-internal-activity + ICT-system-security-and-functioning + AI-system-post-market-data) with the per-reg anchor, scope dimension, trigger, threshold, recipient, and content template preserved verbatim in the 5 sub-SOs. **CRITICAL — the high-level SO does NOT resolve the CRDA-flagged GENUINE TENSION (CRA user opt-out vs. mandatory monitoring — propagated to GDPR↔CRA, NIS2↔CRA, CRA↔DORA pairs); the conflict is preserved as a conditional emergent tension requiring Layer 2 OJ-level resolution.**'

id='SO-D-10.1.GDPR' yaml_id='SO-D-10.1.GDPR' regulation='GDPR' subdomain_id='D-10.1' applies_to='[GDPR]' inherits_from='SO-GDPR-030 + SO-GDPR-008' source_SR='SR-GDPR-019 + SR-GDPR-020 + SR-GDPR-021' activation='if GDPR in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_5' verified_relationship=None objective='The controller and processor implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure the **ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems and services** (Art. 32(1)(b) GDPR) and **regularly test, assess and evaluate their effectiveness** (Art. 32(1)(d) GDPR); personal-data processing systems and services are monitored for the five Art. 32(2) risk types, with a clear definition of the moment of `becoming aware of` a breach to anchor the Art. 33(1) 72-hour notification clock.

**CSF anchors (from `SR-GDPR-019` + `SR-GDPR-020` v0.3 security_rationale):**
DE.CM-01 (primary), DE.CM-09, DE.AE-02, ID.IM-04.
*(DE.CM-01 — Networks and network services are monitored to find potentially adverse events — anchors the GDPR Art. 32(2) 5-risk-type monitoring mapped to NIST CSF 2.0 DE.CM-01; DE.CM-09 — Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored — anchors the personal-data processing systems monitoring per DomainAnalysis cross-validation; DE.AE-02 — Adverse events are analyzed to identify or determine the scope of an incident — anchors the breach-`becoming-aware` clock per Art. 33(1); ID.IM-04 — Adequate resource capacity to ensure availability is maintained — anchors the Art. 32(1)(b) ongoing availability dimension. The four subcategories together enable the controller or processor to demonstrate ex post, against the Art. 5(2) accountability burden, that the 5-risk-type monitoring was operational and that the breach-`becoming-aware` clock was correctly anchored for Art. 33(1) notification.)*' considerations=[] anchors=['Art. 32(1)', 'Art. 32(2)', 'Art. 33(1)', 'Art. 5(2)'] csf=['DE.AE-02', 'DE.CM-01', 'DE.CM-09', 'ID.IM-04']

id='SO-D-10.1.NIS2' yaml_id='SO-D-10.1.NIS2' regulation='NIS2' subdomain_id='D-10.1' applies_to='[NIS2]' inherits_from='SO-NIS2-005' source_SR='SR-NIS2-009 + SR-NIS2-014' activation='if NIS2 in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='2_of_5' verified_relationship=None objective='Essential and important entities establish an **incident-handling capability** covering prevention, detection, analysis, containment, response, and recovery of incidents (Art. 21(2)(b) NIS 2); the detection dimension is the partial-coverage dimension of D-10.1, operating on an all-hazards basis and feeding the Art. 23(1) significant-incident notification chain.

**CSF anchors (from `SR-NIS2-009` + `SR-NIS2-014` v0.3 security_rationale):**
DE.CM-01 (primary), DE.CM-09, DE.AE-02, ID.IM-04.
*(DE.CM-01 — Networks and network services are monitored to find potentially adverse events — anchors the NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(b) incident-handling detection capability mapped to NIST CSF 2.0 DE.CM-01; DE.CM-09 — Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored — anchors the all-hazards network and information systems monitoring per DomainAnalysis cross-validation; DE.AE-02 — Adverse events are analyzed to identify or determine the scope of an incident — anchors the Art. 23 significant-incident detection trigger; ID.IM-04 — Adequate resource capacity — anchors the prevention+detection+response feedback loop. The four subcategories together enable the NSIE to demonstrate ex post, against the competent authority (CSIRT), that the Art. 21(2)(b) detection capability was operational on the all-hazards basis and that the Art. 23(1) significant-incident notification was correctly triggered. For DORA financial entities, the DORA Art. 9(1) continuous monitoring discharges both obligations — DORA-dominant.)*' considerations=[] anchors=['Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 23', 'Art. 23(1)', 'Art. 9(1)'] csf=['DE.AE-02', 'DE.CM-01', 'DE.CM-09', 'ID.IM-04']

id='SO-D-10.1.CRA' yaml_id='SO-D-10.1.CRA' regulation='CRA' subdomain_id='D-10.1' applies_to='[CRA]' inherits_from='SO-CRA-020 + SO-CRA-068' source_SR='SR-CRA-100 + SR-CRA-101' activation='if CRA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='3_of_5' verified_relationship=None objective='A product with digital elements **provides security-related information by recording and monitoring relevant internal activity, including access to or modification of data, services or functions, and provides an opt-out mechanism for the user** (Annex I Part I (2)(l) CRA); the manufacturer **facilitates the sharing of information about potential vulnerabilities** through a single contact address (Annex I Part II (6) CRA).

**CSF anchors (from `SR-CRA-100` + `SR-CRA-101` v0.3 security_rationale):**
DE.CM-01 (primary), DE.CM-09, ID.IM-04.
*(DE.CM-01 — Networks and network services are monitored to find potentially adverse events — anchors the CRA Annex I Part I (2)(l) on-device internal-activity monitoring mapped to NIST CSF 2.0 DE.CM-01; DE.CM-09 — Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored — anchors the product-level on-device monitoring per DomainAnalysis cross-validation; ID.IM-04 — Adequate resource capacity — anchors the manufacturer-side observability dimension.
