layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl: id='SO-D-10.2.HL' subdomain_id='D-10.2' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source=None verified_relationship_basis=None emergent_tensions=None objective='Audit logging and traceability are established through a **layered audit-records architecture** spanning compliance records with integrity and traceability, product-level technical documentation traceability, entity-level information security policy documentation, and AI-system event logging with retention floors.' considerations=['**4 of 5 regulations participate** (GDPR, CRA, DORA, AI Act — **NIS 2 is fully out-of-scope** per CRDA T3-vs-text gap: OJ Art. 21(2)(j) does not mention logging, audit trails, or traceability). DORA is **partial coverage only** via Art. 9(4)(a) (logging implicit in CIA+A monitoring, not a standalone audit-logging mandate). Distinct anchors: GDPR Art. 30(3) compliance records with Art. 5(2) accountability + Art. 31 SA cooperation; CRA Annex VII §5-§8 + Annex VII §3 + Annex I Part II (3) + Art. 13(4) sentence 1 + Art. 13(22) MSA cooperation (10 years or support period, whichever longer); DORA Art. 9(4)(a) information security policy with CIA+A rules; AI Act Art. 12(1)+(2) automatic event logging + Art. 19(1) provider log retention ≥6-month floor + `under their control` POLY + GDPR escape clause.', '**CRDA-deep verified (6 pairs: 6 SAME — COMPLEMENTARY — no EQUAL, no CORRECTED, no GENUINE TENSION)**; 1 substantively scope-disjoint N (typically) pair (GDPR ↔ CRA — different record types, different triggers); 5 of 6 pairs Conditional-Y. The high-level SO does NOT collapse the 4 audit-logging mandates into a single duty.', '**Notable OJ-consistent reconciliation (NOT a tension) — floor-within-ceiling pattern**: AI Act Art. 19(1) `at least six months` hard floor is a subset of the GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) `as long as necessary` envelope. When the high-risk AI system processes personal data and the logs contain personal data, the AI Act ≥6-month floor is the FLOOR and the GDPR `necessary` is the CEILING. The OJ does NOT resolve this as a conflict because the two regimes operate on different time scales (one is a floor, one is a ceiling).', '**Scope caveats**: (a) GDPR ↔ CRA substantively scope-disjoint (compliance records vs. product cybersecurity documentation) — different record types, different triggers; no overlap on a single event at a single party; (b) DORA partial coverage at D-10.2 — logging implicit, not standalone; (c) NIS 2 fully out-of-scope — no sub-SO emitted.'] anchors=['Annex I Part II (3)', 'Annex VII', 'Art. 12(1)', 'Art. 13(22)', 'Art. 13(4)', 'Art. 19(1)', 'Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 30(3)', 'Art. 31', 'Art. 5(1)', 'Art. 5(2)', 'Art. 9(4)', '§3', '§5', '§8'] csf=[] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation='auto  # activates when ≥2 applicable regs have ≥1 pair with Y or Conditional-Y-on-same-party scope overlap AND ≥1 sub-SO activates; for D-10.2 the 4×4 matrix above shows 5 of 6 pairs have Conditional-Y activation on the joint-condition operator (1 N (typically) pair: GDPR ↔ CRA is substantively scope-disjoint), so the high-level SO engages whenever ≥2 regs are applicable and the joint condition is met; the 6 SAME — COMPLEMENTARY pairs stack on a layered 4-audit-records architecture; no EQUAL pair, no GENUINE TENSION pair, no CORRECTED reclassification, no scope-disjoint pair beyond the 1 N (typically) GDPR ↔ CRA pair. The high-level SO does NOT collapse any per-reg audit-logging mandate; it surfaces the common audit-logging duty (records with integrity + traceability + supervisor/MSA availability + log retention floors + product-level documentation traceability) with the per-reg anchor, scope dimension, trigger, threshold, recipient, and content template preserved verbatim in the 4 sub-SOs. **NOTABLE — the high-level SO does NOT need to surface any emergent tension**: the CRDA-deep verified classifications document 0 GENUINE TENSIONS at D-10.2; the OJ-consistent floor-within-ceiling reconciliation (AI Act Art. 19(1) 6-month floor within GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) ceiling envelope) is preserved as a scope-caveat in the aggregation logic, not as a tension.'

layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-10.3 Compliance Testing
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl: id='SO-D-10.3.HL' subdomain_id='D-10.3' is_high_level=True applies_to=['ALL'] derivation_source=None verified_relationship_basis=None emergent_tensions=None objective='Compliance testing is established through a **5-parallel-testing-programme architecture** spanning effectiveness-evaluation of security measures, effectiveness-assessment of risk-management measures, product-level conformity-assessment, entity-level digital operational resilience testing with TLPT, and AI-system-level testing for risk management with real-world-conditions and accuracy/robustness/cybersecurity baseline testing.' considerations=['5 of 5 regulations participate with **distinct anchors, cadences, and methodologies** — GDPR (Art. 32(1)(d) `regularly testing, assessing and evaluating` + Art. 35(11) DPIA review on risk change — entity-level effectiveness-evaluation of security measures); NIS 2 (Art. 21(2)(f) `policies and procedures to assess the effectiveness of cybersecurity risk-management measures` — entity-level effectiveness-assessment, no quantitative cadence under Recital 56); CRA (Annex I Part II (3) `effective and regular tests` + Annex VII §6 test reports + Annex VIII Part I (Module A internal production control) + Annex VIII Part II (Module B+C and H notified-body EU-type examination) — product-level conformity-assessment via OJ-codified modules); DORA (Art. 24(1) `sound and comprehensive digital operational resilience testing programme` + Art. 25(1) 12-way testing modalities portfolio + Art. 26(1) TLPT for significant entities `on a regular basis` — financial-entity testing programme); AI Act (Art. 9(6) testing for risk management + Art. 9(7) real-world-conditions testing per Art. 60 + Art. 15(1) accuracy/robustness/cybersecurity baseline `throughout their lifecycle` — AI-system-level testing).', '**CRDA-deep verified (10 pairs: 9 SAME — COMPLEMENTARY + 1 SAME — EQUAL NIS 2 ↔ DORA on testing-programme dimension, DORA-dominant for significant financial entities under Art. 26(1) TLPT)** — no CORRECTED, no CONTRADICTORY, no scope-disjoint N (typically) pairs; 0 GENUINE TENSIONS. The high-level SO does NOT collapse the 5 testing mandates into a single testing programme.', '**No OJ-level consolidation rule for testing** (per CRDA-deep line 29: `All 5 regulations impose testing with different scopes, methodologies, and cadences. No OJ-level consolidation rule exists. Phase 1 entities must implement 5 parallel testing programmes.`) — structurally different from D-09.2 where CRA Art. 13(4) sentence 2 permits AI Act Art. 9 risk-management to substitute for CRA risk assessment; that rule covers the *risk-assessment object*, not the *testing object*. Even on the CRA↔AI_Act pair (CRDA-deep line 388), the CRA Annex I Part II (3) + Annex VII §6 + Annex VIII modules stack separately from the AI Act Art. 9(6) + Art. 9(7) + Art. 15(1).', '**Scope caveats**: (a) NIS 2 ↔ DORA EQUAL discharges both on the DORA-dominant stack for significant financial entities (NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(f) is partial coverage); (b) DORA-led stack for financial entities — DORA Art. 24(1) testing programme is broader (digital operational resilience + 12-way modalities + TLPT) than GDPR/NIS 2 testing; (c) AI Act lifecycle-testing dimension under Art. 15(1) `throughout their lifecycle` is distinct from the point-in-time or `regularly` cadences of the other 4 regulators.'] anchors=['Annex I Part II (3)', 'Annex VII', 'Annex VIII', 'Annex VIII Part I (Module A internal production control)', 'Annex VIII Part II (Module B+C and H notified-body EU-type examination)', 'Art. 13(4)', 'Art. 15(1)', 'Art. 21(2)', 'Art. 24(1)', 'Art. 25(1)', 'Art. 26(1)', 'Art. 32(1)', 'Art. 35(11)', 'Art. 60', 'Art. 9', 'Art. 9(6)', 'Art. 9(7)', '§6'] csf=[] inherits_from=None source_SR=None activation="auto  # activates when ≥2 applicable regs have ≥1 pair with Y or Conditional-Y-on-same-party scope overlap AND ≥1 sub-SO activates; for D-10.3 the 5×5 matrix above shows every pair has Y or Conditional-Y activation on the joint-condition operator (no N (typically) scope-disjoint pairs), so the high-level SO engages whenever ≥2 regs are applicable; the 9 SAME — COMPLEMENTARY pairs stack on a layered 5-testing-architecture; the 1 SAME — EQUAL pair (NIS 2 ↔ DORA) discharges both obligations on the DORA-dominant testing-programme stack for significant financial entities under Art. 26(1) TLPT. The high-level SO does NOT collapse any per-reg testing mandate; it surfaces the common compliance-testing duty (regular/effective testing of security measures + risk-management-measure effectiveness assessment + product conformity-assessment + entity testing programme + AI-system testing for risk management + accuracy/robustness/cybersecurity baseline + real-world-conditions testing + TLPT for significant entities) with the per-reg anchor, scope dimension, trigger, threshold, recipient, cadence, and content template preserved verbatim in the 5 sub-SOs. **CRITICAL — NO OJ-LEVEL CONSOLIDATION RULE EXISTS FOR TESTING (CRDA-deep line 29)**: 'All 5 regulations impose testing with different scopes, methodologies, and cadences. No OJ-level consolidation rule exists. Phase 1 entities must implement 5 parallel testing programmes.' Unlike the CRA Art. 13(4) sentence 2 risk-assessment consolidation rule (which applies only to D-09.2 risk-assessment), there is no cross-regulation consolidation rule at D-10.3 — the 5 parallel testing programmes are the operative consequence."

id='SO-D-10.3.GDPR' yaml_id='SO-D-10.3.GDPR' regulation='GDPR' subdomain_id='D-10.3' applies_to='[GDPR]' inherits_from='SO-GDPR-032 + SO-GDPR-009' source_SR='SR-GDPR-019 + SR-GDPR-021 + SR-GDPR-022' activation='if GDPR in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='1_of_5' verified_relationship=None objective='The controller and processor implement appropriate technical and organisational measures including **a process for regularly testing, assessing and evaluating the effectiveness of technical and organisational measures for ensuring the security of the processing** (Art. 32(1)(d) GDPR); the DPIA is **reviewed at least when there is a change of the risk represented by processing operations** (Art. 35(11) GDPR).

**CSF anchors (from `SR-GDPR-019` + `SR-GDPR-021` + `SR-GDPR-022` v0.3 security_rationale):**
PR.IP-07 (primary), ID.RA-05, DE.AE-02, GV.OV-03.
*(PR.IP-07 — Configuration change control processes are in place — anchors the GDPR Art. 32(1)(d) `regularly testing, assessing and evaluating the effectiveness of technical and organisational measures` mapped to NIST CSF 2.0 PR.IP-07; ID.RA-05 — Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to establish risk tolerances — anchors the Art. 35(11) DPIA review on risk change dimension; DE.AE-02 — Adverse events are analyzed to identify or determine the scope of an incident — anchors the effectiveness-evaluation input to the incident-handling chain; GV.OV-03 — Cybersecurity risk management strategy outcomes are reviewed and inform changes — anchors the Art. 35(11) DPIA review feedback loop into the risk-management strategy. The four subcategories together enable the controller or processor to demonstrate ex post, against the Art. 5(2) accountability burden, that the Art. 32(1)(d) effectiveness-evaluation was operational with `regularly testing` cadence + Art. 35(11) DPIA review on risk change trigger.)*' considerations=[] anchors=['Art. 32(1)', 'Art. 35(11)', 'Art. 5(2)'] csf=['DE.AE-02', 'GV.OV-03', 'ID.RA-05', 'PR.IP-07']

*(PR.IP-07 — Configuration change control processes are in place — anchors the NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(f) `policies and procedures to assess the effectiveness of cybersecurity risk-management measures` mapped to NIST CSF 2.0 PR.IP-07; ID.RA-05 — Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to establish risk tolerances — anchors the effectiveness-assessment feedback loop into the risk-management framework; GV.OV-03 — Cybersecurity risk management strategy outcomes are reviewed and inform changes — anchors the Art. 21(2)(f) effectiveness-assessment feedback into the all-hazards risk-management strategy outcomes; DE.AE-02 — Adverse events are analyzed to identify or determine the scope of an incident — anchors the effectiveness-assessment input to the incident-handling chain. The four subcategories together enable the NSIE to demonstrate ex post, against the competent authority (CSIRT), that the Art. 21(2)(f) effectiveness-assessment policies and procedures were operational with `policies and procedures to assess the effectiveness` cadence + methodology + evidence templates.)*' considerations=[] anchors=['Art. 21(2)'] csf=['DE.AE-02', 'GV.OV-03', 'ID.RA-05', 'PR.IP-07']

id='SO-D-10.3.CRA' yaml_id='SO-D-10.3.CRA' regulation='CRA' subdomain_id='D-10.3' applies_to='[CRA]' inherits_from='SO-CRA-071 + SO-CRA-072' source_SR='SR-CRA-101 + SR-CRA-103 + SR-CRA-104' activation='if CRA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='3_of_5' verified_relationship=None objective="Manufacturers of products with digital elements **carry out effective and regular tests and reviews of the product** (Annex I Part II (3) CRA), and the technical documentation shall contain **the reports of the tests carried out to verify the conformity of the product with digital elements and of the vulnerability-handling processes with the essential cybersecurity requirements set out in Part I and Part II of Annex I** (Annex VII §6 CRA); conformity is demonstrated via the Annex VIII Part I (Module A internal production control) or Part II (Module B+C and H notified-body EU-type examination) conformity-assessment modules depending on product classification (Class I / Class II / critical per Art. 6 + Annex III).

**CSF anchors (from `SR-CRA-101` + `SR-CRA-103` + `SR-CRA-104` v0.3 security_rationale):**
PR.IP-07 (primary), ID.RA-05, DE.AE-02, GV.OV-03.
*(PR.IP-07 — Configuration change control processes are in place — anchors the CRA Annex I Part II (3) `effective and regular tests and reviews` mapped to NIST CSF 2.0 PR.IP-07; ID.RA-05 — Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to establish risk tolerances — anchors the Annex VII §6 test reports as input to the conformity-assessment risk dimension; DE.AE-02 — Adverse events are analyzed to identify or determine the scope of an incident — anchors the Annex I Part II (3) effective and regular tests as input to the vulnerability-handling chain; GV.OV-03 — Cybersecurity risk management strategy outcomes are reviewed and inform changes — anchors the Annex VIII Part I–IV modules feedback loop into the manufacturer's quality-management system (Art. 13(8) cross to D-09.1). The four subcategories together enable the manufacturer to demonstrate ex post, against the MSA, that the Annex I Part II (3) `effective and regular tests` + Annex VII §6 test reports + Annex VIII Part I–IV conformity-assessment modules were operational on the product layer with `effective and regular` cadence + appropriate Module selection (A vs. B+C and H) per product classification.)*" considerations=[] anchors=['Annex I', 'Annex I Part II (3)', 'Annex III', 'Annex VII', 'Annex VIII Part I', 'Annex VIII Part I (Module A internal production control)', 'Art. 13(8)', 'Art. 6', '§6'] csf=['DE.AE-02', 'GV.OV-03', 'ID.RA-05', 'PR.IP-07']

id='SO-D-10.3.DORA' yaml_id='SO-D-10.3.DORA' regulation='DORA' subdomain_id='D-10.3' applies_to='[DORA]' inherits_from='SO-DORA-019 + SO-DORA-020 + SO-DORA-021' source_SR='SR-DORA-008 + SR-DORA-009 + SR-DORA-010' activation='if DORA in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='4_of_5' verified_relationship=None objective='Financial entities **establish, maintain and review a sound and comprehensive digital operational resilience testing programme as an integral part of the ICT risk-management framework** (Art. 24(1) DORA), using a 12-way portfolio of testing methodologies (Art. 25(1) DORA); **significant financial entities carry out advanced testing of their ICT systems using threat-led penetration testing (TLPT) on a regular basis** (Art. 26(1) DORA per the Regulatory Technical Standards under Art. 26(8)).

**CSF anchors (from `SR-DORA-008` + `SR-DORA-009` + `SR-DORA-010` v0.3 security_rationale):**
PR.IP-07 (primary), ID.RA-05, DE.AE-02, GV.OV-03, PR.PS-04.
*(PR.IP-07 — Configuration change control processes are in place — anchors the DORA Art. 24(1) `sound and comprehensive digital operational resilience testing programme as an integral part of the ICT risk-management framework` mapped to NIST CSF 2.0 PR.IP-07; ID.RA-05 — Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to establish risk tolerances — anchors the Art. 25(1) 12-way modalities risk-input dimension; DE.AE-02 — Adverse events are analyzed to identify or determine the scope of an incident — anchors the Art. 25(1) testing modalities input to the incident-handling chain; GV.OV-03 — Cybersecurity risk management strategy outcomes are reviewed and inform changes — anchors the Art. 24(1) `establish, maintain and review` testing programme lifecycle feedback loop; PR.PS-04 — Software installation, operation, and updates are performed consistent with the security policy — anchors the Art. 25(1) testing modalities operational dimension + Art. 26(1) TLPT operational dimension. The five subcategories together enable the financial entity to demonstrate ex post, against the NCA + EBA Guidelines supervisory baseline, that the Art. 24(1) `sound and comprehensive` testing programme + Art. 25(1) 12-way modalities portfolio + Art. 26(1) TLPT for significant entities were operational on the financial-entity ICT systems with `on a regular basis` TLPT cadence + appropriate proportionality calibration per Art. 4.)*' considerations=[] anchors=['Art. 24(1)', 'Art. 25(1)', 'Art. 26(1)', 'Art. 26(8)', 'Art. 4'] csf=['DE.AE-02', 'GV.OV-03', 'ID.RA-05', 'PR.IP-07', 'PR.PS-04']

id='SO-D-10.3.AI_Act' yaml_id='SO-D-10.3.AI_Act' regulation='AI_Act' subdomain_id='D-10.3' applies_to='[AI_Act]' inherits_from='SO-AI_Act-007 + SO-AI_Act-008' source_SR='SR-AI_Act-003 + SR-AI_Act-014' activation='if AI_Act in applicable_regs' phase_1A_role='5_of_5' verified_relationship=None objective="Providers of high-risk AI systems ensure the systems are **tested for the purpose of identifying the most appropriate and targeted risk management measures**, and **testing shall ensure that high-risk AI systems perform consistently for their intended purpose** (Art. 9(6) AI Act); testing procedures may include **testing in real-world conditions in accordance with Article 60** (Art. 9(7) AI Act); high-risk AI systems are **designed and developed to achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity, and to perform consistently in those respects throughout their lifecycle** (Art. 15(1) AI Act).

**CSF anchors (from `SR-AI_Act-003` + `SR-AI_Act-014` v0.3 security_rationale):**
PR.IP-07 (primary), ID.RA-05, PR.PS-04, GV.OV-03.
*(PR.IP-07 — Configuration change control processes are in place — anchors the AI Act Art. 9(6) `tested for the purpose of identifying the most appropriate and targeted risk management measures` mapped to NIST CSF 2.0 PR.IP-07; ID.RA-05 — Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to establish risk tolerances — anchors the Art. 9(6) testing-for-risk-management risk-input dimension + Art. 9(7) real-world-conditions testing risk-input dimension; PR.PS-04 — Software installation, operation, and updates are performed consistent with the security policy — anchors the Art. 15(1) `throughout their lifecycle` lifecycle-testing dimension + the AI-system operational dimension; GV.OV-03 — Cybersecurity risk management strategy outcomes are reviewed and inform changes — anchors the Art. 9(6) testing-for-risk-management feedback loop into the AI-Act provider's risk-management-system documentation (Art. 9 — cross to D-09.1). The four subcategories together enable the AI Act provider to demonstrate ex post, against the MSA + AI Office supervisory baseline, that the Art. 9(6) testing-for-risk-management + Art. 9(7) real-world-conditions testing per Art. 60 + Art. 15(1) accuracy/robustness/cybersecurity baseline testing `throughout their lifecycle` were operational on the AI-system layer with appropriate risk-management calibration.)*" considerations=[] anchors=['Art. 15(1)', 'Art. 60', 'Art. 9', 'Art. 9(6)', 'Art. 9(7)', 'Article 60'] csf=['GV.OV-03', 'ID.RA-05', 'PR.IP-07', 'PR.PS-04']
